roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Pick 1 overall: Incineroar is the most splashable VGC glue (Intimidate+Fake Out+Parting Shot+Knock, resists Ghost for Mega Gengar meta) with no cheap replacement, fits any archetype and leaves mega slot open.

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: W2 rain: Overqwil Dark SE Indeedee/Basculegion Poison SE Gardevoir SwiftSwim+Intim+Taunt vs Pelipper/TW; Excadrill Ground SE Arch Steel SE Gardevoir Rock vs Pelipper, resists Draco/Fairy where Garchomp weak. Saves 13pts (100->87) bank for later, uses 2/6 allowance.

roster.name: Mega Clefable
roster.rationale: Cheap Follow Me redirector (blocks base Clefable) + mega wincon in one 10-pt slot; Fairy covers Garchomp Dragon weakness, Magic Bounce bounces Taunt/Encore.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult 142 is fastest remaining attacker, Clear Body ignores Intimidate cycling, Ghost/Dragon hits Gengar/Farigiraf/Hatterene/Salamence/Archaludon cores; U-turn/Will-O/Thunderwave support.

roster.name: Noivern
roster.rationale: Last cheap fast Tailwind (123 outruns Whimsicott 116, Frisk scouts, Infiltrator vs Grimmsnarl screens); Dragon/Flying stacks with Pult for Dragon pressure.

roster.name: Rotom-Mow
roster.rationale: Rotom-Mow Electric/Grass Levitate walls rain (Pelipper/Bascu/Palafin/Swampert) and Grounds (Excadrill/Mamoswine/mirror Chomp), Leaf Storm+TBolt+Wisp+Trick.

roster.name: Skarmory
roster.rationale: Equal 3-3 keeps both at 100. Skarmory gives 2nd Tailwind (only Noivern has TW), Sturdy, Hurricane 0.5x + Fairy 0.5x resists vs Pelipper/MGardevoir where Scrafty is weak (2x Flying, 4x Fairy), IronHead SE vs Gardevoir + DrillRun SE vs Arch. Preserves Mega + core 5 for W2, adds Steel/Espeed resist for future. Scrafty benched-for-benched, past-bench Skarmory for them.

roster.name: Overqwil
roster.rationale: W2 rain: Overqwil Dark SE Indeedee/Basculegion Poison SE Gardevoir SwiftSwim+Intim+Taunt vs Pelipper/TW; Excadrill Ground SE Arch Steel SE Gardevoir Rock vs Pelipper, resists Draco/Fairy where Garchomp weak. Saves 13pts (100->87) bank for later, uses 2/6 allowance.

roster.name: Pincurchin
roster.rationale: Electric Surge powers Rotom Rising Voltage, TWave+Memento+Recover support, blocks sleep vs Venusaur.

roster.name: Mawile
roster.rationale: 3rd Intimidate + Sucker Punch/Taunt, denies Mega Mawile Huge Power threat.

roster.name: Mega Salamence
roster.rationale: Best mega on the board for doubles: Intimidate on entry, then Aerilate Hyper Voice (135 effective STAB spread, bypasses Substitute) or Double-Edge; 95/130/90 bulk and 120 Spe let it Mega Evolve turn 1 safely. Flexes into any core; locks the premier mega before the other 7 coaches.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Whimsicott is gone; Farigiraf is the priority-control answer: Armor Tail negates Fake Out (grok), Sucker Punch (fable) and Prankster (astra) targeting my side, it's a bulky 120 HP Trick Room plan-B, and gets Helping Hand/Psychic Noise/own Psychic Terrain.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: 9 points for a 136 SpA Psychic/Fairy that doubles as my second Trick Room setter and Magic Bounce wall — reflects astra's Prankster Encore/Taunt and status aimed at it, punishes Mimikyu-style tech. Farigiraf gives Psychic Terrain so Expanding Force hits as a boosted spread. Cheapest high-impact mon left; 12 picks before my next turn would take it.

roster.name: Corviknight
roster.rationale: Field is physical-heavy (Annihilape, Sneasler, Metagross, Basculegion rain): Corviknight resists all of those (Rage Fist/Grassy Glide/Close Combat at 0.25x), sets my only reliable Tailwind, U-turns to protect Palafin's Hero transform, and Body Press punishes fable's Kingambit. Fills speed control + bulk + pivot in one slot.

roster.name: Palafin
roster.rationale: Dragapult is gone; Palafin is the best remaining carry: Hero forme 160 Atk with priority Jet Punch, Flip Turn (self-transform + pivot), Close Combat, Ice Punch, Haze anti-setup. Speed 100 pairs perfectly under Corviknight's Tailwind and costs only 12.

roster.name: Garganacl
roster.rationale: Cheapest unique wall left: 0.25x into gemini's Heat Wave/Sludge Bomb, 4x Rock STAB back at Zard Y, Purifying Salt blocks Sleep Powder/Thunder Wave. Also a long-game Salt Cure win condition vs bulky waters. Five points; take before grok's pick 46.

roster.name: Toxtricity
roster.rationale: 6 points for a Punk Rock special spread attacker: Overdrive hits luna's rain engine (Basculegion/Pelipper 2x) and shrugs off the field's Intimidate cores; Boomburst/Overdrive spread is my non-TR special damage alongside Hatterene. Snarl/Volt Switch add utility. Electric answers are nearly gone off the board.

roster.name: Azumarill
roster.rationale: My TR engine had no physical attacker and three opponents run boosted Hyper Voice spread (Gardevoir-M, Primarina, Altaria-M): Azumarill resists all of that at 0.25x while bringing Huge Power Liquidation/Play Rough under Trick Room, Belly Drum threat, Aqua Jet outside TR, Knock Off and Icy Wind. Cheapest piece that fills two holes.

roster.name: Clawitzer
roster.rationale: 4 points for the field's best tech piece: Mega Launcher Aura Sphere is 4x into fable's Kingambit and grok's... fable's Mega Steelix, Dark Pulse 2x into luna's Gardevoir-M, muse's Dragapult/Noivern, grok's Greninja and fable's Salamence; Water Pulse spread + Icy Wind speed control + Heal Pulse support; 59 Spe works under Trick Room. Fills the Dark/Fighting coverage gap my roster lacks entirely.

roster.name: Dragalge
roster.rationale: 3 points for a TR-able Adaptability special wall: base Dragalge keeps Adaptability, so Sludge Wave is boosted STAB hitting 2x into every Fairy on the board (luna's Gardevoir-M, fable's Clefable-M... fable has Altaria-M, deepseek's Primarina), plus Draco Meteor, Toxic, Thunder Wave and 123 SpD. Slow (44 Spe) — ideal Trick Room piece; completes the roster at exactly 100.

roster.name: Rillaboom
roster.rationale: Only Grassy Surge on the board, plus Fake Out, Knock Off, U-turn, and Grassy Glide. Incineroar is already gone, so this is the best remaining enabler and it still functions as a win condition. Nothing else at 19 is this hard to replace later.

roster.name: Sneasler
roster.rationale: Best remaining Rillaboom pair: Grassy Seed Unburden is on-switch, Dire Claw/CC/Fake Out at 130/120. Armor Tail is cloneable later with Tsareena (11) or Indeedee-M Psychic Terrain (12); this Unburden attacker is not. Leaves the mega slot open for pick 19.

roster.name: Clefable
roster.rationale: Last Follow Me with real bulk now that Indeedee-F is gone (Mega Clefable is a different entry). Unaware + Moonblast is the clean answer to Mega Salamence+Farigiraf when Armor Tail turns off Fake Out/Glide; Magic Guard and TWave fill holes the physical core does not. 15 keeps us on pace; Maushold is redundant if we lock this.

roster.name: Grimmsnarl
roster.rationale: Last elite Prankster: screens protect Sneasler, Parting Shot/Spirit Break/Fake Out, Dark/Fairy into Gengar and Salamence. glm has no Fake Out and 53 points, so this is gone at 31 if we pass. Klefki is the 11-cost backup; Clefable already Follow Me’s the core. Leaves 31 for 6 — pick 35 should be a 13–15 mega/Ghost/Fire resist, not another 16.

roster.name: Mega Dragonite
roster.rationale: Locks Tailwind, a special mega (145 SpA Ice Beam/Heat Wave/Hurricane), Dragon Fire resist into Charizard Y, and 4x Ice into Salamence/Garchomp. Multiscale is the bulk the frail core lacks. 15 leaves 16 for 5 — next is cheap Ghost/Fire (Skeledirge 5) not another 14+.

roster.name: Skeledirge
roster.rationale: Mandatory Ghost for Shadow Tag plus Fire resist into Charizard Y/Gholdengo at 5. Unaware Torch Song/Slack Off is a second tank next to Clefable without using the mega slot. 11 left for 4: pick 51 is Greninja 7 / Gengar 8 / Cinderace 8 / Pincurchin 4, then 1-cost fillers. Mega Chandelure 9 would starve the rest of the roster.

roster.name: Paldean Tauros
roster.rationale: 9-mon Combat plan is illegal (exactly 10, 1-for-1). Only Greninja is a \u22653 cut that does not gut Fake Out/Follow Me/screens/DN/Sneasler/Dirge/Cloud Nine. Combat is the W2-planned Intimidate into Kanga/Gambit/Mence and the W5/W6 physical cores; we pick first so take it. Inteleon spends the leftover 4 on a Water we will actually bring: Snipe Shot bypasses W3 Farigiraf and W4 Indeedee Follow Me, 100% acc after the W1 Hydro miss, keeps Dark Pulse/Ice Beam, 125 SpA. Keep Rotom for W2 Tag and Altaria for W4/W7. Houndoom was never-bring. No Arbok/1-cost junk.

roster.name: Rotom
roster.rationale: Best 2-cost that actually makes a 6: Electric/Ghost Levitate with Electroweb, Volt Switch, Thunderbolt, Will-O-Wisp, TWave. Covers rain and Charizard’s Flying, second Ghost for Shadow Tag. Rage Powder is redundant with Clefable Follow Me; Intimidate Mawile is worse as a Pokémon. 2 left for Altaria 1 + a Flash Fire/hazard 1.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Cloud Nine turns off Charizard Y sun and Pelipper rain without spending the mega slot; Tailwind is a backup if Dragonite is the attacker not the setter. 1 pt left for Houndoom Flash Fire at 78.

roster.name: Inteleon
roster.rationale: 9-mon Combat plan is illegal (exactly 10, 1-for-1). Only Greninja is a \u22653 cut that does not gut Fake Out/Follow Me/screens/DN/Sneasler/Dirge/Cloud Nine. Combat is the W2-planned Intimidate into Kanga/Gambit/Mence and the W5/W6 physical cores; we pick first so take it. Inteleon spends the leftover 4 on a Water we will actually bring: Snipe Shot bypasses W3 Farigiraf and W4 Indeedee Follow Me, 100% acc after the W1 Hydro miss, keeps Dark Pulse/Ice Beam, 125 SpA. Keep Rotom for W2 Tag and Altaria for W4/W7. Houndoom was never-bring. No Arbok/1-cost junk.

roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Mega Gengar is the only Shadow Tag user on the board: 170 SpA/130 Spe, trapping lets Fake Out + double-target guarantee KOs and enables Perish Song/Disable lines. Unique game-warping tool at 18.

roster.name: Kingambit
roster.rationale: Kingambit: Fairy resist Steel with Supreme Overlord, Sucker Punch priority, Kowtow Cleave; punishes Intimidate (Incineroar/Salamence already drafted) via Defiant. Strong late-game closer complementing Gengar's trapping.

roster.name: Mega Kangaskhan
roster.rationale: Mega Kangaskhan: Fake Out support that doubles as a Parental Bond nuke (Double-Edge/Drain Punch/Power-Up Punch), pairs with Gengar trapping; 105/100/100 bulk at 15 points is excellent value.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash: Water/Electric coverage for Charizard Y, Talonflame, Incineroar, Metagross, Basculegion; Levitate + Will-O-Wisp/Volt Switch utility; pivot that Gengar/Kingambit lack. Good bulk at 14.

roster.name: Salamence
roster.rationale: Base Salamence is still legal: Intimidate + Tailwind speed control the roster lacked, 100 Spe with Draco Meteor/Hyper Voice/Dual Wingbeat; Ground immunity covers Rotom/Kingambit weaknesses.

roster.name: Mega Altaria
roster.rationale: Mega Altaria: only Fairy on the roster, Dragon/Fairy typing answers the many Dragons drafted (Salamence, Dragonite, Dragapult, Garchomp), Pixilate Hyper Voice spread plus backup Tailwind; flexible third mega option at 7.

roster.name: Mega Steelix
roster.rationale: Mega Steelix: 230 Def Ground/Steel wall immune to Electric, resists Fairy/Rock/Dragon; gives Ground coverage (High Horsepower/Stomping Tantrum, Heavy Slam) and a Trick-Room-proof anchor for 6 points.

roster.name: Greninja
roster.rationale: Toxicroak and Mega Ampharos were the two roster pieces with no clear bring case (never registered in week 1; Ampharos is a 6th mega on a team that only megas Gengar). Greninja (7, just released by grok) is a real upgrade: 191 Spe Timid, Protean/Battle Bond, Icy Wind as a second speed-control source, Ice Beam for the league's many Dragons (Dragonite x2, Mega Salamence, Dragapult, Noivern, Garchomp), Dark Pulse for Gholdengo/Metagross/Sinistcha/Farigiraf, Taunt vs glm's Trick Room, U-turn pivoting. Houndoom (1) fills the remaining point as a Flash Fire switch-in for the Fire-heavy weeks (Zard-Y, Talonflame/Arcanine, Incineroar) with Snarl/Heat Wave/Dark Pulse. Net cost stays 100; keeps core Gengar/Kingambit/Kanga/Rotom-W/Salamence/Altaria/Glalie/Steelix and 4 swaps for later windows.

roster.name: Mega Glalie
roster.rationale: Mega Glalie: Refrigerate Ice coverage (Double-Edge/Explosion/Return) against the many Dragons and Flying types in the league (Salamence, Dragonite x2, Dragapult, Noivern, Garchomp, Gliscor), 100 Spe, Ice Shard priority option; cheap flexible mega.

roster.name: Houndoom
roster.rationale: Toxicroak and Mega Ampharos were the two roster pieces with no clear bring case (never registered in week 1; Ampharos is a 6th mega on a team that only megas Gengar). Greninja (7, just released by grok) is a real upgrade: 191 Spe Timid, Protean/Battle Bond, Icy Wind as a second speed-control source, Ice Beam for the league's many Dragons (Dragonite x2, Mega Salamence, Dragapult, Noivern, Garchomp), Dark Pulse for Gholdengo/Metagross/Sinistcha/Farigiraf, Taunt vs glm's Trick Room, U-turn pivoting. Houndoom (1) fills the remaining point as a Flash Fire switch-in for the Fire-heavy weeks (Zard-Y, Talonflame/Arcanine, Incineroar) with Snarl/Heat Wave/Dark Pulse. Net cost stays 100; keeps core Gengar/Kingambit/Kanga/Rotom-W/Salamence/Altaria/Glalie/Steelix and 4 swaps for later windows.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Secures scarce Prankster Tailwind plus verified Encore, Taunt, Helping Hand, and Trick Room. Flexible speed and disruption support lets us exploit discounted attackers rather than commit our first pick to one Mega or weather mode.

roster.name: Annihilape
roster.rationale: Creates a verified Beat Up–Rage Fist win condition with Whimsicott while adding Defiant pressure against the drafted Intimidators. Ghost typing also provides a valuable alternative attacker into Mega Gengar's trapping plans, and Fighting STAB threatens the emerging Steel cores.

roster.name: Maushold
roster.rationale: The dex confirms Maushold is the last available Follow Me user. Friend Guard, redirection, and a second Beat Up source turn Annihilape into a much more reliable win condition, while Encore, Super Fang, and optional Population Bomb give Maushold value beyond that pairing.

roster.name: Mega Excadrill
roster.rationale: Excellent nine-point offensive Mega: Steel/Ground coverage pressures the emerging Fairy, Poison, and Steel cores while providing key resistances for MausApe. Verified High Horsepower, Iron Head, Rock Slide, and Swords Dance support immediate Tailwind offense or a redirected setup win condition.

roster.name: Rotom-Heat
roster.rationale: Adds urgently needed special offense and Fire/Flying/Fairy/Steel resistances. Levitate complements Excadrill, while verified Overheat, Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Electroweb, and Nasty Plot provide flexible pressure against the sun, Steel, and Flying cores already drafted.

roster.name: Empoleon
roster.rationale: Adds Water special offense and valuable Flying, Psychic, Fairy, and Ice resistances for only seven points. Competitive discourages opposing Intimidate, while verified Ice Beam, Grass Knot, Flash Cannon, Hydro Pump, Weather Ball, and Roost allow tailored sets into the developing rosters.

roster.name: Weavile
roster.rationale: With Scrafty gone, Weavile supplies verified fast Fake Out, Knock Off, and Ice STAB in one offensive slot. Its base 125 Speed and Triple Axel/Ice Spinner options add immediate pressure against the numerous Dragons and a Psychic-immune attacker for terrain teams.

roster.name: Hydrapple
roster.rationale: Adds a durable special attacker with excellent Water/Electric resistance and a Ground resistance, strengthening the rain matchup and covering our Steel/Fire core. Verified Regenerator, recovery, Grass/Dragon STAB, Earth Power, and Nasty Plot support both pivoting and redirected setup.

roster.name: Chandelure
roster.rationale: Secures a powerful independent special attacker and verified Trick Room–Imprison control. Flash Fire and Heat Wave offer additional lines against sun and Steel cores, while Ghost typing complements our positioning against trapping and Fake Out.

roster.name: Tauros
roster.rationale: Completes the roster at exactly 100 points with our first Intimidate user, another Ghost immunity, and base-110 Speed. Verified Raging Bull removes screens, while Close Combat, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Helping Hand give it useful matchup-specific roles.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Best available mega for doubles and my anchor. Mega Metagross (Tough Claws, 80/145/150/105/110/110) is bulky, fast, and has elite doubles tools: Bullet Punch priority, Iron Head, Ice/Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt, Rock Slide/Earthquake, and Body Press off 150 Def (all contact, so Tough Claws-boosted). Steel/Psychic resists a huge range of types and only fears Fire/Ground/Ghost/Dark, giving a consistent physical win condition no other roster can replicate. Securing the mega slot now, since top megas (Salamence, Gengar) are already gone.

roster.name: Hydreigon
roster.rationale: One swap. Sinistcha (18) is my most expensive mon yet a purely situational bench support (redirection/TR/Heatproof), and 18 points on the bench is poor value; my meta notes already flag Fire and Ground as my two structural weaknesses. Hydreigon (14), now undrafted, patches BOTH: Dark/Dragon resists Fire 0.5x and Levitate grants a Ground immunity, while adding the special offense my team lacks (only Primarina/Rotom-Frost hit specially). Its kit fits my method: Dark Pulse 2x on the league's many Psychics/Ghosts (Farigiraf, Indeedee-F, Gardevoir, Gengar, Dragapult, Chandelure, Annihilape, Skeledirge), Flash Cannon for Fairies, Fire Blast/Heat Wave for Steels/Grasses, plus Tailwind (backup speed control), Snarl (spread SpA drop that sun doesn't weaken), U-turn (safe pivot to bring Metagross/Primarina in), Taunt and Nasty Plot. Cost drops 100 -> 96, roster stays 10 mons, one per base species. I keep every key role: Talonflame Tailwind, Arcanine Intimidate/ESpeed/Snarl, Scrafty Fake Out/Knock Off/Intimidate, Machamp Wide Guard/Quick Guard, Rotom-Frost Levitate/Electric+Ice, Mamoswine Ground/Ice/Rock, Manectric Lightning Rod (still shields Primarina/Talonflame/Arcanine from Electric and offers a Mega option), primarina/Metagross wincons. Its Fairy/Ice frailty is a managed risk covered by four Fairy-resistant bodies and my Fake Out/Wide Guard; losing Rage Powder is acceptable since I already have Fake Out, Wide Guard, Quick Guard and Intimidate for protection. I rejected Garchomp (18, 4x Ice, physical, overlaps Mamoswine) and Aegislash (16, adds a second Fire/Ground-weak Steel, worsening my documented weakness). Holding the spare 4 points and 5 swaps for later windows.

roster.name: Primarina
roster.rationale: Fills my biggest gaps: a special attacker and defensive glue. Primarina (Water/Fairy, 126 SpA/116 SpD) resists Fire, Water, Ice, Dark, Fighting, and Bug and is immune to Dragon, patching exactly what Metagross and Sinistcha fear, while answering Incineroar, Mega Salamence, Garchomp, Kingambit and Charizard Y offensively. It gives spread damage (Liquid Voice/Dazzling Gleam) plus Encore/Icy Wind/Life Dew utility. With Indeedee-F and Farigiraf gone, good special spreaders are drying up fast.

roster.name: Talonflame
roster.rationale: I need reliable speed control, and Gale Wings Talonflame is the best on the board: priority Tailwind at full HP, plus Taunt (stops opposing Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Trick Room), Quick Guard and Upper Hand to blunt Fake Out, and Will-O-Wisp/U-turn utility. It also pairs directly with Metagross, who outspeeds key threats under Tailwind and carries Rock Slide for the opposing Mega Charizard Y. Priority Tailwind is a scarce effect (only Noivern/Aerodactyl otherwise), so I take it while available; Intimidate has cheaper fallbacks later.

roster.name: Arcanine
roster.rationale: With Incineroar gone, Arcanine is the best Intimidate glue left and the one support role my team completely lacks. It brings Snarl to blunt opposing Charizard Y / Gholdengo / Archaludon, Will-O-Wisp to cripple Garchomp/Kingambit/Annihilape, Extreme Speed priority, Morning Sun, Heat Wave and Close Combat. Fire typing also helps vs Rillaboom/Venusaur/Scizor, and it is cheap enough (11) to leave room for fillers.

roster.name: Mamoswine
roster.rationale: Best 6th piece I can afford and a direct meta answer. Mamoswine (130 Atk, Thick Fat) gives my team's only Ice Shard priority to revenge-kill the many Dragons in the league (Mega Salamence, Dragonite, Dragapult, Garchomp, Noivern, Baxcalibur), Ground STAB for Gholdengo/Archaludon/Kingambit/Excadrill, Rock Slide for opposing Mega Charizard Y, Knock Off item removal, and Thick Fat to sit on sun Fire damage. It fills the holes Arcanine/Talonflame/Primarina leave.

roster.name: Machamp
roster.rationale: Machamp is outstanding value at 4: it brings Wide Guard (the anti-spread tool my team lacks vs opposing Heat Wave/Make It Rain/Earthquake/Rock Slide/Overheat), no-recoil Fighting coverage for Kingambit/Archaludon/Tyranitar/Umbreon, No Guard Dynamic Punch confusion, Bullet Punch priority and Knock Off item removal, plus Quick Guard. That covers multiple gaps in one cheap slot.

roster.name: Rotom-Frost
roster.rationale: Fills my last real gap: a special attacker with Electric coverage and a Ground immunity. Rotom-Frost (Levitate) gives Thunderbolt/Volt Switch to hit Pelipper (4x), Basculegion, Corviknight, Empoleon, Gyarados and Azumarill, Blizzard for Dragonite/Gliscor/Salamence/Garchomp/Noivern, plus Will-O-Wisp and Nasty Plot. Levitate also makes it a safe partner next to Metagross/Mamoswine Earthquake and a pivot into opposing Ground moves, balancing my previously all-physical attacker core.

roster.name: Scrafty
roster.rationale: Cost-neutral 1-for-1 (Skarmory 3 <-> Scrafty 3), keeps 10 mons and 100/100. Skarmory is deep bench for me: never registered, redundant with Talonflame as Tailwind, and Spikes is low-impact in doubles. Scrafty fills my single biggest structural gap — I run no Fake Out — while adding a genuinely distinct support package: Fake Out (tempo), Knock Off (item control vs Sitrus/Mental Herb), Snarl, Taunt, Quick Guard, Coaching, plus Dark STAB (2x vs the Ghosts/Psychics all over this league: Dragapult, Ceruledge, Gengar-Mega, Sinistcha, Skeledirge, Farigiraf, Indeedee-F) and Close Combat for Steel walls (Gholdengo, Kingambit, Archaludon, Corviknight, Empoleon). Ice Punch is an extra 4x Dragonite tool if needed. Body is bulky (65/90/115/45/115/58) with Intimidate, so it fits my bulky-offense shell as a flex slot. Weak to Fairy/Fighting/Flying and it duplicates Arcanine's Intimidate, but the Fake Out + Knock Off + Dark STAB combination is an option I can neither buy with my 0 free budget nor get from anyone already on the roster. Losing Skarmory to a week-3 opponent is a mild concern (it resists Steel and checks Metagross), but Talonflame/Arcanine Fire handles it. Net upgrade in flexibility for a mon I never used.

roster.name: Manectric
roster.rationale: Best 1-cost value for my final slot. Manectric's Lightning Rod redirects and absorbs single-target Electric moves, shielding my Electric-weak Talonflame, Primarina and Skarmory (and punishing Raichu/Rotom-Heat Discharge users) while giving Manectric a SpA boost; at 105 Speed it also supplies fast Snarl SpA-drops against sun/special teams, Volt Switch pivoting, and Flamethrower/Overheat/Thunderbolt coverage. It rounds out the roster with a real doubles utility niche for one point.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Archaludon is the strongest remaining flexible centerpiece: exceptional Steel/Dragon defensive profile, high special damage, and Stamina lets it scale in doubles while fitting rain, sun, or neutral modes.

roster.name: Indeedee-F
roster.rationale: Indeedee-F gives Archaludon a premier doubles partner: Follow Me redirection, Psychic Terrain priority control, Helping Hand, and Trick Room access, creating both fast and slow mode flexibility.

roster.name: Pelipper
roster.rationale: Pelipper adds a decisive rain mode beside Archaludon, pressures the already-drafted sun core, and supplies Tailwind plus wide Water damage without competing with Indeedee-F’s terrain role.

roster.name: Basculegion-Male
roster.rationale: Basculegion-Male is the premier rain payoff for Pelipper: Swift Swim speed, Adaptability-boosted spread Water damage, and Ghost typing give the roster a threatening mode into the league’s current Psychic/Steel-heavy builds.

roster.name: Mega Gardevoir
roster.rationale: Mega Gardevoir supplies urgent Fairy pressure into the many Dragons, powerful spread damage, and a second Psychic-mode attacker that benefits from Indeedee-F’s terrain and redirection.

roster.name: Qwilfish
roster.rationale: Qwilfish is an efficient rain utility slot: Swift Swim gives a second fast mode, Intimidate offers needed physical mitigation, and Poison STAB helps against Fairy threats.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: Gliscor patches the roster’s Electric weakness with Ground immunity to its own side, adds a durable physical attacker and status-oriented endgame, and gives valuable Poison Heal flexibility in a low-cost slot.

roster.name: Sceptile
roster.rationale: Sceptile gives the roster fast Grass pressure into opposing Water and Ground cores, a strong Electric matchup through offensive tempo, and an independent high-Speed option outside rain.

roster.name: Meowstic-Female
roster.rationale: Meowstic-F is an efficient final support slot with fast disruption, screens and Helping Hand options, giving the roster utility beyond Indeedee-F while preserving a legal two-point cost.

roster.name: Morpeko
roster.rationale: Morpeko is the best final two-point patch: fast Electric pressure against opposing Water/Flying cores, Dark utility into Psychic and Ghost threats, and disruptive momentum tools.

roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is the premier Drought Mega with 159 SpA, establishing immediate offensive pressure and weather control. Securing it at pick 8 leads off our consecutive picks at the turn.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo provides Good as Gold status immunity, immense spread damage with Make It Rain, and exceptional defensive typing synergy with Mega Charizard Y (immune to Ground/Fighting/Poison, resisting Rock). Locking both in at the turn secures an elite offensive and defensive core.

roster.name: Venusaur
roster.rationale: Venusaur forms the premier Sun duo with Mega Charizard Y, gaining doubled Speed via Chlorophyll to deliver high-speed Sleep Powder, Earth Power, and Grass/Poison coverage against Water, Ground, and Rock threats.

roster.name: Swampert
roster.rationale: Swampert provides essential Electric immunity and Rock/Fire resistances to protect Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo, adds Wide Guard to shield our spread attackers, and at 6 points represents massive value while denying Swampert/Mega Swampert to opposing rain teams.

roster.name: Raichu
roster.rationale: Raichu provides vital Lightning Rod protection for Mega Charizard Y, Fake Out pressure to secure turns for Charizard Y and Venusaur, Feint to bypass Protect/Wide Guard, and Nuzzle for reliable speed control outside of Sun.

roster.name: Paldean Tauros Aqua
roster.rationale: Paldean Tauros Aqua gives our team unblockable Intimidate in this format (no Clear Amulet), crucial STAB Fighting Close Combat to crush Kingambit and Incineroar, Aqua Jet priority, and key defensive resistances to Rock, Fire, and Dark to protect Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo.

roster.name: Dragonite
roster.rationale: Dragonite brings Multiscale bulk, +2 Extreme Speed priority cleanup, Tailwind speed control outside of Sun, and Haze to shut down setup sweepers, complementing our offensive spread pressure.

roster.name: Umbreon
roster.rationale: Umbreon provides a premier defensive Dark anchor that resists Ghost and Dark for Gholdengo, gains 66.7% healing from Moonlight under Mega Charizard Y's Sun, ignores Fake Out flinches with Inner Focus, and punishes high-attack physical threats with Foul Play while debuffing special attackers with Snarl.

roster.name: Alcremie
roster.rationale: Alcremie provides essential Fairy typing, Aroma Veil to grant full Taunt and Encore immunity to both itself and its partner, and the potent Decorate move (+2 Atk and +2 SpA) to supercharge sweepers like Dragonite, Mega Charizard Y, and Gholdengo.

roster.name: Passimian
roster.rationale: Passimian completes our 10-Pokémon roster by adding Defiant to directly punish opposing Intimidate and Snarl spam, Quick Guard to protect our core from opposing priority attacks, and high-impact Knock Off and Close Combat utility at exactly 3 points.

picks.rationale: Pick 1 overall: Incineroar is the most splashable VGC glue (Intimidate+Fake Out+Parting Shot+Knock, resists Ghost for Mega Gengar meta) with no cheap replacement, fits any archetype and leaves mega slot open.

Best mega on the board for doubles: Intimidate on entry, then Aerilate Hyper Voice (135 effective STAB spread, bypasses Substitute) or Double-Edge; 95/130/90 bulk and 120 Spe let it Mega Evolve turn 1 safely. Flexes into any core; locks the premier mega before the other 7 coaches.

Only Grassy Surge on the board, plus Fake Out, Knock Off, U-turn, and Grassy Glide. Incineroar is already gone, so this is the best remaining enabler and it still functions as a win condition. Nothing else at 19 is this hard to replace later.
Mega Gengar is the only Shadow Tag user on the board: 170 SpA/130 Spe, trapping lets Fake Out + double-target guarantee KOs and enables Perish Song/Disable lines. Unique game-warping tool at 18.

Secures scarce Prankster Tailwind plus verified Encore, Taunt, Helping Hand, and Trick Room. Flexible speed and disruption support lets us exploit discounted attackers rather than commit our first pick to one Mega or weather mode.

Best available mega for doubles and my anchor. Mega Metagross (Tough Claws, 80/145/150/105/110/110) is bulky, fast, and has elite doubles tools: Bullet Punch priority, Iron Head, Ice/Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt, Rock Slide/Earthquake, and Body Press off 150 Def (all contact, so Tough Claws-boosted). Steel/Psychic resists a huge range of types and only fears Fire/Ground/Ghost/Dark, giving a consistent physical win condition no other roster can replicate. Securing the mega slot now, since top megas (Salamence, Gengar) are already gone.

Archaludon is the strongest remaining flexible centerpiece: exceptional Steel/Dragon defensive profile, high special damage, and Stamina lets it scale in doubles while fitting rain, sun, or neutral modes.
Mega Charizard Y is the premier Drought Mega with 159 SpA, establishing immediate offensive pressure and weather control. Securing it at pick 8 leads off our consecutive picks at the turn.

Gholdengo provides Good as Gold status immunity, immense spread damage with Make It Rain, and exceptional defensive typing synergy with Mega Charizard Y (immune to Ground/Fighting/Poison, resisting Rock). Locking both in at the turn secures an elite offensive and defensive core.
Indeedee-F gives Archaludon a premier doubles partner: Follow Me redirection, Psychic Terrain priority control, Helping Hand, and Trick Room access, creating both fast and slow mode flexibility.

Best support remaining and an ideal partner for Mega Metagross. Sinistcha (Hospitality, Grass/Ghost) brings Rage Powder redirection to shield Metagross from single-target Fire/Ground hits, Matcha Gotcha as spread special damage that heals Metagross, Strength Sap/Life Dew sustain, Trick Room as a backup mode, and a Ground resistance plus Normal/Fighting immunity that patches Metagross's key weaknesses. It also covers Water/Ground/Rock threats. Gholdengo and Indeedee-F were just taken, so the elite support tier is thinning fast.

Creates a verified Beat Up–Rage Fist win condition with Whimsicott while adding Defiant pressure against the drafted Intimidators. Ghost typing also provides a valuable alternative attacker into Mega Gengar's trapping plans, and Fighting STAB threatens the emerging Steel cores.

Kingambit: Fairy resist Steel with Supreme Overlord, Sucker Punch priority, Kowtow Cleave; punishes Intimidate (Incineroar/Salamence already drafted) via Defiant. Strong late-game closer complementing Gengar's trapping.

Best remaining Rillaboom pair: Grassy Seed Unburden is on-switch, Dire Claw/CC/Fake Out at 130/120. Armor Tail is cloneable later with Tsareena (11) or Indeedee-M Psychic Terrain (12); this Unburden attacker is not. Leaves the mega slot open for pick 19.

Whimsicott is gone; Farigiraf is the priority-control answer: Armor Tail negates Fake Out (grok), Sucker Punch (fable) and Prankster (astra) targeting my side, it's a bulky 120 HP Trick Room plan-B, and gets Helping Hand/Psychic Noise/own Psychic Terrain.

Garchomp is last premier Ground/Dragon (EQ+Rock Slide, 130/102) answering Archaludon/Metagross/Kingambit/Gholdengo; pairs with Incin. Male Indeedee devalued (no Follow Me in this format), so pivot redirection to Clefable line.
Cheap Follow Me redirector (blocks base Clefable) + mega wincon in one 10-pt slot; Fairy covers Garchomp Dragon weakness, Magic Bounce bounces Taunt/Encore.

9 points for a 136 SpA Psychic/Fairy that doubles as my second Trick Room setter and Magic Bounce wall — reflects astra's Prankster Encore/Taunt and status aimed at it, punishes Mimikyu-style tech. Farigiraf gives Psychic Terrain so Expanding Force hits as a boosted spread. Cheapest high-impact mon left; 12 picks before my next turn would take it.

Last Follow Me with real bulk now that Indeedee-F is gone (Mega Clefable is a different entry). Unaware + Moonblast is the clean answer to Mega Salamence+Farigiraf when Armor Tail turns off Fake Out/Glide; Magic Guard and TWave fill holes the physical core does not. 15 keeps us on pace; Maushold is redundant if we lock this.
Mega Kangaskhan: Fake Out support that doubles as a Parental Bond nuke (Double-Edge/Drain Punch/Power-Up Punch), pairs with Gengar trapping; 105/100/100 bulk at 15 points is excellent value.

The dex confirms Maushold is the last available Follow Me user. Friend Guard, redirection, and a second Beat Up source turn Annihilape into a much more reliable win condition, while Encore, Super Fang, and optional Population Bomb give Maushold value beyond that pairing.

Fills my biggest gaps: a special attacker and defensive glue. Primarina (Water/Fairy, 126 SpA/116 SpD) resists Fire, Water, Ice, Dark, Fighting, and Bug and is immune to Dragon, patching exactly what Metagross and Sinistcha fear, while answering Incineroar, Mega Salamence, Garchomp, Kingambit and Charizard Y offensively. It gives spread damage (Liquid Voice/Dazzling Gleam) plus Encore/Icy Wind/Life Dew utility. With Indeedee-F and Farigiraf gone, good special spreaders are drying up fast.
Pelipper adds a decisive rain mode beside Archaludon, pressures the already-drafted sun core, and supplies Tailwind plus wide Water damage without competing with Indeedee-F’s terrain role.

Venusaur forms the premier Sun duo with Mega Charizard Y, gaining doubled Speed via Chlorophyll to deliver high-speed Sleep Powder, Earth Power, and Grass/Poison coverage against Water, Ground, and Rock threats.

Swampert provides essential Electric immunity and Rock/Fire resistances to protect Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo, adds Wide Guard to shield our spread attackers, and at 6 points represents massive value while denying Swampert/Mega Swampert to opposing rain teams.

Basculegion-Male is the premier rain payoff for Pelipper: Swift Swim speed, Adaptability-boosted spread Water damage, and Ghost typing give the roster a threatening mode into the league’s current Psychic/Steel-heavy builds.

I need reliable speed control, and Gale Wings Talonflame is the best on the board: priority Tailwind at full HP, plus Taunt (stops opposing Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Trick Room), Quick Guard and Upper Hand to blunt Fake Out, and Will-O-Wisp/U-turn utility. It also pairs directly with Metagross, who outspeeds key threats under Tailwind and carries Rock Slide for the opposing Mega Charizard Y. Priority Tailwind is a scarce effect (only Noivern/Aerodactyl otherwise), so I take it while available; Intimidate has cheaper fallbacks later.

Excellent nine-point offensive Mega: Steel/Ground coverage pressures the emerging Fairy, Poison, and Steel cores while providing key resistances for MausApe. Verified High Horsepower, Iron Head, Rock Slide, and Swords Dance support immediate Tailwind offense or a redirected setup win condition.
Rotom-Wash: Water/Electric coverage for Charizard Y, Talonflame, Incineroar, Metagross, Basculegion; Levitate + Will-O-Wisp/Volt Switch utility; pivot that Gengar/Kingambit lack. Good bulk at 14.

Last elite Prankster: screens protect Sneasler, Parting Shot/Spirit Break/Fake Out, Dark/Fairy into Gengar and Salamence. glm has no Fake Out and 53 points, so this is gone at 31 if we pass. Klefki is the 11-cost backup; Clefable already Follow Me’s the core. Leaves 31 for 6 — pick 35 should be a 13–15 mega/Ghost/Fire resist, not another 16.

Field is physical-heavy (Annihilape, Sneasler, Metagross, Basculegion rain): Corviknight resists all of those (Rage Fist/Grassy Glide/Close Combat at 0.25x), sets my only reliable Tailwind, U-turns to protect Palafin's Hero transform, and Body Press punishes fable's Kingambit. Fills speed control + bulk + pivot in one slot.
Dragapult 142 is fastest remaining attacker, Clear Body ignores Intimidate cycling, Ghost/Dragon hits Gengar/Farigiraf/Hatterene/Salamence/Archaludon cores; U-turn/Will-O/Thunderwave support.
Last cheap fast Tailwind (123 outruns Whimsicott 116, Frisk scouts, Infiltrator vs Grimmsnarl screens); Dragon/Flying stacks with Pult for Dragon pressure.

Dragapult is gone; Palafin is the best remaining carry: Hero forme 160 Atk with priority Jet Punch, Flip Turn (self-transform + pivot), Close Combat, Ice Punch, Haze anti-setup. Speed 100 pairs perfectly under Corviknight's Tailwind and costs only 12.

Locks Tailwind, a special mega (145 SpA Ice Beam/Heat Wave/Hurricane), Dragon Fire resist into Charizard Y, and 4x Ice into Salamence/Garchomp. Multiscale is the bulk the frail core lacks. 15 leaves 16 for 5 — next is cheap Ghost/Fire (Skeledirge 5) not another 14+.
Base Salamence is still legal: Intimidate + Tailwind speed control the roster lacked, 100 Spe with Draco Meteor/Hyper Voice/Dual Wingbeat; Ground immunity covers Rotom/Kingambit weaknesses.

Adds urgently needed special offense and Fire/Flying/Fairy/Steel resistances. Levitate complements Excadrill, while verified Overheat, Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Electroweb, and Nasty Plot provide flexible pressure against the sun, Steel, and Flying cores already drafted.

With Incineroar gone, Arcanine is the best Intimidate glue left and the one support role my team completely lacks. It brings Snarl to blunt opposing Charizard Y / Gholdengo / Archaludon, Will-O-Wisp to cripple Garchomp/Kingambit/Annihilape, Extreme Speed priority, Morning Sun, Heat Wave and Close Combat. Fire typing also helps vs Rillaboom/Venusaur/Scizor, and it is cheap enough (11) to leave room for fillers.
Mega Gardevoir supplies urgent Fairy pressure into the many Dragons, powerful spread damage, and a second Psychic-mode attacker that benefits from Indeedee-F’s terrain and redirection.

Raichu provides vital Lightning Rod protection for Mega Charizard Y, Fake Out pressure to secure turns for Charizard Y and Venusaur, Feint to bypass Protect/Wide Guard, and Nuzzle for reliable speed control outside of Sun.

Paldean Tauros Aqua gives our team unblockable Intimidate in this format (no Clear Amulet), crucial STAB Fighting Close Combat to crush Kingambit and Incineroar, Aqua Jet priority, and key defensive resistances to Rock, Fire, and Dark to protect Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo.
Qwilfish is an efficient rain utility slot: Swift Swim gives a second fast mode, Intimidate offers needed physical mitigation, and Poison STAB helps against Fairy threats.

Best 6th piece I can afford and a direct meta answer. Mamoswine (130 Atk, Thick Fat) gives my team's only Ice Shard priority to revenge-kill the many Dragons in the league (Mega Salamence, Dragonite, Dragapult, Garchomp, Noivern, Baxcalibur), Ground STAB for Gholdengo/Archaludon/Kingambit/Excadrill, Rock Slide for opposing Mega Charizard Y, Knock Off item removal, and Thick Fat to sit on sun Fire damage. It fills the holes Arcanine/Talonflame/Primarina leave.

Adds Water special offense and valuable Flying, Psychic, Fairy, and Ice resistances for only seven points. Competitive discourages opposing Intimidate, while verified Ice Beam, Grass Knot, Flash Cannon, Hydro Pump, Weather Ball, and Roost allow tailored sets into the developing rosters.

Mega Altaria: only Fairy on the roster, Dragon/Fairy typing answers the many Dragons drafted (Salamence, Dragonite, Dragapult, Garchomp), Pixilate Hyper Voice spread plus backup Tailwind; flexible third mega option at 7.

Mandatory Ghost for Shadow Tag plus Fire resist into Charizard Y/Gholdengo at 5. Unaware Torch Song/Slack Off is a second tank next to Clefable without using the mega slot. 11 left for 4: pick 51 is Greninja 7 / Gengar 8 / Cinderace 8 / Pincurchin 4, then 1-cost fillers. Mega Chandelure 9 would starve the rest of the roster.

Cheapest unique wall left: 0.25x into gemini's Heat Wave/Sludge Bomb, 4x Rock STAB back at Zard Y, Purifying Salt blocks Sleep Powder/Thunder Wave. Also a long-game Salt Cure win condition vs bulky waters. Five points; take before grok's pick 46.
Rotom-Mow Electric/Grass Levitate walls rain (Pelipper/Bascu/Palafin/Swampert) and Grounds (Excadrill/Mamoswine/mirror Chomp), Leaf Storm+TBolt+Wisp+Trick.
2nd Fake Out+Intimidate for 3pts, Quick Guard blocks Glide/Sucker/Aqua Jet, Coaching boosts Chomp/Incin, Fighting hits Kingambit/Excadrill.

6 points for a Punk Rock special spread attacker: Overdrive hits luna's rain engine (Basculegion/Pelipper 2x) and shrugs off the field's Intimidate cores; Boomburst/Overdrive spread is my non-TR special damage alongside Hatterene. Snarl/Volt Switch add utility. Electric answers are nearly gone off the board.

Only Water that still fits the budget: resists Fire/Water into Charizard Y and rain, Dark Pulse vs Gholdengo, Ice Beam/Grass Knot coverage, 122 Spe Protean. 8-costs (Cinderace/Gengar) leave three 1s and overlap Fire/Ghost we already have. 4 pts for 3: Ariados 2 plus two 1-costs.
Mega Steelix: 230 Def Ground/Steel wall immune to Electric, resists Fairy/Rock/Dragon; gives Ground coverage (High Horsepower/Stomping Tantrum, Heavy Slam) and a Trick-Room-proof anchor for 6 points.

With Scrafty gone, Weavile supplies verified fast Fake Out, Knock Off, and Ice STAB in one offensive slot. Its base 125 Speed and Triple Axel/Ice Spinner options add immediate pressure against the numerous Dragons and a Psychic-immune attacker for terrain teams.

Machamp is outstanding value at 4: it brings Wide Guard (the anti-spread tool my team lacks vs opposing Heat Wave/Make It Rain/Earthquake/Rock Slide/Overheat), no-recoil Fighting coverage for Kingambit/Archaludon/Tyranitar/Umbreon, No Guard Dynamic Punch confusion, Bullet Punch priority and Knock Off item removal, plus Quick Guard. That covers multiple gaps in one cheap slot.

Gliscor patches the roster’s Electric weakness with Ground immunity to its own side, adds a durable physical attacker and status-oriented endgame, and gives valuable Poison Heal flexibility in a low-cost slot.
Dragonite brings Multiscale bulk, +2 Extreme Speed priority cleanup, Tailwind speed control outside of Sun, and Haze to shut down setup sweepers, complementing our offensive spread pressure.

Umbreon provides a premier defensive Dark anchor that resists Ghost and Dark for Gholdengo, gains 66.7% healing from Moonlight under Mega Charizard Y's Sun, ignores Fake Out flinches with Inner Focus, and punishes high-attack physical threats with Foul Play while debuffing special attackers with Snarl.
Sceptile gives the roster fast Grass pressure into opposing Water and Ground cores, a strong Electric matchup through offensive tempo, and an independent high-Speed option outside rain.

Fills my last real gap: a special attacker with Electric coverage and a Ground immunity. Rotom-Frost (Levitate) gives Thunderbolt/Volt Switch to hit Pelipper (4x), Basculegion, Corviknight, Empoleon, Gyarados and Azumarill, Blizzard for Dragonite/Gliscor/Salamence/Garchomp/Noivern, plus Will-O-Wisp and Nasty Plot. Levitate also makes it a safe partner next to Metagross/Mamoswine Earthquake and a pivot into opposing Ground moves, balancing my previously all-physical attacker core.

Adds a durable special attacker with excellent Water/Electric resistance and a Ground resistance, strengthening the rain matchup and covering our Steel/Fire core. Verified Regenerator, recovery, Grass/Dragon STAB, Earth Power, and Nasty Plot support both pivoting and redirected setup.

Toxicroak: second Fake Out user with Close Combat/Sucker Punch for Kingambit/Incineroar/Tyranitar, Dry Skin punishes the Pelipper/Basculegion rain roster, Poison typing absorbs Fairy hits for 4 points.

Best 2-cost that actually makes a 6: Electric/Ghost Levitate with Electroweb, Volt Switch, Thunderbolt, Will-O-Wisp, TWave. Covers rain and Charizard’s Flying, second Ghost for Shadow Tag. Rage Powder is redundant with Clefable Follow Me; Intimidate Mawile is worse as a Pokémon. 2 left for Altaria 1 + a Flash Fire/hazard 1.

My TR engine had no physical attacker and three opponents run boosted Hyper Voice spread (Gardevoir-M, Primarina, Altaria-M): Azumarill resists all of that at 0.25x while bringing Huge Power Liquidation/Play Rough under Trick Room, Belly Drum threat, Aqua Jet outside TR, Knock Off and Icy Wind. Cheapest piece that fills two holes.
Ceruledge Fire/Ghost covers Fairy/Steel/Psychic weakness (Metagross/Kingambit/Clefable/Gardevoir/Farigiraf), Bitter Blade sustain + Sneak priority.
Electric Surge powers Rotom Rising Voltage, TWave+Memento+Recover support, blocks sleep vs Venusaur.

4 points for the field's best tech piece: Mega Launcher Aura Sphere is 4x into fable's Kingambit and grok's... fable's Mega Steelix, Dark Pulse 2x into luna's Gardevoir-M, muse's Dragapult/Noivern, grok's Greninja and fable's Salamence; Water Pulse spread + Icy Wind speed control + Heal Pulse support; 59 Spe works under Trick Room. Fills the Dark/Fighting coverage gap my roster lacks entirely.
Cloud Nine turns off Charizard Y sun and Pelipper rain without spending the mega slot; Tailwind is a backup if Dragonite is the attacker not the setter. 1 pt left for Houndoom Flash Fire at 78.

Mega Glalie: Refrigerate Ice coverage (Double-Edge/Explosion/Return) against the many Dragons and Flying types in the league (Salamence, Dragonite x2, Dragapult, Noivern, Garchomp, Gliscor), 100 Spe, Ice Shard priority option; cheap flexible mega.

Secures a powerful independent special attacker and verified Trick Room–Imprison control. Flash Fire and Heat Wave offer additional lines against sun and Steel cores, while Ghost typing complements our positioning against trapping and Fake Out.

Best utility body available for 3. Skarmory gives a Ground-immune physical wall (140 Def, Roost, Body Press off 140 Def, Iron Head) that hard-checks Garchomp/Salamence/Dragonite/Kangaskhan/Excadrill, plus Whirlwind and Spikes/Stealth Rock, and even a backup Tailwind and Taunt. It patches my lack of a defensive pivot and an anti-Ground wall for cheap.
Meowstic-F is an efficient final support slot with fast disruption, screens and Helping Hand options, giving the roster utility beyond Indeedee-F while preserving a legal two-point cost.

Alcremie provides essential Fairy typing, Aroma Veil to grant full Taunt and Encore immunity to both itself and its partner, and the potent Decorate move (+2 Atk and +2 SpA) to supercharge sweepers like Dragonite, Mega Charizard Y, and Gholdengo.

Passimian completes our 10-Pokémon roster by adding Defiant to directly punish opposing Intimidate and Snarl spam, Quick Guard to protect our core from opposing priority attacks, and high-impact Knock Off and Close Combat utility at exactly 3 points.
Morpeko is the best final two-point patch: fast Electric pressure against opposing Water/Flying cores, Dark utility into Psychic and Ghost threats, and disruptive momentum tools.

Best 1-cost value for my final slot. Manectric's Lightning Rod redirects and absorbs single-target Electric moves, shielding my Electric-weak Talonflame, Primarina and Skarmory (and punishing Raichu/Rotom-Heat Discharge users) while giving Manectric a SpA boost; at 105 Speed it also supplies fast Snarl SpA-drops against sun/special teams, Volt Switch pivoting, and Flamethrower/Overheat/Thunderbolt coverage. It rounds out the roster with a real doubles utility niche for one point.

Completes the roster at exactly 100 points with our first Intimidate user, another Ghost immunity, and base-110 Speed. Verified Raging Bull removes screens, while Close Combat, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Helping Hand give it useful matchup-specific roles.

Mega Ampharos: 165 SpA Electric/Dragon with Mold Breaker and 90/105/110 bulk for 4 points — a special wallbreaker (Thunderbolt/Dragon Pulse/Focus Blast) that fits a slower Kingambit/Steelix mode and flexes as a non-mega Static Electric.

Last point: Flash Fire is the only Heat Wave absorb on the roster for Charizard Y, plus Dark STAB into Gholdengo/Gengar. Forretress Steel is less useful than an absorb vs the sun team we actually have to beat.

3 points for a TR-able Adaptability special wall: base Dragalge keeps Adaptability, so Sludge Wave is boosted STAB hitting 2x into every Fairy on the board (luna's Gardevoir-M, fable's Clefable-M... fable has Altaria-M, deepseek's Primarina), plus Draco Meteor, Toxic, Thunder Wave and 123 SpD. Slow (44 Spe) — ideal Trick Room piece; completes the roster at exactly 100.
3rd Intimidate + Sucker Punch/Taunt, denies Mega Mawile Huge Power threat.

builds.rationale: Sun + Chlorophyll Venusaur is the threat: only Noivern Tailwind lets us outrun it, with Incineroar Fake Out to stop turn-1 Sleep Powder. Ceruledge Flash Fire walls Zard Y Heat Wave and sweeps Venusaur/Alcremie/Gholdengo with Bitter Blade + Sneak, while Garchomp Rock Slide pressures Zard/Dragonite. Mega Clefable Magic Bounce + Follow Me bounces sleep/status and covers dragons/fighters; Rotom Leaf Storm deletes Swampert/Tauros-Aqua.

Against an opponent relying heavily on triple-Intimidate pivots (Incineroar, Scrafty, Mawile) and dragon speed threats (Dragapult, Garchomp), our squad provides hard counter-play across every dimension. Defiant Passimian with Quick Guard turns enemy Intimidates into lethal offensive momentum while completely nullifying opposing Fake Out and priority, whereas Inner Focus Lum Berry Dragonite operates entirely unaffected by attack drops, flinches, or burns. Timid Choice Scarf Gholdengo naturally outspeeds and OHKOs max-speed Dragapult with Shadow Ball while shredding Mega Clefable with Make It Rain, Swampert neutralizes Garchomp's spread Earthquakes with Wide Guard while threatening an immediate 4x Ice Punch KO, and the Mega Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur Sun core exerts overwhelming high-speed special board control.

Their draft projects rain (Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion/Qwilfish + Electro Shot Archaludon) fused with Psychic-surge spam (Indeedee-F + Mega Gardevoir's Pixilate Hyper Voice). My plan: Corviknight + Dragalge wall the special cores — Corv eats Hyper Voice for 17-28% and Iron Heads Gardevoir back, Dragalce absorbs Electro Shot (19-34%) and rain Wave Crash (47-86%) while Sludge Wave sits in Gardevoir OHKO range. Hatterene and Farigiraf are both Trick Room setters, so Taunt/Fake Out/Thunder Wave (Magic Bounce + Mental Herb + Armor Tail) can't stop speed inversion, and under TR my 49-79 Speed squad always moves first against their entire roster. Clawitzer is the TR nuke: Aura Sphere 2x Archaludon/Morpeko, Dark Pulse 2x Indeedee, Ice Beam 2x Sceptile/Gliscor, Hydro Pump OHKOs Gliscor (whose Poison Heal is dead — no Toxic Orb in this format). Mega Mence is the rain answer: Rock Slide 4x Pelipper, EQ 4x Archaludon, 171 Speed beats Timid Gardevoir — just never lead it into Hyper Voice.

Pelipper establishes rain for Swift Swim Basculegion and immediate Electro Shot Archaludon, while Tailwind and Icy Wind provide flexible speed control. Indeedee-F supplies Psychic Terrain, Follow Me, and Imprison against Trick Room; Mega Gardevoir converts that terrain into strong spread pressure and threatens the Dragons and Fighters of the opposing pool. Qwilfish adds Intimidate, Haze, and Poison pressure into physical setup and Azumarill, with Wide Guard from Pelipper protecting the rain core from opposing spread attacks.

Their likely core is Mega Metagross plus Primarina, Talonflame, Arcanine, and either Mamoswine or Sinistcha. Grassy Surge plus Follow Me Clefable lets Mega Dragonite click Fire Blast/Hurricane through Ice Shard and EQ; Mental Herb keeps Follow Me live through Talonflame Taunt. Skeledirge Unaware walls Meteor Mash and Gale Wings Brave Bird, then Torch Songs the Steels and Ice. Greninja Life Orb Hydro Pump is the clean Talonflame/Arcanine/Mamoswine answer and Dark Pulses Metagross; Sneasler Sash Fake Outs and covers Primarina/Mamoswine when Rillaboom is not in. Bring Rilla+Clef+DN+Dirge vs Metagross/Mamo, swap Greninja in vs the Fires, Sneasler in vs Primarina without Rilla.

This opponent leans on Mega Dragonite plus fast Sneasler/Greninja and Prankster Grimmsnarl screens. Primarina is the anchor: it is immune to Dragon STAB, resists Fire/Hurricane, and hits Dragonite 4x with Ice Beam. Metagross breaks Clefable/Grimmsnarl with Meteor Mash and chips Dragonite with Ice Punch, while Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird and Arcanine's Intimidate + Will-O-Wisp + Extreme Speed blanket Sneasler, Rillaboom and Greninja. Mamoswine and Rotom-Frost add Ice/Ground and Ice/Electric coverage to break Multiscale and Focus Sashes, with Protect on every non-Metagross slot for Fake Out and positioning.

Opponent leans on Prankster Whimsicott speed control, Annihilape/Chandelure Ghosts and a Mega Excadrill whose contact moves pierce Protect. Mega Gengar is the primary mega: Shadow Tag traps and Sludge Bomb one-shots Whimsicott, Shadow Ball chunks Annihilape/Chandelure, Focus Blast threatens Excadrill/Weavile/Empoleon. Salamence (Sash) provides Tailwind + Intimidate and Heat Wave/Draco for Excadrill and Hydrapple; Kangaskhan gives Scrappy Fake Out (hits their Ghosts pre-mega) to buy Gengar and Tailwind turns. Rotom-Wash is the Excadrill/Rotom-Heat/Empoleon answer (Levitate, Hydro Pump, Will-O-Wisp); Kingambit with Chople cleans Weavile/Chandelure/Whimsicott with Sucker Punch and punishes Tauros Intimidate via Defiant. Altaria is the flex mega for Annihilape/Hydrapple/Weavile-heavy brings (Ground-immune, Fairy spread). Avoid Intimidating Annihilape (Defiant) and keep Gengar/Kingambit away from Excadrill Ground moves.

Play Tailwind offense with Whimsicott and Excadrill, or build an Annihilape endgame with Beat Up and Maushold's redirection; bring four with a clear damage plan rather than automatically bringing both supports. Weavile supplies the fastest unboosted Fake Out in this matchup and pressures Salamence, while Hydrapple answers Rotom-Wash and supplies special damage. Against Mega Gengar, establish Tailwind safely—often with Annihilape protecting—and remember that Annihilape can escape Shadow Tag, but our other five cannot. Preserve Excadrill against Mega Altaria, and use Defiant Annihilape to discourage Salamence's Intimidate.

offers.offerReasoning: All 8 rosters sit at 100, so only equal-cost 1-for-1s are legal. No 18-cost piece exists to get Incineroar; no 11-cost piece exists to get Arcanine. Core 19/16/15s would have to move for Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Kanga/Primarina, which guts the Mega-DN enable core and those coaches will not sell W1 staples anyway. Rotom-for-Tauros/Qwilfish/Mawile is Arbok-tier Intimidate and wrecks the Combat FA (drop Houndoom+Rotom, sign Combat 3). Keep the 10, take Combat in FA.

offers.message: 3-for-3 benched swap, both stay 100. You get Intimidate/FakeOut/KnockOff Scrafty (hits Ghosts like Sinistcha/Gengar, CC for Steels) for your crime-fighting core. We get Sturdy Tailwind/Taunt Steel for rain prep. Win-win fit.
offers.offerReasoning: Equal 3-3 keeps both at 100. Skarmory gives 2nd Tailwind (only Noivern has TW), Sturdy, Hurricane 0.5x + Fairy 0.5x resists vs Pelipper/MGardevoir where Scrafty is weak (2x Flying, 4x Fairy), IronHead SE vs Gardevoir + DrillRun SE vs Arch. Preserves Mega + core 5 for W2, adds Steel/Espeed resist for future. Scrafty benched-for-benched, past-bench Skarmory for them.
offers.responseReasoning: Cost-neutral 1-for-1 (Skarmory 3 <-> Scrafty 3), keeps 10 mons and 100/100. Skarmory is deep bench for me: never registered, redundant with Talonflame as Tailwind, and Spikes is low-impact in doubles. Scrafty fills my single biggest structural gap — I run no Fake Out — while adding a genuinely distinct support package: Fake Out (tempo), Knock Off (item control vs Sitrus/Mental Herb), Snarl, Taunt, Quick Guard, Coaching, plus Dark STAB (2x vs the Ghosts/Psychics all over this league: Dragapult, Ceruledge, Gengar-Mega, Sinistcha, Skeledirge, Farigiraf, Indeedee-F) and Close Combat for Steel walls (Gholdengo, Kingambit, Archaludon, Corviknight, Empoleon). Ice Punch is an extra 4x Dragonite tool if needed. Body is bulky (65/90/115/45/115/58) with Intimidate, so it fits my bulky-offense shell as a flex slot. Weak to Fairy/Fighting/Flying and it duplicates Arcanine's Intimidate, but the Fake Out + Knock Off + Dark STAB combination is an option I can neither buy with my 0 free budget nor get from anyone already on the roster. Losing Skarmory to a week-3 opponent is a mild concern (it resists Steel and checks Metagross), but Talonflame/Arcanine Fire handles it. Net upgrade in flexibility for a mon I never used.

offers.message: 12-for-12 benched swap, both stay 100. You get Fire/Ghost for Steels/Grasses, we get Ground/Ice for Dragons. Fair.
offers.offerReasoning: Second offer attempt to gain Ice, else will pass.
offers.responseReasoning: Value is nominal (12<->12) but fit is not. Ceruledge (Fire/Ghost, 125 Atk, Bitter Blade/Poltergeist/Shadow Sneak/Swords Dance/Flash Fire) is a strong mon, but it would be my THIRD Fire-type (Talonflame, Arcanine already) and stacks shared Water/Ground/Rock/Ghost/Dark weaknesses on a bulky-offense team whose remaining flaw is exactly that (Metagross already 2x weak to Ground). Its main niche — Ghost/Dark pressure on Psychics/Ghosts — is now partly covered by the Scrafty I just acquired (Dark STAB, Knock Off). Meanwhile Mamoswine is my ONLY Ground-type, ONLY Rock Slide spread, my Ice Shard priority revenge killer, my 4x Rock Slide answer to Charizard-Y (the core of my already-built week-2 sun plan) and Freeze-Dry covers Water-types; none of that is replaceable in-house. Schedule factor: the offer comes from muse, my week-3 opponent, who would receive a Mamoswine that hits my Metagross 2x with Earthquake and threatens Talonflame with Rock Slide/Ice Shard right before facing me. I keep Mamoswine and address the Fire/Ghost role in-house if needed.

offers.offerReasoning: No trade improves the roster enough to justify disturbing the six-piece rain/terrain core. Equal-budget legal bench swaps are lateral, while meaningful Week 2 targets would require sacrificing a core member or violate the 100-point cap.

Every coach sits at exactly 100/100, so only equal-cost swaps are legal. My tradable pieces are the 4-pointers (Toxicroak, Mega Ampharos, Mega Glalie) and the 6-point Mega Steelix; the only equal-cost pieces on other rosters (Pincurchin, Clawitzer, Machamp, Rotom-Frost, Alcremie at 4; Toxtricity, Hydrapple, Chandelure at 6) are sidegrades at best and none fixes a real gap (redirection, reliable Intimidate/Fake Out beyond Kangaskhan). Glalie now has a defined role vs grok's Dragonite/Rillaboom, Toxicroak keeps the Dry Skin niche vs luna's rain, Steelix is the Fairy/Electric wall. No offer beats overpaying or churning for nothing.

offers.message: Equal-cost offer: Maushold for Gholdengo, keeping both rosters at 100. Maushold gives your sun team a non-Mega Friend Guard + Follow Me option alongside Charizard, and can protect Dragonite's setup or Venusaur from single-target pressure. It also has Helping Hand, Super Fang, Encore and Feint, so it needn't be a passive redirection slot. You retain Charizard as your headline special attacker; I gain a special attacking option for my Tailwind team.
offers.offerReasoning: Gholdengo's verified Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Nasty Plot/Thunderbolt/Trick compress immediate special offense and setup alongside Whimsicott, improving pressure into upcoming Fairy/Psychic cores and adding spread offense independent of MausApe. Losing unique Friend Guard/redirection is material, but this premium equal-cost attacker justifies it while preserving Whimsicott, Annihilape, and Mega Excadrill. Maushold offers genuine sun/setup support to the counterparty, though their demonstrated Gholdengo usage makes rejection plausible. No budget or species conflict.
offers.responseReasoning: Gholdengo is an indispensable offensive pillar, providing Good as Gold status immunity, Ghost/Steel defensive typing, and premier special spread damage (Make It Rain). Trading it for Maushold would strip our core special firepower and give a direct competitor a devastating Tailwind sweeper, while our roster already possesses ample redirection and support tools.

offers.offerReasoning: The Maushold-for-Gholdengo offer was rejected; our roster remains unchanged at 100/100. No remaining trade offers a sufficiently clear multi-week improvement to justify surrendering core roles. Retain Friend Guard/Follow Me, Whimsicott–Excadrill offense, Chandelure's Imprison/TR, and Hydrapple's Water resilience. Address upcoming matchups through rebuilt sets and separately evaluate targeted free-agent changes rather than making a lateral trade merely to transact.

Roster is at exactly 100/100 and every coach in the league is also at 100, so any trade forces incoming cost ≤ outgoing — only lateral or point-down swaps are possible, never upgrades. No hard hole has appeared: W1 won 2-1, the W2 script vs astra (Farig+Corv lead, TR core, Azu/Drag/Garg executes) is locked and counters the observed Whim/Weav/Ape/ExcMega core, and my notebook's transaction plan says trade only if a hole appears after W2. Bench (Mence, Clawitzer, Toxtricity, Palafin) already covers the scheduled archetypes. Preserving the TR engine intact is worth more than any available lateral swap; I keep both remaining windows for a targeted fix (second Wide Guard user, Ghost STAB, status-item holder) if W2 exposes one.
Roster is structurally complete at 100/100 points with optimal role compression, weather synergy, and tactical counters for upcoming matchups. Retaining full roster as planned.

No offer. Every roster in the league sits at exactly 100/100, so any swap must be exactly equal-priced to keep both sides legal — the market is effectively locked to same-cost 1-for-1s. My structural gap (no Fake Out) is now filled by Scrafty, and my written rule is to transact only when bench value converts into a starter-level upgrade, else do nothing. Scanning equal-cost targets: (a) Fillers Machamp 4 / Rotom-Frost 4 / Manectric 1 have no better same-cost body available (pincurchin, clawitzer, toxicroak, glalie-mega, ampharos-mega, alcremie, altaria, houndoom are all lateral or Mega-conflicting, and I value Machamp's Wide/Quick Guard and Rotom-Frost's Levitate+Electric/Ice). (b) Mamoswine 12 is NOT surplus: it is my only Ground STAB, only Rock Slide spread (4x Charizard-Y, my week-2 line), Ice Shard priority and Freeze-Dry Water coverage; the only unused 12s are Palafin (build-around Zero to Hero, clunky without reliable pivoting) and Rotom-Heat (Ground immunity already covered by Rotom-Frost's Levitate, and it adds a Water/Rock weakness). (c) Sinistcha 18 is my only Rage Powder, only Trick Room and my Heatproof/Scald sun tech; the 18-cost bodies I could ask for (Incineroar now redundant with Arcanine+Scrafty, Garchomp duplicates Mamoswine's Ground and adds a 4x Ice weakness, Gengar-Mega conflicts with Metagross, Indeedee-F duplicates redirection, Farigiraf) are either not clearly better or are their owners' core (glm brought Farigiraf 3/3), so acceptance odds are low and the gain is uncertain. (d) Arcanine 11 is core and the only 11 (Salamence) is a used core piece that duplicates Talonflame's Flying and Arcanine's Intimidate. Per my risk rule not to worsen the Fire/Ground weakness profile, I hold the roster and make no offer.

moves.reasoning: 9-mon Combat plan is illegal (exactly 10, 1-for-1). Only Greninja is a \u22653 cut that does not gut Fake Out/Follow Me/screens/DN/Sneasler/Dirge/Cloud Nine. Combat is the W2-planned Intimidate into Kanga/Gambit/Mence and the W5/W6 physical cores; we pick first so take it. Inteleon spends the leftover 4 on a Water we will actually bring: Snipe Shot bypasses W3 Farigiraf and W4 Indeedee Follow Me, 100% acc after the W1 Hydro miss, keeps Dark Pulse/Ice Beam, 125 SpA. Keep Rotom for W2 Tag and Altaria for W4/W7. Houndoom was never-bring. No Arbok/1-cost junk.

W2 rain: Overqwil Dark SE Indeedee/Basculegion Poison SE Gardevoir SwiftSwim+Intim+Taunt vs Pelipper/TW; Excadrill Ground SE Arch Steel SE Gardevoir Rock vs Pelipper, resists Draco/Fairy where Garchomp weak. Saves 13pts (100->87) bank for later, uses 2/6 allowance.

No free agent is a clear upgrade within the 100-point cap without cutting a core piece. Garchomp is appealing but replacing Basculegion, Indeedee, or Archaludon would weaken the established rain/terrain matchup plan; bench swaps are lateral or irrelevant.

Toxicroak and Mega Ampharos were the two roster pieces with no clear bring case (never registered in week 1; Ampharos is a 6th mega on a team that only megas Gengar). Greninja (7, just released by grok) is a real upgrade: 191 Spe Timid, Protean/Battle Bond, Icy Wind as a second speed-control source, Ice Beam for the league's many Dragons (Dragonite x2, Mega Salamence, Dragapult, Noivern, Garchomp), Dark Pulse for Gholdengo/Metagross/Sinistcha/Farigiraf, Taunt vs glm's Trick Room, U-turn pivoting. Houndoom (1) fills the remaining point as a Flash Fire switch-in for the Fire-heavy weeks (Zard-Y, Talonflame/Arcanine, Incineroar) with Snarl/Heat Wave/Dark Pulse. Net cost stays 100; keeps core Gengar/Kingambit/Kanga/Rotom-W/Salamence/Altaria/Glalie/Steelix and 4 swaps for later windows.

Keep the 100-point roster and all six swaps for the two remaining windows. The Gholdengo trade was rejected, not executed. Week1 exposed sequencing and preservation errors rather than a demonstrated roster failure; five members were never brought, so dismantling the support core now would be premature. For week2, existing Chandelure Imprison/TR, Rotom-Heat special pressure, Excadrill, and optional Maushold protection address dual speed control without relying on blocked Prankster Taunt. Preserve Weavile's natural Speed above Mega Salamence and Hydrapple's Water resilience for upcoming matchups. Araquanid would add valuable Wide Guard and slow Water offense, but financing it through Maushold forfeits our sole reliable Follow Me/Friend Guard combination, while its Flying/Electric weaknesses mean it is not a complete rain answer. Cheap Wide Guard substitutions likewise sacrifice useful roles without clearly improving the full six. Reassess after testing matchup-specific sixes in week2; prioritize genuine rain and spread-defense gaps then, rather than buying redundant Fire/Ghost/Steel offense or competing Megas now.

No swaps this window. The registered six (Farigiraf/Corv/Hatt/Azu/Drag/Garg) is locked for the W2 script vs astra and fits every scheduled archetype; W1 confirmed the core works (2-1, only loss was a misread, Corv untouched in G3). Bench pieces (Mence, Clawitzer, Palafin, Toxtricity) cover the known modes, and Clawitzer is specifically the first swap-in vs Mega Excadrill. Free-agent adds like Aegislash (16) or Mawile-Mega (16) would require dropping Mence (20) or Farigiraf (18) — the former sheds my only fast-sweeper insurance for a role Corv+Garg already fill, the latter is core. Everyone else is at/near budget and the pool upgrades available are lateral at best. Keeping all 6 season swaps banked for windows 2-3 preserves optionality if W2 exposes a hard hole (target list: second Wide Guard user, Ghost STAB, status-item holder).

Conserving all free-agent swaps. Roster is perfectly balanced at 100/100 points, featuring elite weather synergy (Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur), unblockable Intimidate (Tauros-Aqua), priority control (Dragonite Extreme Speed, Swampert Wide Guard, Passimian Quick Guard), Lightning Rod redirection (Raichu), and status immunity (Gholdengo Good as Gold), with direct tactical advantages against Week 2 opponent entrant 5.

One swap. Sinistcha (18) is my most expensive mon yet a purely situational bench support (redirection/TR/Heatproof), and 18 points on the bench is poor value; my meta notes already flag Fire and Ground as my two structural weaknesses. Hydreigon (14), now undrafted, patches BOTH: Dark/Dragon resists Fire 0.5x and Levitate grants a Ground immunity, while adding the special offense my team lacks (only Primarina/Rotom-Frost hit specially). Its kit fits my method: Dark Pulse 2x on the league's many Psychics/Ghosts (Farigiraf, Indeedee-F, Gardevoir, Gengar, Dragapult, Chandelure, Annihilape, Skeledirge), Flash Cannon for Fairies, Fire Blast/Heat Wave for Steels/Grasses, plus Tailwind (backup speed control), Snarl (spread SpA drop that sun doesn't weaken), U-turn (safe pivot to bring Metagross/Primarina in), Taunt and Nasty Plot. Cost drops 100 -> 96, roster stays 10 mons, one per base species. I keep every key role: Talonflame Tailwind, Arcanine Intimidate/ESpeed/Snarl, Scrafty Fake Out/Knock Off/Intimidate, Machamp Wide Guard/Quick Guard, Rotom-Frost Levitate/Electric+Ice, Mamoswine Ground/Ice/Rock, Manectric Lightning Rod (still shields Primarina/Talonflame/Arcanine from Electric and offers a Mega option), primarina/Metagross wincons. Its Fairy/Ice frailty is a managed risk covered by four Fairy-resistant bodies and my Fake Out/Wide Guard; losing Rage Powder is acceptable since I already have Fake Out, Wide Guard, Quick Guard and Intimidate for protection. I rejected Garchomp (18, 4x Ice, physical, overlaps Mamoswine) and Aegislash (16, adds a second Fire/Ground-weak Steel, worsening my documented weakness). Holding the spare 4 points and 5 swaps for later windows.

weeklyReviews.reasoning: Reconcile 3 changes: Scrafty->Skarmory, Ceruledge->Overqwil, Garchomp->Excadrill. Update plan roster/cost, W2 six (Skarmory over Scrafty, bench new mons with reasons), new roles, build rules (2nd TW), future rosters (deepseek +Scrafty/Hydreigon -Sinistcha/Skarmory, claude -Ampharos, grok +Tauros/Inteleon).

W1 window closed with a different path than the pre-window plan: dropped Greninja and Houndoom, signed Combat and Inteleon, kept Rotom. Rewrote plan, sets, rules, calcs, W2, later weeks, and transactions so every later build sees the 10 we actually own. W2 default is now Combat over Clef; Inteleon is the Water/Snipe Shot for W3-W7 Follow Me and weather weeks, not a Gengar-lead partner. Opponent W2/W6 rosters updated for their window.

Roster changed: Toxicroak + Mega Ampharos out, Greninja (7) + Houndoom (1) in (both picked up from grok, who replaced them with Tauros-Paldea-Combat and Inteleon). Updated plan roster/roles, verified Greninja/Houndoom stats and calcs, rewrote the week 2 scout for grok's new roster (Greninja Dark Pulse threat gone; Inteleon Dark Pulse/Sniper crit and Tauros Close Combat are the new threats; Tauros Intimidate feeds Kingambit Defiant), refreshed league_scouting roster changes for deepseek/muse and swapped Ampharos/Toxicroak angles for Greninja/Houndoom angles. Noted Choice Specs is illegal in this format.

Reconciliation after window 1. Roster actually changed: OUT Sinistcha (dropped, 18) and Skarmory (traded to muse for Scrafty). IN Hydreigon (14) and Scrafty (3). Spend fell 100 -> 96, so 4 budget is FREE. Rewrote plan/roster/playbook to the new 10 (Fake Out + Intimidate tempo shell gained; redirection, Trick Room, Spikes and the Heatproof sun-soak lost). Updated transactions for the 4-free next window with role targets (redirection/TR control/Toxicroak free agent). Updated meta edge/weakness lines and refreshed opp_w2 (my six vs sun), opp_w3 (muse gained Skarmory/Overqwil/Excadrill, lost Garchomp/Ceruledge/Scrafty), opp_w4 (claude dropped Toxicroak/Ampharos-Mega, added Greninja/Houndoom), opp_w5 (no TR reversal available).

W1 loss dissected: sun prep wrong, WideGuard+InnerFocus+Espeed punished Garchomp/Ceru. Fix validated G2. W2 rain+terrain scouted. Ghost immunity, Thunder-in-rain, terrain override via calcs. Only Noivern has Tailwind - must bring + add Skarmory backup. Ceruledge dead -> Skarmory swap saves 9.

Full W1 review: series won 2-1 with 0 errors in G2/G3; archived the repeatable script and G1 lessons in 'series-w1-luna'. Scouted all three public series to build forward intel: verified astra (W2) sheets incl. Piercing Drill (Protect-pierce at 1/4 damage), Annihilape Defiant+Rage Fist, Weavile Fake Out, and their 3/3 Whimsicott+Weavile lead; wrote 'intel-w2-astra' and 'intel-w3-w7' dossiers with observed moves/habits and unknown-slot assumptions. Ran ~30 damage checks to build a verified W2 kill-pair book (Corv BP+Garg BP one-turn TR kill on Mega Excadrill; Dragalge 4x on Whimsicott; Garg/Azu answer Chand/Rotom-Heat; Farigiraf Ghost-immunity wall). Consolidated all sim laws (TR, Protect streaks, FM, Draco self-drop, Defiant/Competitive, Piercing Drill, Normal/Psychic Ghost immunity) into 'laws'. New plan page prioritizes the W2 six (Farig/Corv/Hatt/Azu/Drag/Garg, bench Mence due to Defiant) and defers transactions.

Week 1 lost 1-2 to gpt-6-astra. Root causes: repeating the exact G2 bring/lead in G3 into an adapting opponent, Salamence Sash giving zero value (double-targeted/multi-hit every game), no Ground-immune answer to Mega Excadrill brought, Gengar-Mega committed without our own Tailwind. Reorganised memory: plan page with roster roles, hard rules and week-2 bring vs grok; separate pages for verified stats/damage numbers, grok scouting (from public series 2 with calcs), gpt-6-astra series memory (playoff use), league scouting of other coaches, and piloting principles. Added transaction guidance: bench Toxicroak/Ampharos are the tradable pieces; target cheap Intimidate/Tailwind/Fake Out support.

Preserved roster flexibility after a win while identifying the actual G2 resource failure and G3 cumulative-priority survival error. Added sourced scouting of all remaining coaches, with detailed near-term anti-TR/rain preparation and corrected base-versus-Mega Salamence speed assumptions. Flagged current learnset discrepancies rather than perpetuating unverified Whimsicott utility. Transaction guidance evaluates coverage and opportunity cost without treating one week's benching as proof for a cut or full-board searches as availability.

Week 1 review. Kept the proven four (Metagross/Primarina/Talonflame/Arcanine) as the identity but rewrote the playbook around tools week 1 ignored: Talonflame/Skarmory Tailwind (my speed-control fix), Machamp Wide Guard/Quick Guard/Knock Off, Sinistcha Rage Powder/Trick Room/Heatproof/Scald (so the 18-cost is NOT wasted — keep it). Corrected a week-1 error: Fighting is neutral on Steel/Psychic Metagross, not resisted. Dex-verified every rival mega rather than importing mainline assumptions (Mega Clefable Fairy/Flying Magic Bounce, Mega Excadrill Piercing Drill, Mega Gengar Shadow Tag, etc.). Added a transaction-window stance with a costed Fake Out wishlist, and one scout page per remaining opponent (weeks 2-7) separating observed sets from hypotheses. The reserved notebook page is left untouched (validation forbids setting/deleting it); its content becomes a new 'playbook' page.

Reviewed the complete Week 1 turn records and build. The same voluntary Indeedee switch enabled Trick Room in both losses, so the new memory elevates active Imprison and target/position verification to hard rules, while tailoring the transaction and preparation plan to Week 2's different roster.

Week 1 was a decisive 2-0 victory against Muse. Our roster demonstrated flawless synergy, with Swampert's Wide Guard, Dragonite's Inner Focus + E-Speed, Scarf Gholdengo, and Mega Charizard Y performing at peak execution. Heading into Week 2 against #1 seed deepseek-v4.1-flash, our roster is 100% complete and requires 0 transactions. DeepSeek's core (Mega Metagross, Talonflame, Arcanine, Primarina, Sinistcha, Mamoswine) is heavily countered by Charizard Y's Sun Overheat/Heat Wave, Swampert's Wide Guard, Passimian's Quick Guard and Defiant, Raichu's Lightning Rod and Fake Out, and Venusaur's Chlorophyll. Stored comprehensive memory pages for scouting/meta analysis, detailed team matchup playbooks, and exact technical set references.
