decisions.rationale: Lead Incin+Noivern for Fake Out into Venusaur to stop Sleep Powder and Tailwind to outrun Chlorophyll sun. Back Ceruledge Flash Fire wall/sweeper and Garchomp Rock Slide vs Zard/Dnite with EQ+Noivern immunity synergy.

Lead Dragonite and Gholdengo with Swampert and Mega Charizard Y in reserve. Dragonite's Inner Focus blocks Fake Out and Intimidate, while Gholdengo is immune to Fake Out and outspeeds the entire opposing team with Choice Scarf (223 Spe). This completely shuts down Incineroar/Garchomp lead pressure while threatening an immediate OHKO on Garchomp with 4x Ice Spinner and spread pressure with Make It Rain. Swampert provides Wide Guard and Ice Punch in the back, while Mega Charizard Y brings immense special nuclear offense.

Fake Out useless (Gholdengo Ghost immune, Dnite InnerFocus no flinch). Noivern Tailwind now risks double-target KO through sash (Espeed 31-45% + ShadowBall 42-61%). Protect preserves sash/TW for T2 while Incin Flare Blitz threatens 74-134% OHKO range on Gholdengo (better than Lariat 52-96%).

Gholdengo is heavily threatened by Incineroar's Flare Blitz / Darkest Lariat, so we switch Gholdengo out to Swampert who resists Fire and takes minimal damage. Dragonite targets Noivern with 4x Ice Spinner to break its Focus Sash, positioning Dragonite to finish Noivern next turn with Extreme Speed (+2 priority) regardless of whether Noivern sets Tailwind. Wide Guard on Swampert will also neutralize any Garchomp spread moves if opponent relies on Tailwind speed.

Tailwind is free: Noivern 192 outruns Dnite 100-132 and Swampert 80-112, only Espeed 31-45% goes first and cannot KO from full, WideGuard does not block Tailwind. Incin at 92% risks HighHorsepower 69-102% but Lariat neutral 25-46% into weakened Swampert is best chip; Flare Blitz NVE did only 25%. Get speed up now before Zard/Venu come in.

Noivern's Protect chance is drastically reduced after turn 1. Dragonite targets Noivern with 4x Ice Spinner to break its Focus Sash, preparing an Extreme Speed finish on turn 3. Swampert targets Incineroar with STAB super-effective High Horsepower to heavily damage or KO Incineroar (66-121% damage against 91% HP), removing the opponent's Intimidate pivot. Both Dragonite and Swampert have high bulk and easily survive incoming attacks this turn.

Incin 26% dies to any Ground/Water hit (HighHorse 69-102%) but still has Intimidate value, so switch first to Ceru which walls Dnite (Espeed immune, Ice 16-23%) and resists Ice Punch. Noivern 1% sash gone has no future TW value vs Espeed, so sack it to Taunt Dnite (384 TW speed outruns 100-132) to deny their Tailwind and preserve our speed edge for Ceru/Garchomp sweep.
Forced double replacement: only Incin 26% and Garchomp 100% remain. Restore Incin to slot A and Garchomp to slot B to keep Tailwind offense alive.

Dragonite's Extreme Speed (+2 priority) guarantees the KO on 1% HP Noivern before it can act (Air Slash/Taunt). Swampert's High Horsepower guarantees the KO on 26% HP Incineroar while remaining on the field, which preserves Wide Guard to completely wall Garchomp's spread moves on turn 4 even through opposing Tailwind.

Incin re-entered so Fake Out works and at 160 TW outruns Swampert to flinch WideGuard/attack before it moves. Garchomp dies to IceSpinner 97-138% + IcePunch 51-75% if it attacks, so Protect (+4 beats Espeed +2) to stay full. Sac Incin after Fake Out value to preserve Garchomp for last TW turn.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Dragonite)
decisions.rationale: Swampert uses Wide Guard (+3 priority), which blocks all three of Garchomp's attacking moves (Rock Slide, Earthquake, Breaking Swipe are all spread moves). This guarantees Dragonite cannot be double-targeted down by Darkest Lariat + Breaking Swipe, ensuring Dragonite survives and lands 4x Ice Spinner to OHKO Garchomp. Even if Incineroar Fakes Out Swampert to flinch Wide Guard, Dragonite easily survives Garchomp's Breaking Swipe from 100% HP to retaliate with Ice Spinner.

No bench so Parting Shot just debuffs. Debuff Dnite -1 before its IceSpinner (Incin 160 TW outruns 100-132) to turn 97-138% OHKO into survivable, plus Breaking Swipe spread -1 Atk to both foes for max survival vs double Ice. Beats Rock Slide damage because survival matters more at 1 turn TW left; WideGuard blocks either spread but Parting Shot still lands.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Dragonite)
decisions.rationale: Swampert uses Wide Guard (+3 priority), which cannot be flinched this turn (Incineroar already consumed Fake Out). Wide Guard 100% blocks all three of Garchomp's attacking moves (Breaking Swipe, Rock Slide, Earthquake), ensuring Dragonite takes at most single-target damage from 26% Incineroar. Dragonite at 100% HP easily survives and lands 4x Ice Spinner to OHKO Garchomp. Opponent's Tailwind ends this turn.
Position lost: 26%+20% no Tailwind vs 87%+53% plus 2 fresh including Scarf Gholdengo, Garchomp spread walled by WideGuard and 4x Ice weak, no bench. Forfeit unwinnable game1 to focus series.

reflections.summary: G1 loss: expected sun lead but got Dnite+Gholdengo into Swampert. FakeOut dead into Ghost/InnerFocus, Protect stalled T1 but T2 Tailwind cost Noivern sash and Incin Sitrus. Ceru switch-in OHKOed by HH, Noivern picked by Espeed, leaving Incin+Garchomp vs Dnite+Swampert. Garchomp all-spread walled by WideGuard and 4x Ice weak (97-138% Spinner), Tailwind expired for loss. Adjust to Clefable+Rotom over Garchomp+Ceru.
reflections.adjustment: Drop Garchomp+Ceruledge (all Garchomp damage spread walled by WideGuard and 4x Ice weak; Ceru OHKOed by High Horsepower and 76-110% to Shadow Ball). Bring Mega Clefable FollowMe + Rotom-Mow instead. Keep Incin+Noivern lead core but back with Clefable/Rotom: Fake Out Swampert stops WideGuard/attack, Tailwind goes up on sash, Rotom Leaf Storm deletes Swampert through WideGuard (single-target) and Levitate immunes High Horsepower, Clefable redirects/bounces and Moonblasts Dragonite.

reflections.summary: Game 1 was a decisive victory. Leading Dragonite + Gholdengo completely disarmed the opponent's Fake Out / Intimidate strategy. Pivoting Gholdengo to Swampert absorbed Incineroar's Flare Blitz, while Dragonite broke Noivern's Sash with Ice Spinner. Turn 3 produced a double KO as Dragonite cleaned Noivern with +2 Extreme Speed and Swampert OHKOed switching Ceruledge with High Horsepower. Swampert's Wide Guard then completely blocked Garchomp's Breaking Swipe on Turn 5 while Dragonite chunked Garchomp to 20%, prompting an immediate concession on Turn 6 with our entire team alive (4v2).
reflections.adjustment: Stick to the winning Dragonite + Gholdengo lead with Swampert and Mega Charizard Y in reserve. Be prepared for opponent to bring Clefable-Mega or Rotom-Mow to counter Swampert; Gholdengo's Make It Rain and Charizard's Sun-boosted Fire moves hard counter both adjustments.

decisions.rationale: Bring Incin/Noivern/Clefable/Rotom as planned. Lead Incin+Noivern for FakeOut pressure into Venusaur/Swampert/Passimian plus immediate Tailwind to outrun Chlorophyll; back Clefable FollowMe+bounce for sleep and Rotom LeafStorm for Swampert.

Lead Dragonite and Gholdengo with Swampert and Charizard in reserve. Dragonite's Inner Focus ignores Fake Out and Intimidate, Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds the entire enemy roster, Swampert provides a 100% hard lock against Garchomp's all-spread moveset via Wide Guard, and Charizard provides nuclear fire offense and Drought in the back.

G1 they swapped Gholdengo to Swampert T1, leaving only Dnite Ice Spinner. Tailwind is free then (Noivern outruns Dnite, sash survives at 1HP) and gives immediate speed (Incin 160 TW outruns Dnite same turn). Lariat into foe2 hits Swampert if swap (neutral ~36% to secure LeafStorm range) or Gholdengo 52-96% if stay, avoiding Flare Blitz NVE into Swampert and recoil. Protect delays TW and cost Incin HP last time.

Repeat the proven Game 1 Turn 1 line: Switch Gholdengo out to Swampert to cleanly absorb Incineroar's Fire attack, while Dragonite targets Noivern with 4x Ice Spinner to either break its Focus Sash immediately or force its Protect. Dragonite's Inner Focus ignores Fake Out/Intimidate, and +2 Extreme Speed bypasses any opposing Tailwind next turn.

Fake Out fails (not first turn), Incin risks HH ~90% and Noivern 1% dies to Espeed (+2 beats all Noivern moves). Double switch baits: Swampert HHs Incin-slot into Rotom Levitate immune, Dnite Ice into Noivern-slot into Clefable 27-39% resist (vs 42-92% into Rotom). Then TW Rotom LeafStorm 139-310% OHKOs Swampert 66% and Clefable Moonblast 58-104% pressures Dnite. Preserves Incin 100%+Sitrus and Noivern 1% for later TW/Intimidate.

Dragonite uses +2 priority Extreme Speed into Noivern to secure the KO before Noivern or Tailwind-boosted Incineroar can act. Incineroar lacks Protect, so Swampert uses STAB super-effective High Horsepower into Incineroar to deal 66-121% damage and remove its Sitrus Berry / bring it to critical HP.

Rotom LeafStorm 139-310% OHKOs Swampert 66% (no Protect). Swampert staying risks double Ice into Rotom (IcePunch 42-61% + Spinner 42-92% = 84-153% KO range) to trade 1-for-1. Clefable FollowMe (+2, 160 TW outruns Espeed/attacks) redirects both Ices into Clefable (Spinner 27-39% resist, survives from 64%) to guarantee LeafStorm and preserve Rotom. No Mega (base Fairy neutral to Ice vs Mega Flying 2x weak). If Swampert switches to Gholdengo/Zard/Venu resist, LeafStorm wasted+drop but Rotom saved and TW still 2 turns.

Execute a defensive double switch: Swampert expects Rotom-Mow's 4x Grass Leaf Storm, which Charizard easily absorbs (0.25x resistance). Dragonite expects Clefable's 2x Fairy Moonblast, which Gholdengo comfortably absorbs (0.5x resistance). This preserves both Dragonite and Swampert at full/high HP while letting opponent waste their Tailwind turns and giving us dominant offensive positioning with Scarf Gholdengo and Mega Charizard Y.

Mega Zard sun HeatWave 59-82% into Rotom (Occa) + MakeItRain 19-27% = 78-109% KO range on Rotom, and MakeItRain 68-99% always KOs Clefable 64% (HeatWave 52-73% also KOs high). FollowMe useless vs double spread. Switch Rotom (-2) to Incin resists both (Rain 14-20%, Heat NVE) + resets -2 for later Swampert, Protect Clefable to survive. Preserves both, stalls mega/sun turn with TW 1 left.

Gholdengo's Make It Rain deals 65.3-117.6% to Clefable, guaranteeing the KO on its remaining 64% HP while chipping Rotom-Mow. Charizard uses Protect without Mega Evolving to safely stall out the final turn of opposing Tailwind; withholding Mega Evolution prevents Drought from activating, ensuring Clefable cannot use Sun-boosted Flamethrower against Gholdengo. With Tailwind ending this turn, Charizard Y and Scarf Gholdengo will hold complete speed control for the remainder of the match.

Incin just switched so FakeOut live; FakeOut Charizard (flinch stops sun HeatWave even if it Mega-evolves first, Gholdengo immune so target Zard). Gholdengo -2 locked into MakeItRain weak (34-49% vs Clefable, 7-10% vs Incin) so Clefable safe to Flamethrower Gholdengo 40-72% SE (better than Moonblast NVE). Stops spread damage this turn, chips Gholdengo for FlareBlitz KO range next.

Opposing Tailwind has expired, granting our side full Speed dominance. Gholdengo's Make It Rain deals 27.7-60% into Clefable while non-Mega Charizard's Overheat deals 40.1-82.9%, combining for a guaranteed KO (minimum 67.8% vs 64% HP) even if Clefable Mega Evolves. Withholding Mega Evolution keeps Drought inactive, ensuring that even if Incineroar Fakes Out Charizard, Clefable cannot OHKO Gholdengo with a Sun-boosted Flamethrower (dealing at most 91.5%).

Gholdengo 28% dies to any Incin STAB (Lariat min 52% >28%, no recoil vs FlareBlitz). Gholdengo -4 weak so Incin 80% tanks both spreads (Rain NVE 7-10%, Heat NVE). Clefable 22% dies to any spread (Rain -4 22-33% + Heat 52-73%) so Protect (full success, didn't Protect last turn) to survive. Preserves Rotom 100% for T7 vs Zard/Swampert instead of switching now into 59-82% Heat.

Both our Pokémon hold absolute Speed control over the unboosted foes (Scarf Gholdengo at 223 and Charizard at 152 vs foe max 112). Fake Out is no longer available to Incineroar. Gholdengo's Make It Rain deals 21.8-40% to Clefable, guaranteeing the KO on its remaining 21% HP. Mega Charizard Y activates Drought and uses Heat Wave; because both attacks are spread moves, Follow Me cannot redirect them, ensuring Clefable is eliminated while heavily damaging Incineroar.

Send in Dragonite to replace Gholdengo. Dragonite at full HP possesses +2 priority Extreme Speed, which naturally outspeeds Clefable (132 vs max 112 Spe) to guarantee the KO on Clefable's remaining 21% HP before it can act, while Mega Charizard Y in Drought exerts overwhelming board pressure alongside healthy Swampert in reserve.

Clefable 22% dies to Espeed (36% earlier) before any attack (+2 beats 0) and to sun Heat 52-73%, Protect 50% unreliable. Incin 70% survives double (Espeed 23-33% + sun Heat 21-30% =44-63% leaves 7-26%). Sac expendable Noivern 1% (cannot set TW at 1% vs spread/priority) to absorb slot: switch Clefable->Noivern preserves Clefable 22% + Rotom 100% clean for T8 (vs risking Rotom 59-82% Heat +25-36% Espeed =84-118% KO range if switched now). Incin Lariat Zard 31-59% vs 47% KOs high roll.

Zard KO'd, Noivern sacked as planned. Incin 22% dies to Espeed (23-33%) but must stay; bring Rotom 100% (not Clefable 22% which also dies to Espeed) for LeafStorm OHKO vs Swampert 66% incoming + Tbolt vs Dnite. Preserve Clefable 22% for later.

Dragonite's +2 priority Extreme Speed outspeeds Clefable (132 vs max 112 Spe) even if Clefable attempts Follow Me (+2 priority), dealing 21.3-46.5% to guarantee the KO on Clefable's remaining 21% HP before it can move. Targeting Clefable with Charizard would be redundant if Clefable doesn't Protect and futile if it does, so Charizard uses 100%-accurate super-effective Scorching Sands into Incineroar to deal 38.6-71.8% damage and bring it into critical range without sacrificing Special Attack stages.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Incin 22% dies to Espeed (23-33%) before any move, but sacs to absorb Espeed aimed at low slot. Rotom LeafStorm 139-310% OHKOs Swampert 66% (no Protect). Rotom 106 outruns Swampert 80-112 (usually) so KOs before IcePunch 42-61%; Dnite alone max 92% Spinner or 36% Espeed cannot OHKO Rotom 100%, so Rotom survives if Dnite Espeeds Incin (likely pick). Incin Lariat Dnite 25-47% chips if they ignore Incin (Ice NVE).
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Dragonite's +2 priority Extreme Speed deals 21.8-39.4% to Incineroar, guaranteeing the KO on its remaining 21% HP before it can act. Swampert targets Rotom-Mow with super-effective Ice Punch (40.8-76.8%). Even if Rotom-Mow connects with Leaf Storm into Swampert, its Special Attack drops to -2, leaving it completely incapable of threatening full-health Lum Berry Dragonite, who easily finishes Rotom-Mow and Clefable (21% HP) to seal the match and series win.

2v1 vs Dnite 100% but Clefable 22% dies to Espeed 36% before Moonblast 58-104% (Espeed +2 beats 0, Dnite 100-132 faster than 80). Must halve damage with burn to survive (burned Espeed 18% <22% lets Moonblast go). Lum cures first WoW so need two WoWs: T9 Clefable Protect (100%, blocks Espeed, preserves) + Rotom WoW (85%, consumes Lum). No Mega (base Fairy neutral to Ice vs Mega Flying 2x). Rotom -2 weak so support, not attack.

Dragonite's +2 priority Extreme Speed moves first in the turn (naturally outspeeding Clefable at 132 vs max 112 Spe) and deals 21.3-46.5%, guaranteeing the KO on Clefable's remaining 21% HP before it can move. Rotom-Mow at -2 SpA deals a negligible 17.9-26.8% with Thunderbolt and cannot status Dragonite through Lum Berry, securing a guaranteed win.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: WoW missed (15%), Lum intact, still need burn to halve Espeed 36% to 18% <22% so Moonblast can go. T9 Protect blocked Espeed as planned. Retry Protect (50% consecutive) + WoW (85%): Protect blocks Espeed pick, WoW consumes Lum. Without burn Moonblast never lands vs faster Espeed.

Clefable used Protect on Turn 9, making a consecutive Protect highly likely to fail. Dragonite's +2 priority Extreme Speed acts first, easily securing the KO on Clefable's remaining 21% HP (21.3-46.5% damage). Dragonite sits at 100% HP with Lum Berry intact, while Rotom-Mow at -2 SpA deals negligible damage with Thunderbolt, guaranteeing victory.

1v1 Rotom 100% -2 vs Dnite 100% Lum gone. Must burn (halves Espeed 25-36% to 12-18% and Spinner 42-92% to 21-46% + 6% chip) to win stall. WoW 85% sticks now. Protect next to stall burn + chip with Tbolt 14-26%.

Rotom-Mow holds an Occa Berry (which only reduces Fire damage, not Ice), so Dragonite's STAB-tier 2x super-effective Ice Spinner hits for 49.7-92.8% damage. Meanwhile, Rotom-Mow at -2 SpA deals a paltry 17.9-26.8% with Thunderbolt into Dragonite's 100% HP, locking in an unlosable 2HKO.

Dragonite's super-effective Ice Spinner deals 24.8-46.4% to Rotom-Mow's remaining 32% HP. Even through burn and potential Protect, Rotom-Mow at -2 SpA is incapable of dealing meaningful damage to Dragonite's 94% HP pool (Thunderbolt does max 26.8%), ensuring a guaranteed victory this turn or next.

Rotom 32% -2 vs 88% brn. Protect 50% stalls only 6% (88->82%) and chain dies. Must chip: Tbolt 14-26% vs 88% ->62-74% + burn 6% ->56-68%. Survives burned Spinner 21-46% low roll 21-31% (44%) to continue miracle. No other out.

Even if Rotom survives with sliver HP, its -2 SpA Thunderbolt deals at most 26.8% to Dragonite's 88% HP pool, locking up the series sweep.

reflections.summary: Lost G2 and series 0-2. Adjustment (Garchomp/Ceru -> Clefable/Rotom) helped: avoided WideGuard wall and HH OHKO, got TW up T1, baited HH immune, KOed Gholdengo/Zard/Swampert to reach 2v1 vs solo Dnite 100% (vs G1 forfeit with 0 KOs). Lost winning endgame to variance + structural -2: T3 LeafStorm crit into switched Zard 0.25x left Rotom -2 all game (Tbolt 14-26% vs Dnite), T9 WoW missed (15%), T10 Protect failed (50%) losing Clefable 22% before Moonblast 58-104% could fire vs faster Espeed, Lum ate first burn, Spinner high-rolled 68% (100->32%), burned 1v1 Rotom -2 couldn't outrace Dnite.
reflections.adjustment: Future vs this Dnite/Swampert/Gholdengo/Zard core: keep Rotom+Clefable over Garchomp+Ceru (spread walled by WideGuard, Ceru OHKOed by HH) but fix endgame. Don't LeafStorm blind T3 into likely Zard/Gholdengo resist (0.25x/0.5x + -2 crippled Rotom all game); Tbolt Dnite or double-target Dnite instead, save LeafStorm for confirmed Swampert stay. After TW expires, preserve Incin HP (don't trade 48% into Scorching Sands SE) and preserve one Protect for Clefable Moonblast turn — Moonblast 58-104% is only Dnite answer, it never fired because 22% dies to +2 Espeed first. Bring Noivern back later for second TW instead of sacking 1% early if Dnite left.

reflections.summary: Game 2 and the series (2-0) were won through superior positioning, disciplined weather management, and dominant priority control. Leading Dragonite + Gholdengo once again neutralized Incineroar's Intimidate and Fake Out, prompting opponent to pivot into Rotom-Mow and Clefable. Our Turn 3 defensive double switch (swapping Charizard into Swampert's slot to absorb 4x-resisted Leaf Storm, and Gholdengo into Dragonite's slot to absorb Moonblast) reduced Rotom to -2 Special Attack while keeping all four of our Pokémon alive. On Turn 5, intentionally delaying Charizard's Mega Evolution prevented Drought from boosting Clefable's Flamethrower, allowing Gholdengo to comfortably survive and chip Clefable into KO range. Dragonite then closed out the match via Lum Berry (nullifying Will-O-Wisp) and consecutive +2 Extreme Speeds and Ice Spinners, methodically eliminating Noivern, Incineroar, Clefable, and Rotom-Mow.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series against this opponent, maintain the Dragonite + Gholdengo lead with Swampert and Charizard Y in reserve as the default baseline. If opponent leans heavily into Rotom-Mow + Clefable leads to anticipate Swampert, consider leading Charizard Y + Venusaur to exert immediate Sun-boosted Chlorophyll Sleep Powder and Sludge Bomb pressure before Clefable or Rotom can set up.

decisions.rationale: Bringing the TR control core. Corviknight leads to wall Mega Gardevoir's Hyper Voice (0.5x, Iron Head is 2x back; Body Press 2x Archaludon) while Hatterene sets Trick Room on T1 - Magic Bounce covers Indeedee's Imprison and there's no Taunt/Encore/Disable on their sheets. Once TR is up all my mons (49-87 Spe) outspeed their entire roster (93+ min) and move first. Farigiraf is the backup setter with Armor Tail blanking their only priority (Aqua Jet) plus Foul Play 2x Basculegion; Dragalge soaks Electro Shot (0.5x) and Adaptability Sludge Wave is 2x/OHKO-range on Gardevoir. Dropped Mence (loses to Hyper Voice focus; Intimidate wasted into Mirror Armor... their Intimidate Qwilfish is the threat, but walls matter more here) and Clawitzer (79 Spe is dead weight without TR, Farigiraf's double-setter insurance is more consistent).

Lead Indeedee-F with Pelipper to establish Psychic Terrain/rain while immediately threatening to Imprison Trick Room and retaining Follow Me support. Basculegion and Mega Gardevoir provide strong rain and anti-Dragon endgame pressure.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Hatterene sets TR (-7 resolves last; even if Indeedee uses its own TR first, my TR overwrites with a fresh 5t and helps me either way - all my speeds 49-87 sit below their 93+ range). If Imprison is used, Magic Bounce bounces it. Corviknight Iron Heads Indeedee (2x STAB): if Indeedee Follow-Me redirects, it takes the hit anyway and may KO/crit; terrain stays up regardless. Targeting Pelipper is 0.5x and sash-protected, so Indeedee is the lane.
Imprison immediately denies Hatterene's revealed Trick Room, while Pelipper establishes Tailwind to offset the opponent's potential Tailwind and enable the incoming rain offense.

Imprison is the linchpin of their anti-TR plan, and it only holds while Indeedee is on the field. Both attacks into Indeedee: Iron Head (22-43%) + Dark Pulse (29-54%) vs 76% - combined odds to KO are solid, and if Follow Me is used it redirects both into the same target anyway. Hatterene can't Protect (Imprison blocks it) and can't TR, so Dark Pulse is the only real action. Even if Indeedee survives, it must burn Protect/Follow Me or switch, and if it self-TRs, TR helps me more than them. Pelipper's Hurricane into Hatterene (37-56%) is survivable with Sitrus.
Indeedee uses Follow Me to keep both attacks away from Pelipper while Imprison remains active, and Pelipper pressures the dangerous Hatterene with Hurricane.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Indeedee sits at 14% - any hit ends Imprison. Corv moves before Hatterene (87 > 49), so Iron Head kills it first and Trick Room resolves right after, same turn, even if Indeedee only tried to Protect/switch... if it Protects, TR fails and I adapt T4, but at 14% they more likely switch it out or eat the KO. Freeing Hatterene's TR the same turn is worth risking a Hurricane chip (37-56% on 56%, Sitrus covers the low end).

Resubmitting: TR was rejected as disabled while Imprison is live, so the KO->TR chain in one turn isn't possible. Instead: Corv Iron Head ends Indeedee (14% < 22% min), which kills Imprison for next turn; Hatterene Dark Pulses Pelipper to chip through its Sash rather than wasting a target on an already-doomed Indeedee (its attack would fizzle after Corv's KO). Hatterene can't be KO'd by a plain Hurricane except a ~max roll (37-56% on 56 HP%), Sitrus covers sub-50. TR goes up cleanly next turn once Imprison is gone.

Farigiraf is the immediate TR setter - Imprison died with Indeedee, so TR is legal again and I want the speed inversion up before their Tailwind even expires. Farigiraf also handles the likely Gardevoir switch-in well (0.5x to terrain-boosted Expanding Force, tanky 213 HP) whereas Dragalge would walk into 2x Expanding Force while terrain is still up. Armor Tail + Mental Herb protect the TR attempt; Dragalge stays fresh for the rain lane afterwards.
Hatterene is at 55% and remains the primary Trick Room threat; Helping Hand amplifies Pelipper's Hurricane for a likely knockout while Imprison continues to deny Trick Room.
Bring in Basculegion to exploit the remaining rain and Tailwind immediately; Pelipper remains active while the next opposing Pokémon is revealed.

Basculegion is the linchpin: its rain Wave Crash is the only guaranteed OHKO on my last TR setter, so TR is impossible while it lives. Farigiraf Protects (only safe action - if it attacks, it dies to Wave Crash before resolving). Corviknight Iron Heads Basculegion for chip: if Basc crashes Corv in response, Corv survives all rolls (58.5+15.5 min vs 100%) while Basc pays ~64-86% total (my chip + Helmet + LO + recoil) - setting up a kill. If Basc refuses to crash Corv, I keep chipping while it sits passive. Corv eats the risk because Dragalge (no Helmet, Leftovers) is worse at punishing crashes and Corv's Iron Head/Helmet are my best Basc pressure.

Farigiraf is the remaining Trick Room enabler. Double-targeting it with rain-boosted Wave Crash and Hurricane uses the current speed advantage and gives the best chance to remove it before Trick Room.

Protect's next-use success is 33% - a 67% chance to lose my last TR setter to a rain Wave Crash is unacceptable when a free switch exists. Farigiraf to the bench preserves it at 100% for the post-rain TR window (T6+: Wave Crash 67-98% can never solo it). Corviknight stays and chips Basculegion down (every % helps the eventual TR-turn survival odds and the kill race), taking at most 74-109% combined burst on 100% HP - survivable on all but high-high rolls.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Farigiraf's Protect is now less reliable; repeat the double-target to punish it and potentially KO before its negative-priority Trick Room can resolve. Basculegion's rain-boosted Wave Crash is the main knockout attempt.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: This is the planned TR window: rain expired, so Basculegion's Wave Crash (67-98%) can no longer solo-KO a full-HP Farigiraf - TR resolves after their attacks and lands unless they roll high-high with crash+Hurricane into the same target (~45-50% death chance, less if Hurricane misses). Foul Play now would 'trade' Basc but leave Farigiraf at 2-33%, permanently ending TR - worse EV than keeping the setter at full HP. Corviknight chips Basculegion to 20-28% so that the very first Foul Play under TR is a guaranteed KO.

Preserve the heavily injured Basculegion from Farigiraf's super-effective Dark attack, Mega Evolve Gardevoir, and double-target Farigiraf with Hyper Voice plus Hurricane to deny another Trick Room attempt.

Under Trick Room Corviknight acts before Gardevoir and Iron Head's minimum (48%) exceeds Gardevoir's 4% - a guaranteed kill that also denies their Mega and any Protect read. Farigiraf Protects rather than chipping: the Foul Play chip (~10-24%) is worth far less than keeping 59% HP, since Farigiraf only needs to survive 2-3 Hurricanes (and every KO'd foe shifts chip duty to Corviknight's Roost loop). Confusion makes every Farigiraf action a 33% no-op, so no-risk Protect maximizes setter survival while Gardevoir dies regardless.

Gardevoir is at 5% and Trick Room lets Corviknight move first, so Mega Protect preserves it from another Iron Head while securing the Mega resource. Pelipper continues attacking the confused Farigiraf.

Corviknight takes the kill job (never confused): Iron Head minimum 48% removes Gardevoir-Mega's 4% before it can act, unless it chains a reduced-success Protect (33%). Farigiraf Foul Plays Pelipper for the only meaningful chip available - double-tapping a 4% target wastes both attacks and leaves Pelipper untouched at 100%, whereas this split keeps the endgame boss on a kill clock. Basculegion stays benched until a slot opens, and the kill of Gardevoir forces it in next turn where Foul Play (min 39.6% vs 37%) or a Corv-baited Wave Crash suicide closes it out.

A second Protect is unreliable and Corviknight's Iron Head would otherwise remove the 5%-HP Mega Gardevoir. Switch to the 37%-HP Basculegion as a buffer while Pelipper keeps pressuring the confused Farigiraf.

Farigiraf is at 23% and will die to essentially any incoming hit - its last safe high-value action is Foul Play, which is a guaranteed KO on Basculegion's 21% (min 39.6%), removing the only mon that can OHKO my side before Trick Room expires. Corviknight sets Tailwind this turn: it costs nothing while TR is up (my doubled 144/174 still act first vs their doubled 186+), and from T11 it lets both survivors outspeed Pelipper (93-128), turning the endgame grind into a 2-attacker kill clock instead of a lone Corviknight race.
Farigiraf is at only 23%, so Basculegion must commit Wave Crash while Pelipper provides a second knockout attempt. Removing the Trick Room setter is more important than preserving Basculegion at 22%.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

The 4% Gardevoir is a Protect-bait (they Protected it predictively at T7 and sac-swapped it out once already) - Iron Heading it is 60%+ a wasted turn. Pelipper is the actual endgame boss and the only mon that can out-damage Corviknight's Roost loop over time, so every guaranteed chip matters: Iron Head takes it to 62-70%. Gardevoir at 4% cannot survive my Iron Head once it acts post-TR (Corviknight outspeeds it 174 to 120-152 under Tailwind, and its Protect chain is reduced), and even its best anti-Corv play (Mystical Fire + Hurricane) leaves Corviknight alive to Roost-stabilize.

With Trick Room still active, both attacks can resolve before Corviknight's Iron Head. Mystical Fire is the strongest super-effective hit, while Hurricane adds chip and together gives the best immediate chance to finish Corviknight.

Roost is the only safe action: with Gardevoir-Mega alive (Mystical Fire 33-47% even at -1 SpA) plus Pelipper's Hurricane, any Corviknight attack this turn risks the 48-70% combo against 40% HP. Roosting to ~90% survives everything and sets up the guaranteed Iron Head kill on Gardevoir next turn - its Protect chain was reset (Protect T7, Mystical Fire T10), so at most one successful Protect remains before the 2x STAB connects. Pelipper cannot burst Corviknight alone (Hurricane 15-23%, 70% acc).
Corviknight is at 39%; repeat the super-effective Mystical Fire plus Hurricane before it can Roost, accepting the risk to 5%-HP Gardevoir to maximize the knockout chance.

With Corviknight at 31% and Mystical Fire alone (22-37% at -2 SpA) nearly lethal, the only live win path is using my Tailwind speed priority to remove the Mystical Fire source before it acts: Iron Head's 48% minimum vastly exceeds Gardevoir's 4%. If they Protect (likely), Corviknight survives on Hurricane alone (8-16%), Roosts last next turn to ~58-66% where the decayed (-3 SpA) MF + Hurricane combo can no longer kill, and the 1v1 Pelipper grind is fully sustainable via Roost. Roosting instead leaves Corviknight eating the full MF+Hurricane combo at 31% with no kill pressure - strictly worse.
Corviknight is at 31%; Mystical Fire remains the only strong super-effective option, and Hurricane supplies the needed finishing chip before another Roost.

The gamble paid off - Gardevoir-Mega died before it could act, leaving the Mystical Fire threat gone. Now Corviknight at 11% must Roost: it outsped by Pelipper (93-128), any Hurricane hit is lethal at 11%, so the only live line is Hurricane missing (30%) followed by an unconfused Roost (67%) to 61%, after which the Roost/Iron Head loop out-sustains and out-chips Pelipper 1v1 indefinitely. Attacking instead leaves Corviknight killable to the very next Hurricane.
Gardevoir is fainted; Pelipper must use its final Hurricane to finish the confused 10%-HP Corviknight.

reflections.summary: Game 1 lost 0-1 in 13 turns. Structure was mostly right, variance and two fixable choices killed it. What worked: killing Indeedee to end Imprison (TR gate), Farigiraf's Foul Play executions (Basculegion KO), Corviknight's Miracle-armor grind (walls Hyper Voice/MF, Mirror Armor made their Mystical Fire self-nerf -1 SpA per use, Tailwind-priority kill on Gardevoir-Mega at T12), and correct kill-order math throughout. What went wrong: (1) their anti-TR screen (Tailwind+Imprison lead, Helping Hand+Hurricane snipe) - Hatterene died T3 to the burst I'd read but chose to trade into; my T3 resubmit (Dark Pulse chip on Pelipper instead of Protecting Hatterene) was the key fixable error - Hatterene Protect (100% chain) survives and TR goes up a turn earlier with a setter intact; (2) Dragalge's entry T5 was a pure sponge turn and it died to a max-roll Wave Crash (~84%) + Hurricane - entry-turn Protect would have kept it alive; (3) the 4% Gardevoir survived 6 turns on sac-swaps/Protect while Corv chipped Pelipper - by the time G died (T12, they finally didn't Protect), Corv was at 11% and the T13 Roost needed a Hurricane miss (30%) that didn't come. The 1 decision error was the T3 rejected submission (Hatterene Trick Room disabled by live Imprison). Net: right plan, wrong setter-safety sequencing; game 2 should lead the walls and Protect entries instead of trading into bursts.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the TR frame but restructure the opener: G1 lost the setter race to their anti-TR screen (Imprison + burst snipes). Game 2: lead Corviknight + Dragalge, bench Hatterene + Farigiraf. Corv presses Indeedee (IH 22-43%/hit; dead by ~T3, ending Imprison), Dragalge Protects its entry turn (it was the burst victim: rain Wave Crash rolled 84% + Hurricane). Setters enter only after Indeedee is gone, setter Protects its entry turn (streak resets - entry-turn Protect is 100%). Under TR: double-tap Gardevoir (Corv IH + Dragalge Sludge Wave) so sac-swap/Protect can't preserve it; Foul Play executes Basc; Pelipper is the slow boss only Corv can out-sustain - keep Corv >=60% entering endgames and never attack into MF+Hurricane coverage below ~50%.

reflections.summary: Won 1-0 in 13 turns. The Indeedee-F/Pelipper lead successfully established Psychic Terrain, rain, Tailwind, and Imprison, completely denying Hatterene's initial Trick Room and enabling Hurricane to remove Hatterene. The game became difficult after Indeedee and Basculegion were sacrificed; Dragalge resisted Wave Crash, and Farigiraf eventually set Trick Room. Gardevoir plus Pelipper still overcame the endgame, with Mystical Fire and repeated Hurricane finally removing Corviknight despite Roost, Mirror Armor, and a Hurricane miss.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the anti-Trick Room lead concept, but consider Archaludon over Basculegion into this opponent: Basculegion's Wave Crash was resisted by Dragalge and recoil plus Foul Play made it fragile, while rain-powered Electro Shot pressures Corviknight. Avoid exposing Mega Gardevoir to Corviknight's Iron Head unless Protect or a knockout is secured; use Pelipper's Wide Guard/Protect more deliberately against the physical endgame.

decisions.rationale: G2 skeleton: lead Corviknight+Dragalge (sponge Hyper Voice 20-28%, absorb Electro Shot 18-27% and one rain Wave Crash), bench Hatterene+Farigiraf for TR inversion. Mence benched (G-Mega Pixilate HV ~60-90% on it; they always bring Gardevoir). T1: Corv IH -> Indeedee + Dragalge Protect; kill Imprison tech early, then Farigiraf in first, TR once safe.

Use the established anti-Trick Room lead: Indeedee supplies Psychic Terrain and Imprison while Pelipper establishes rain. Bring Archaludon and Gardevoir to pressure the recurring Corviknight/Dragalge core without relying on Basculegion into Dragalge.

Same lead as G1: Pelipper+Indeedee. Corv IH -> Indeedee (22-43%, physical so Psychic Seed's +1 SpD is irrelevant; pressures the Imprison TR-block). Dragalge Protects its entry turn (100%) to safely absorb the T1-3 burst that killed Dragalge/Hatterene in G1; keeps it healthy as the Wave Crash absorber while rain is up.

Re-establish Imprison immediately to deny Trick Room from either revealed setter. Pelipper uses rain-boosted Hurricane into Dragalge for meaningful neutral pressure while preserving the anti-TR structure.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Indeedee (75%, Imprison active) is the TR-block linchpin: Corv Body Press hits it hardest (Def 172 as attack, est ~27-50% vs Bold defenses; +1 SpD irrelevant), Dragalge Sludge Wave spreads 43-86% onto Pelipper (removing Sash relevance, rain dies with Pelipper) + more Indeedee chip (combined likely leaves it 0-33%). Accept 0.5x self-chip on Corv (Roost heals it later). Risk: Pelipper WideGuard eats the spread — BP pressure remains.

Imprison is already active, so Indeedee can safely rotate into Archaludon, which resists Dragalge's Poison pressure and improves the board against Corviknight/Dragalge. Pelipper keeps immediate rain Hurricane pressure on Dragalge after its prior Protect.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Electro Shot = 81.9-117.1% into Corv (Magnet+rain instant fire) — switching. Farigiraf is the safest entry: ES 40.8-58.7%, Hurricane 31.5-46.9%, worst-case double-target 72.3-105.6% (rarely lethal); it then TRs T4 with Indeedee benched (Imprison dormant). Dragalge SW -> Pelipper is a guaranteed kill (43.1% min > 35%) if not Protected/WideGuarded — killing Pelipper ends rain, defanging Basculegion Wave Crash and future ES insta-fires.

Farigiraf passes (menu limited); Hatterene takes the free slot — it tanks ES at only 25-35.9% (-2 SpA) and T5 its terrain-boosted Psychic is a guaranteed kill on 35% Pelipper (64.7-127.4%, Sash can't save non-full HP) → rain dies, Electro Shot re-charges, Basc loses Swift Swim. Corv stays benched 100% (ES would still do 40-59% to it) as the G-Mega IH answer. T5: Psychic Pelipper + Farigiraf TR (Indeedee benched, Imprison dormant). Contingency: if they re-enter Indeedee (re-arms Imprison), delay TR and chip it with Corv BP on entry.

Draco Meteor is a guaranteed KO on Dragalge from its shown 68% across the damage range, while Pelipper Protects to avoid being removed by another spread attack. This also removes the main special-pressure threat and preserves Pelipper's Focus Sash insurance.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Hatterene)
decisions.rationale: Combo turn: Farigiraf TR (Imprison dormant — Indeedee benched; even if it re-enters later, Imprison can't erase an active TR) + Hatt Psychic -> Pelipper, a guaranteed kill (64.7-127.4% vs 35%, Sash can't save from 35%). Rain ends with Pelipper, de-fanging Electro Shot (re-charges) and Basc's Swift Swim. Intake this turn is safe: Draco is 0x on Hatt (Fairy), ES 25-36%, worst Farig case ~35%. T5+ under TR my whole side moves first.

Bring Indeedee back to restore active Imprison and prevent the newly revealed Hatterene/Farigiraf from establishing Trick Room. Archaludon targets Hatterene with super-effective Flash Cannon while Pelipper safely exits at 36%.

Flash Cannon = 55.1-82.1% vs Hatt's 53% — any targeted hit kills Hatt, so Protect (fresh 100%) blanks it while Farig Crunch -> Indeedee (2x, 32.8-66.2% vs 43%, ~60% kill; it has no Protect and can't dodge). If Indeedee survives on a sliver, Hatt's Psychic (or terrain removal) finishes T6. Hatt kept alive as the guaranteed Pelipper killer (Psychic ≥43% no-terrain) and backup TR setter; Corv 100% benched for the G-Mega/endgame. Rain expires end of T5 either way.

Trick Room is already active, so prioritize removing Hatterene while Indeedee uses Follow Me to redirect the likely Dark/Psychic single-target attacks away from Archaludon. A second Flash Cannon should finish Hatterene from 52% despite Archaludon's Special Attack drop.

Indeedee execute: Farig Crunch floor 32.8% > 10% — guaranteed kill, erasing Imprison/FollowMe/HH for good. Hatt (53%, dies to any Flash Cannon) exits for Corviknight — Corv is nearly untouchable without rain (Flash/Draco 0.5x ~8-15%; ES charge = telegraphed -1 SpA shot next turn). T7 under TR: Corv BP + Farig Foul Play both into Archaludon (29.4-50.9% + ~20-28% = dead ~60% now, guaranteed by T8). TR expires end of T8; plan TR re-set T9 if the 4th/Pelipper grind needs it.

Repeat the Hatterene removal attempt: its Protect is now on reduced success, and Flash Cannon is the strongest available direct pressure. Indeedee's 11% HP is expendable while Follow Me shields Archaludon from single-target attacks and enables the KO attempt.

Indeedee is fainted, so pass with Archaludon and bring in Gardevoir as the final pressure piece. Mega Gardevoir can threaten spread damage into Farigiraf while Archaludon remains the Steel pivot against Corviknight.

Double-tap Archaludon under TR before Gardevoir can matter: BP+Foul Play = 40.6-75.7% vs 55% (~55-60% kill; survivor ≤14.4% dies to BP floor T8 — always before an ES fires). Archaludon first because its only burst (charged ES 60-89% into Corv) can flip the game; -2 SpA makes everything else negligible. Farigiraf then Protects future HVs (39.9-55.4%/turn kills it in 2); T8 contingency: Corv BP-kill + Roost, or pure Roost if Archaludon already dead, before the no-TR G-Mega grind (Corv IH x2-3 + Roost loop).

Under Trick Room, protect Mega Gardevoir from Corviknight's super-effective Iron Head while Archaludon fires rain-independent Electro Shot pressure into Corviknight. This preserves Gardevoir through the remaining Trick Room turn and targets the immediate Steel threat.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Final TR turn: Corv IH -> G-Mega (48-96.5% → 3.5-52%; T10 IH+Foul ≈70% kill, T11 guaranteed at ≤44%). Farig Protects (fresh 100%) so it enters T9 at full HP for the TR re-set — worst-case Farig intake T9 (HV 39.9-55.4 + Hurr 31.5-46.9) is 71-102%, fatal only on double-max rolls. Corv absorbs whatever T8 hits come (worst 35-51% → 38-54%, fine). Under TR T10+: Hatt/Crav execute Pelipper (Psychic ≥43% vs 35%, IH grind backup), G-Mega dies T10-11.

decisions.rationale: Use Pelipper's Hurricane to pressure Farigiraf while Mega Gardevoir Protects through the final Trick Room turn, avoiding Corviknight's super-effective Iron Head. Gardevoir can attack safely once normal speed order returns.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Corv IH (48% floor) executes 17% G-Mega this turn despite moving second — Pelipper+G become their LAST mon. Farig re-sets TR (resolves after enemy attacks; Imprison dead) → T10-14 full inversion vs a lone 35% Pelipper: Corv IH 3-hit grind or Hatt Psychic execute, Pelipper can't out-damage Corv's Roost loop. Residual risk: Farig sniped by HV+Hurr double-max (~4%) — even then Corv wins 1v1 + Hatt Psychic finish.

Now out of Trick Room, focus both attacks on Corviknight: Mega Gardevoir's super-effective Mystical Fire and Pelipper's Hurricane can remove the Steel threat before another Iron Head. Leaving Corviknight alive is the immediate loss condition for the 17% Gardevoir.

Cleanup phase, 3v1 vs 35% Pelipper (their last mon). Corv exits (40%, preserves the Roost-loop insurance) for Hatt — it can't be OHKO'd from 53% (Hurricane max 56.4% but Sitrus heals mid-drop) and T11 under TR its Psychic (floor 43.1% > 25%) kills Pelipper before it moves. Farig Foul Play chips now (WideGuard can't block single-target). Contingency: Pelipper Protect streaks just delay the guaranteed Psychic to T12.
With only Pelipper remaining, continue targeting Corviknight at 39% with Hurricane for the best available chance to remove the Steel threat; no defensive or setup action can recover the position.

Hatt Psychic -> Pelipper: floor 43.1% > 22% remaining, 100% acc, TR means it resolves before Pelipper acts — guaranteed game-winning KO on their final Pokémon. Corv Roosts to 71% (insurance only; the game ends on the Psychic). WideGuard can't block single-target; nothing else can interfere.
Corviknight is now at 21%, within the demonstrated Hurricane damage range; attack it again before it can Roost. Pelipper has no viable alternative to preserve the game.

reflections.summary: WON G2 on T11, series 1-1. The TR-tempo plan executed end to end: Corv+Dragalge lead survived the Imprison+Hurricane screen; Indeedee was ground down (Crunch 2x) and killed T6 — its FollowMe was useless because I targeted it directly; when they sac-swapped Archaludon in, Corv was safely benched from every Electro Shot window (82-117% in rain would have OHKO'd it) and Archaludon died to a BP+Foul Play double-tap under TR while at -2 SpA. Gardevoir-Mega wasted T7-T8 on a Protect streak (2-stack fail) and died T9 to Iron Head (83% roll + execute) — I never ate a single Pixilate Hyper Voice. Pelipper's re-entry reset rain, but the T9 re-TR gave T10-14 inversion and Hatt's Psychic (43.1% floor) executed the 22% last mon. New verified data: Flash Cannon into Hatt is only 47% at -2 SpA but ~94% at full SpA; MF into Corv rolled 31% at 0-stage (vs G1's 60% read — treat as 30-60%); Psychic Terrain confirmed to boost my grounded Psychics x1.5 and NOT block Protect/TR; Imprison volatile confirmed cleared on switch-out; Steel immunity made Sludge Wave zero-cost to my Steel mons. Two blemishes: Dragalge died to Draco Meteor T3 (opened with SW instead of Protecting a fresh streak), and a T10 menu-index mixup between slots (benign, outcome equivalent). Zero decision errors, zero substitutions.
reflections.adjustment: Keep: the 4 (Corv+Dragalge+Hatt+Farig, bench Mence+Clawitzer), TR-tempo skeleton, Corv as the sole HV wall + G-Mega executioner (IH 48-96.5%, rolled 83%), re-TR the turn after expiry (setter survives ~102% worst intake). Change for G3: (1) Dragalge never open-attacks while Archaludon lives — Protect the fresh streak vs Draco (G2's only fatality); (2) kill Pelipper EARLY with Sludge Wave (min 43.1% executes its 35%) — ending rain permanently defangs Electro Shot and Swift Swim; (3) Corv Roosts at >=60% HP, never grinds to 21% again under Hurricane spam; (4) prepare for a possible Archaludon+Pelipper lead: rain ES = 82-117% OHKO on Corv, so Corv exits T1 and only re-enters rainless or post-Archaludon; (5) expect G-Mega to Mega+attack immediately this time — keep Farig/Hatt off-board vs HV (39.9-55.4%/turn each), only Corv tanks it; (6) verify slot-to-mon menu mapping every turn; (7) they read lethal attacks and Protect them — pair kill attempts in the same turn (SW+IH) so one read can't blank the turn.

reflections.summary: Lost Game 2 after successfully removing Dragalge but allowing Trick Room to go up once Indeedee was rotated out. The decisive strategic error was abandoning active Imprison: Farigiraf established Trick Room on turn 4, and later Hatterene/Farigiraf plus Corviknight overwhelmed the endgame. Archaludon also fell to Body Press while targeting Corviknight under Trick Room, and Mega Gardevoir was repeatedly exposed to Iron Head; Corviknight survived at 21%.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Indeedee active until both Trick Room setters are removed or clearly unable to act; switching it out forfeited the main control plan. Against Corviknight under Trick Room, prioritize Protecting Archaludon rather than attacking into a likely Body Press, and avoid consecutive Gardevoir Protects when Iron Head remains available. Preserve Gardevoir behind redirection or wait out Trick Room before committing it.

decisions.rationale: G3 decider. Opponent locked Pelipper/Indeedee/Archaludon/Gardevoir both games and led P+Ind 3 straight — bring the proven anti-rain/TR core: Corv+Dragalge lead (IH->Ind 22-43, Drag absorbs ES/Hurr, SW executes Pelipper), Hatt+Farig back (dual TR setters, Magic Bounce + Armor Tail). Bench Mence (dies to HV; anti-rain only if G-Mega gone) and Clawitzer (TR nuke, redundant vs this 4). Follows G3 plan: never field Corv while rain+Arch coexist.

Lead Indeedee-F/Pelipper to establish Psychic Terrain and rain while Imprison immediately denies the recurring Trick Room core; bring Archaludon for rain-boosted Electro Shot and Gardevoir for decisive spread pressure, preserving the anti-TR and anti-Corviknight plan.

Keep Indeedee active and Imprison to deny either hidden Trick Room user if switched in; Pelipper uses rain-accurate Hurricane into Dragalge for neutral chip, the more vulnerable and recurring target, while staying faster than Corviknight.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: T2 script: BP->Ind slot dominates both branches (stay: 23.2-46.2, plus SW->Ind 20.3-38.6 can kill 77% Ind outright; swap: 29.4-50.9 on Archaludon entry, 2x, vs IH's 0.5x). Dragalge SW puts Pelipper at 14-57%, setting a guaranteed T3 SW execute that I'll pair with BP. G2 T2 evidence says they Protect the swap-in rather than insta-ES, so Corv survives to keep pressure.

Imprison is already active, so use Indeedee’s priority Helping Hand to maximize Pelipper’s rain Hurricane into Dragalge; Dragalge’s Protect is already weakened after turn 1, making this the best chance to force meaningful damage while retaining Trick Room denial.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Double-kill turn: BP->Ind is guaranteed (23.2-46.2 vs 20%) and SW executes both Pelipper (min 43.1 vs 35, kills rain) and Ind (min 20.3 vs 20). If they Protect the read, Ind still dies to BP and Pelipper is set for a T4 re-execute against a broken Protect streak. BP also stays 2x into an Archaludon swap.

Indeedee is at 21% and has done its Imprison job; switch it to the Steel-resistant Archaludon to preserve the position and absorb Sludge Wave, while Pelipper Protects at 36% to avoid being worn down. This retains Pelipper and brings Archaludon safely against both revealed foes.

Denial turn: Archaludon acts first and their G2 script is Draco->Dragalge (kills 58% SW carrier before it fires) — Drag Protect on a fresh streak blocks it plus Hurr. Corviknight exits the rain+Arch ES zone (81.9-117.1 coin-flip OHKO) into Farigiraf, the only healthy Arch-special absorber. Concede tempo now to convert T5: Farig TR resolves -7 first, Drag fires SW before Arch/Pel in inverted order, Pelipper (and any Ind re-entry) dies, rain expires, and a rainless T6 with TR up lets Corv re-enter for the endgame.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Draco Meteor is a guaranteed KO on Dragalge from 58%, removing the immediate rain-resistant threat. Pelipper Protects to avoid Sludge Wave and preserve a rain setter; even if Corviknight’s Body Press removes Archaludon afterward, this trades Archaludon for Dragalge while retaining Pelipper and the backline.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Dragalge)
decisions.rationale: Tool data flipped the plan: their Draco was Protect-blocked, so Archaludon kept 0 SpA — Draco (93.5-136.4) kills 64% Dragalge guaranteed, and rain-ES still coin-flips Corviknight. So SW is off the table this turn; instead Dragalge exits into Hatterene as a sac-bait (their ES kills it; a Draco into Hatt is Fairy-immune and wasted), while Farigiraf sets TR for a rainless, inverted T6 where fresh Corviknight BPs Archaludon to 1-23% and kills it T7 before it ever acts under TR. Pelipper (35%) and Indeedee (20%) both fall to Drag-first SW once Arch is gone.

Dragalge has now spent Protect twice and remains the key threat; double-target it with Draco Meteor plus rain Hurricane to secure its removal before it can attack again. This also pressures through the weakened consecutive-Protect odds, accepting that Farigiraf may establish Trick Room afterward.

The sim shows Archaludon self-dropped to -2 SpA even on the blocked/immune Dracos — its burst is halved, so Corviknight can safely enter now that rain is gone. Farigiraf benches itself (the only body Draco still threatens hard), Corv comes in fresh as the BP finisher, and Hatterene — guaranteed first under TR — chips Archaludon into double-tap kill range for T7, where BP + second Psychic kill it before it acts. Pelipper's Psychic execute (50.3-98.5 vs 35%) waits behind its decaying Protect chain.

Replacement prompt: Dragalge enters over Farigiraf because T7 is a free turn for it — Archaludon (23%) is guaranteed dead to Corv's Body Press (min 29.4) before Arch ever moves under TR, removing Drag's only killer. That lets Drag SW-execute Pelipper immediately (67% vs 33% Protect chain). Farigiraf stays banked as the sole Trick Room re-setter for the post-T9 G-Mega war, where Drag's SW (52.6-95.1) plus Corv's Iron Head kill 68-HP G-Mega in one focused round.

Under Trick Room, Hatterene acts first and is the immediate threat to the fragile Pelipper. Archaludon’s Flash Cannon is a guaranteed KO from Hatterene’s 51%, while Pelipper Protects to survive Hatterene’s priority-under-TR attack and preserve the remaining rain utility.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Guaranteed Archaludon kill: BP min 29.4 covers its 23%, and under TR Corv moves before Arch's slot resolves. Dragalge's SW hits Pelipper for a 67% execute while Corv is Steel-immune to the self-spread. If they retreat Arch for G-Mega, T8's IH+SW (100.7 min) still one-rounds fresh G-Mega before it acts.

Dragalge remains at 64% and is the only active target vulnerable to Archaludon’s guaranteed super-effective Draco Meteor; pair it with Hurricane to maximize removal before its Sludge Wave. Archaludon may be lost to Corviknight under Trick Room, but eliminating Dragalge leaves the healthier Gardevoir/Indeedee endgame against Corviknight and Farigiraf.

Bring the healthy Gardevoir alongside the remaining Indeedee-F. Gardevoir is the only meaningful endgame attacker into Corviknight/Dragalge, while Indeedee’s entry restores Psychic Terrain and preserves the possibility of reversing Trick Room or using redirection next turn.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Close-out sequencing: Drag's SW (unredirectable spread) fires first under TR, killing 20% Indeedee outright and dropping Gardevoir to ≤47.4%; Corv's Iron Head (min 48.1) then kills G before its action — and a dead Indeedee means FollowMe can never redirect the IH. All four foes die by T8-T9 with only G's Protect as a one-turn delay.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Gardevoir)
decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve and Protect Gardevoir through the remaining Trick Room turn, while Indeedee uses Trick Room to reverse the field for next turn. This preserves the full-health win condition from Dragalge’s super-effective Sludge Wave and enables Gardevoir to attack first afterward.

selection: Sludge Wave (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Double-tap kill on a 33% Protect chain: SW (unredirectable, self-free on Steel Corv) drops G-Mega to ≤47.4%, Iron Head (min 48.1) finishes before G's 120-152 Speed ever comes up under TR. If G Protects, Corv is still at 100% with Roost discipline for the T10 fight. This closes the series at 2-1 if it lands.

With Indeedee gone, use Mega Gardevoir’s Psychic Terrain-boosted Expanding Force into Dragalge, the super-effective target and main source of lethal Sludge Wave pressure. This is the best immediate route to a one-Pokémon endgame versus Corviknight.

reflections.summary: SERIES WON 2-1 (G1 L, G2 W, G3 W). G3 decider: won T9 with 0 decision errors; my only loss was Hatterene. Every between-game adjustment from G2's review paid off. (1) The Corv+Drag lead neutralized their 4th consecutive P+Ind lead — T1 Protect ate the Hurricane and BP/IH/SW chipped all three leads into execute range. (2) I exploited their dominant habit — Protecting lethal reads — by pairing kill attempts and re-executing next turn against decaying Protect streaks: Pelipper's T4 Protect failed on schedule and T7 it died before its action resolved. (3) The pivotal denial sequence: their T3 sac-swap to Archaludon + T4 Draco threat triggered T4 Drag fresh-streak Protect (blocking the exact Draco→Drag kill script that lost Drag in G2) and the Corv rain-exit law, then T5 Farig TR'd as rain expired. (4) The damage tool revealed Archaludon at -2 SpA — this sim applies Draco's self-drop even on blocked/immune Dracos — which re-valued Arch as defanged and freed Corviknight to play the endgame at 100% HP. T6 Hatt's Psychic chip cost it to a high Flash roll despite the -2 SpA read (only loss, accepted sac-bait variance). T7-T9 closed it: SW crit-killed Pelipper while BP killed Archaludon the same turn; T8 SW (unredirectable spread) killed Indeedee through the FollowMe threat and exposed G-Mega; T9 SW+Iron Head killed G-Mega before it EVER attacked all game (1 entry-Protect, 0 offensive actions). End state: Corv untouched at 100%, Drag 76%, Farig never damaged. G1 was lost to my Corv tank misread (Mystical Fire 2x band 30-60% at 0-stage, read as survivable); G2 fixed it with the TR cycle; G3 ran the same rain/TR script with the Draco-drop mechanic discovery on top. Core win engine: a fully telegraphed draft exploited with tempo denial, Protect-streak math and TR inversion; one SW crit helped but wasn't load-bearing — Pel was SW-executable T8 regardless.
reflections.adjustment: Vs this opponent/archetype in a future series: keep the G3 script (repeatable, 0 errors) with three tweaks: (1) never field Hatterene vs a live Archaludon below ~65% HP even at -2 SpA — Flash variance killed my only G3 loss and its Psychic chip isn't worth the risk; use Corv entry or Farig Protect instead; (2) manage the TR re-set explicitly — position Farig (or keep Hatt alive) to re-set the turn after expiry; G3 ended before the clock mattered, but longer games need a T10+ plan; (3) G-Mega's entry-turn Protect is a habit, not variance — bank the focused double-tap (SW+IH, 100.7 min vs 68 HP) for the turn AFTER entry and it always lands. Bank the sim mechanic league-wide: Draco self-drops even when blocked/immune, so any opposing Archaludon defangs itself after its first Draco regardless of my answers — absorbing one Draco (Protect or Fairy-immune bait) buys a -2 SpA nuke and frees my Steel walls. Draft note: Mence+Clawitzer were correctly benched all series vs rain+TR spam — don't force them into this archetype; save them for weeks where the opponent lacks a Pixilate spread or the roster needs a nuke.

reflections.summary: Lost game 3 and the series 1-2 primarily because I abandoned the active Imprison plan on turn 3, switching Indeedee out for Archaludon at 21%. Farigiraf then entered and established Trick Room, recreating the opponent’s proven winning structure. Once Trick Room was active, Archaludon was exposed to Corviknight Body Press, Pelipper was eventually lost to Sludge Wave, and Mega Gardevoir could not survive Dragalge plus Iron Head. The between-game adjustment helped early—Imprison denied Trick Room and Archaludon pressured Dragalge—but switching Indeedee backfired and gave up the central win condition.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, keep Indeedee active with Imprison even at low HP until both Trick Room users are removed; do not prioritize preserving it over denial. After Trick Room begins, Protect Archaludon from Body Press rather than accepting a trade, and avoid exposing Gardevoir to Corviknight Iron Head. Track Dragalge’s repeated Protect and switch patterns instead of committing Draco Meteor into a likely protected or newly switched slot. Consider bringing Qwilfish or Basculegion over the least useful slot if they provide a safer post-Trick Room endgame.

decisions.rationale: G1 bring Rilla+Clef+DN+Dirge vs Metagross/Mamo core. Lead Rilla/Clef for T1 Fake Out (Talon to break Gale Wings, else Metagross/Primarina) plus Follow Me if Ice Shard/Ice Punch/Mash aims at a frail target; terrain cuts Mamo EQ. DN and Dirge back: mega DN only with Follow Me vs Ice or when no Ice is in; Dirge Unaware walls Mash, Brave Bird, and Intimidate and Torch Songs Steels. Leave Greninja/Sneasler; Dirge already walls both Fires and Metagross. Thick Fat means Fire is not the Mamo KO—Wood Hammer is. Watch Rotom Blizzard (spread, Follow Me does not save DN).

Bring Metagross/Primarina/Talonflame/Arcanine; lead Metagross+Primarina, back Talonflame+Arcanine. Primarina is the Dragonite/Greninja/Skeledirge wall (immune Dragon; resists Fire/Water/Dark/Ice) with 4x Ice Beam; Metagross is the Sneasler/Clefable answer (immune Poison, resists Fighting, 4x Zen Headbutt, Meteor Mash 2x Fairy) and a second 4x Ice move (Ice Punch) to break Dragonite's Multiscale. Talonflame (195) outspeeds every foe including Greninja (156-191) and Sneasler (154-189) and KOs Rillaboom (Flare Blitz 2x) or Greninja (Brave Bird). Arcanine brings Intimidate to blunt Sneasler/Rillaboom, Will-O-Wisp, and ExtremeSpeed priority to finish Focus-Sash Sneasler. Both leads are immune/resistant to the opponent's key STABs so the lead survives Fake Out turns.

Fake Out Mega Gross so Tough Claws Mash (87–123% into Clef) never lands; Follow Me then takes Primarina’s only action. Primarina cannot KO Clef (Hydro 45–64, Moonblast 38–55, Ice Beam 24–35) and Ice Beam on Rilla (63–89) is the line we dodge so Rilla stays full for T2 Wood Hammer. Do not WH/Glide Primarina T1: Mash still moves first and KO-ranges Clef via Follow Me, and open sheets make Primarina Protect likely. No Dirge switch (Hydro 97–140% KO range). No DN switch (Ice Punch+Ice Beam breaks Multiscale).

Opponent led a support pair (Rillaboom + Clefable), so Clefable will likely Follow Me (+2) and Rillaboom will Fake Out or Wood Hammer Primarina. Answer: Mega Evolve Metagross for Tough Claws and Meteor Mash the redirector itself (Steel 2x vs Fairy, Tough Claws+STAB ~4x effective on Clefable's bulk = guaranteed KO), which removes their Follow Me shield for Dragonite and cannot be redirected since Clefable IS the target. Primarina Protects: Protect is +4 priority, so it beats Rillaboom's Fake Out (+3) and blanks a Helping Hand-boosted Wood Hammer (2x) that would otherwise OHKO it. Worst case (Fake Out on Metagross) I lose only a low-damage 0.5x hit and keep full HP on both.

WH Primarina is a guaranteed OHKO if it stays (144–276%); Glide/HH Glide are not (67–129 / 99.5–191). Clef must Protect—Follow Me into live Mash is 87–123% KO range. This also beats T1 Follow Me read (Mash Clef into Protect) and KOs Mamo if they pivot there. Do not switch Clef to Dirge: Primarina Hydro into that slot is 97–140% and they have no reason to Hydro Clef. Accept the double-Rilla punish (Ice Punch+Ice Beam) as a Rilla-for-Primarina trade; if they pivot Talon/Arcanine, Clef lives and we learn the back. Recoil is 33% of Primarina HP lost (~25% of Rilla) so Rilla lives a single Gross hit plus WH.

Turn 1 was Rillaboom Fake Out on Metagross + Clefable Follow Me; Grassy Terrain heals 1/16 so all four actives are effectively back to full. Clefable will almost certainly Follow Me again (its job) or Protect to block Meteor Mash. Meteor Mash into Clefable cannot be redirected (Clefable IS the redirector) and is a clean Tough Claws+STAB 2x KO on Bold Clefable (~330 dmg vs ~177 HP), so I remove their Follow Me shield before Dragonite arrives. Primarina must NOT stay in: Rillaboom's Wood Hammer is 2x and a guaranteed OHKO on Primarina's 94 Def, and a second consecutive Protect has a heavily reduced success rate, so Protection is not reliable. Switching to Talonflame eats any Grass attack at 0.25x, gains the fastest mon on the field, and sets up a Brave Bird (2x, ~237 vs ~205 HP, beats Sitrus) KO on Rillaboom next turn.

Talon 68% so Gale Wings is off; BB Rilla is still 69–106% KO range and Mash Clef is still 87–123%. Clef consecutive Protect is 1/3, Follow Me is suicide, Moonblast does not KO Talon. Protect Rilla beats the likely T2-Protect punish (BB/Ice Punch/Mash into Rilla) and U-turn-into-Protect keeps Talon stuck. Clef → Dirge punishes Mash-Clef retry (Mash 24–33 into Dirge) and lives BB (33–51). Do not double-switch DN onto Rilla slot: Ice Punch 69–98 Multiscale + BB KO-ranges DN if they double the Grass. Keep Rilla on field so WH is live vs Primarina if they pivot later. Dirge is the Gross+Talon wall; Clef stays in back for Follow Me + DN.

Clefable burned its Protect last turn (next use reduced success), so its most likely move is Follow Me again. Meteor Mash into Clefable cannot be redirected (Clefable IS the redirector) and is a guaranteed 2x Tough Claws KO, so Clefable dies in every branch except the ~1/3 Protect. Brave Bird into Rillaboom is the KO move (~237 dmg > ~205 HP + Sitrus), and note Talonflame is at 68% so Gale Wings priority is OFF - but at 195 Speed it still moves before both foes except Rillaboom's Grassy Glide (+1, only ~30 dmg at 0.25x). Branch analysis: no Follow Me -> Rillaboom dies to Brave Bird and Clefable to Meteor Mash (double KO); Clefable Follow Me -> Talonflame's Brave Bird is redirected onto Clefable (~67%) and Metagross finishes it with Meteor Mash, killing the shield before Dragonite arrives; Clefable Protects -> Meteor Mash is blanked but Brave Bird lands on Rillaboom and KOs it; Clefable switched out to Dragonite -> Meteor Mash chips Dragonite through Multiscale (~17%) and Brave Bird still KOs Rillaboom, setting up an Ice Punch KO next turn. Recoil from Brave Bird is accepted: the value of removing Rillaboom (which 2x OHKOs Primarina) is high.

Rilla cannot stay (BB 69–106% KO) and consecutive Protect is 1/3. Do not switch DN: it gets no move this turn, BB 21–33% breaks Multiscale, then Ice Punch/BB next turn KOs. They have split BB-slot-a / Mash-slot-b twice; Clef on slot a lives BB 30–47 and Ice Punch 24–34 and even BB+Ice Punch 54–81. Clef dies only to Mash on slot a (they have mashed slot b both attacks). Dirge stays and Torch Songs Gross 55–97 plus SpA boost (Shadow Ball same damage, no boost); another Mash/Zen from 81% does not KO Dirge. Next turn Clef can 100% Protect while +1 Torch Song finishes Gross. Keep DN in back for a Follow Me send later.

Dirge died to BB+Zen on slot b; they doubled the Unaware wall. Send DN beside Clef (the Follow Me partner) so T5 we can Mega and Fire Blast Gross (60–106%). Rilla into slot b is weak to another BB+Ice Punch double and does not pressure Gross. Fake Out on a Rilla re-entry is tempting but delays the only remaining Gross answer. Clef Pass. Next turn: Follow Me or Protect Clef; never leave DN on Ice Punch without redirection. Talon 48% Gale Wings still off.

Turn 3 revealed their 4th-game context: Clefable was switched out for Skeledirge and Rillaboom used Protect, so both are still alive and Clefable's Protect counter was reset by switching. Skeledirge is the single biggest threat to my win condition (Torch Song and Shadow Ball are both 2x on Mega Metagross, ~68% each, plus Slack Off/Leftovers/Unaware make it hard to remove later). Zen Headbutt (neutral, ~127) plus Talonflame's Brave Bird (~108) totals ~235 vs Skeledirge's ~162 current HP - a clean KO. Ordering is safe: Talonflame (195) acts first, Metagross (132) still outspeeds Skeledirge (86-118), so Skeledirge is removed before it can Torch Song or Slack Off. This leaves Metagross at 100%, which matters most because their unrevealed 4th mon is one of Sneasler/Dragonite/Greninja and Metagross is my answer to all three (4x Zen Headbutt on Sneasler, Ice Punch on Dragonite, resists Greninja's Water/Dark coming off a 2x weakness being avoided... Dark Pulse IS 2x but Metagross at full HP survives). The recoil cost (~36) plus at most one Grassy Glide (~30 at 0.25x) leaves Talonflame around 25-45%, an acceptable price. Also switching is fully punished by this pair: Zen Headbutt 4x KOs a switched-in Sneasler after Focus Sash, and Brave Bird KOs Greninja.

They doubled slot b (Dirge) last turn; DN is now slot b so Ice Punch+BB is the KO line. Follow Me sends Ice Punch (24–34) + BB (30–47) to Clef (54–81, lives) and DN Fire Blasts with Multiscale intact. Mash Clef still KOs Clef either way; Protect Clef loses DN to the slot-b double. HH Fire Blast is 89–157 still not a guaranteed OHKO and lets Ice Punch hit DN. Hurricane Talon is a 70% acc KO on 48% but leaves Gross 100% with Ice Punch. Mega immediately, Fire Blast Gross (85% acc, 60–106%). ES does not KO Talon.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Their 4th is Dragonite (Sneasler/Greninja not brought); Clefable + Dragonite are active with Rillaboom benched. This turn is about trading securely rather than gambling on the double-Ice KO. Meteor Mash into Clefable is a guaranteed 2x Tough Claws KO whenever Clefable does not Protect, and crucially it still lands if the opponent's read is "they will double Dragonite" (Follow Me or Dragonite Protect): Follow Me is useless against a move already aimed at Clefable, so Clefable dies either way and their shield for Dragonite is gone. Brave Bird into Dragonite chips through Multiscale (~54) so Dragonite is left at ~71% with Multiscale BROKEN, which means next turn a single Metagross Ice Punch (4x, ~327 full) KOs it outright. Talonflame is faster (195) than even Mega Dragonite (max 152), and Dragonite's only fast move is ExtremeSpeed (+2) which does ~50, so the chip is safe to attempt. Choice of Brave Bird over Flare Blitz: Flying is 1x on Dragon/Flying (~54 through Multiscale) while Flare Blitz is 0.5x (~27). Losing Talonflame is affordable - Rillaboom is the only mon left that punishes it, and Primarina/Arcanine are healthy in back.

+1 Ice Punch is 88–125% into Multiscale DN and 83–117% into Rilla—Gross must not get an attack. Fake Out Gross flinches Ice Punch (Protect Gross also means no Ice Punch). Talon outspeeds Fire Blast/Hurricane so those cannot stop BB; only ES (+2) or Fake Out can. ES Talon is 17–33% vs 19% (KO most rolls, 100% acc) before BB. Fire Blast Talon is a guaranteed KO on hit but Talon BBs first and 15% miss. Fake Out Talon + Fire Blast Gross loses DN if Gross is 153–162 Spe and Ice Punches. Fake Out Gross + ES Talon: Gross flinches, Talon likely dies, Multiscale intact. If ES low-rolls, BB DN is only 18–29% Multi. Next turn WH/Fire Blast the 22% Gross.

Their last two mons are Rillaboom + Dragonite (Clefable and Skeledirge are gone, and they have no bench to switch into), so every branch is Protect-or-attack. My two actives are nearly dead (Metagross 22%, Talonflame 19%) and both die to either foe's move, so I optimize positioning instead of gambling. Ice Punch is still the single highest-value click: 4x through Multiscale = 164, dropping Dragonite to ~11% with Multiscale broken, which Arcanine's ExtremeSpeed (+2, ~32) then finishes without needing Primarina. Switching Talonflame out to Arcanine gains three things even in the bad branch: Intimidate weakens Dragonite's ExtremeSpeed and Rillaboom's physical attacks by 25% (Grassy Glide on a 19% Talonflame was a guaranteed KO at 0.25x), a fresh 197 HP body enters instead of a 29 HP one, and Talonflame survives on the bench so it can still be the sacrifice body later - keeping Primarina (my Dragonite wall) safely benched until Rillaboom is dead, since Wood Hammer 2x OHKOs Primarina. If instead they were going to blank me with a double Protect, this line still makes progress (Arcanine in + Intimidate) whereas attacking with both would achieve nothing. Master plan from here: kill Rillaboom with Arcanine's Flare Blitz / Talonflame Brave Bird / Metagross Meteor Mash (+1 Atk = ~233, OHKO through Sitrus), then Arcanine ExtremeSpeed (breaks Multiscale) + Primarina Ice Beam (214) KOs Dragonite.

+1 Ice Punch still 88–125% into Multiscale DN and 83–117% into Rilla; Flare Blitz is 80–118% into Rilla. Only Fire Blast guaranteed-KOs 24% Gross (WH -1 Atk is 15–26 vs 24, not reliable). DN 152 vs Gross 130–162 is a speed gamble: if we outspeed, Fire Blast KOs before Ice Punch and Rilla Protect covers Blitz/ES/WoW. If they Ice Punch Rilla, Protect eats it and Fire Blast still KOs Gross. Protect DN fails to kill Gross so Ice Punch remains next turn. Hurricane Gross is 23–39 vs 24% and 70% acc. Intimidate does not affect Fire Blast. Rilla Protect is 100% (last Protect T3). 4th is Arcanine; Mamo/Rotom not brought.

Intimidate is now on both foes (-1 Atk), Arcanine is at 91%, and the board is Metagross 25% / Arcanine 91% vs Rillaboom 100% (Sitrus, fresh Protect) + Dragonite-Mega 100% (Multiscale, Protect unused). If Rillaboom dies, Primarina can finally come in safely and Arcanine ExtremeSpeed (~32, priority +2) + Primarina Ice Beam (214) KOs a full-health Multiscale Dragonite in one turn, so killing Rillaboom is the win condition. Metagross is a lost cause (it dies to Fire Blast/Hurricane/Wood Hammer and Dragonite is faster), so it is spent on the highest-value click: Ice Punch, 4x for 164 through Multiscale, which drops Dragonite to ~11% with Multiscale broken and makes it die to a single ExtremeSpeed. Arcanine's Flare Blitz (~262 vs 205 HP) OHKOs Rillaboom through Sitrus even if they Protect Dragonite, which is the read I expect them to make against the obvious Ice Punch + ExtremeSpeed double-up on Dragonite. The two attacks target different foes, so a single Protect only blanks one of them: Dragonite Protect still leaves Rillaboom dead; Rillaboom Protect still leaves the Ice Punch free to land (Metagross survives Grassy Glide at 0.5x ~23). Accepting the Flare Blitz recoil (~87) is fine because once Rillaboom is gone my 3 remaining mons beat Dragonite alone.

Metagross is gone and Rillaboom Protected my Flare Blitz, so the board is Arcanine 97% + a replacement vs Rillaboom 100% (Sitrus, -1 Atk, Protect now used twice so its next use is unreliable) + Dragonite-Mega 100% (Multiscale intact, -1 Atk). I must send Talonflame, not Primarina: Rillaboom is still alive and its Wood Hammer (2x, ~228 even at -1 Atk) is a clean OHKO on Primarina, so exposing her now would just hand them my Dragonite wall for free. Talonflame is the perfect sacrifice body - at 19% it is expected to die anyway, and it can either chip Dragonite with Brave Bird (~54, breaking Multiscale) or trade Brave Bird (~237) into Rillaboom if they misplay. Next turn Arcanine's Flare Blitz (~262) OHKOs Rillaboom through Sitrus, and Arcanine's ExtremeSpeed (~32, priority +2) plus Primarina's Ice Beam (214) KOs a full-health Multiscale Dragonite in a single turn once Rillaboom is gone; if Talonflame faints on that turn I get Primarina in for free at the end of it. Primarina also survives one Dragonite hit (Hurricane ~100 of 187), so she only needs one clean turn in the endgame.

decisions.rationale: They sent 19% Talon over Primarina to double Rilla with Arcanine Blitz (80–118%) + BB (69–106%). Rilla Protect is 1/3 but it is the only save; it blocks both if it hits. ES Talon is only 12–23% vs 19% with -1 Atk (not a KO). Fire Blast Talon is a guaranteed KO on 85% acc after they attack; if they BB Rilla, DN is untouched and still KOs Talon. Glide does not KO. If Protect fails we lose Rilla but Talon still dies and DN is 100% Multi vs Arcanine+Prim. If they U-turn, Fire Blast hits Primarina—accepted. Do not Protect DN (Rilla then dies for sure).

Arcanine is the only mon that can reliably kill Rillaboom: it survives everything the pair can do (Fire Blast 0.5x ~70, Wood Hammer 0.5x ~60, ExtremeSpeed ~37 on 191 HP), so it always gets Flare Blitz off - and Flare Blitz (~262) OHKOs Rillaboom through Sitrus unless Rillaboom tries its third Protect (reduced success after two uses). Talonflame is sent at Dragonite-Mega instead of doubling on Rillaboom for three reasons: (1) targeting two different foes is the best hedge, since a single Protect only blanks one of my two attacks; (2) Brave Bird (~54 through Multiscale) BREAKS Multiscale, which is worth more than any chip on Rillaboom - with Multiscale gone, Arcanine's ExtremeSpeed (~32) plus Primarina's Ice Beam (214) KOs a full-health Dragonite in one turn; (3) I do NOT want to rely on Talonflame for the Rillaboom kill, because Dragonite's ExtremeSpeed (+2, faster than Arcanine) KOs 19% Talonflame before it can move. If Talonflame dies (whether to ExtremeSpeed before acting or to Brave Bird recoil after chipping), Primarina comes in at the END of the turn, which is exactly what I want: she then faces no Grass attack and is active and able to act alongside Arcanine's ExtremeSpeed for the one-turn KO. Primarina survives a single Dragonite hit (Hurricane ~100 of 187), so she only needs that one clean turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Order is safe either way: ExtremeSpeed resolves first, and even if Dragonite moves before Primarina it cannot remove her - Fire Blast is 0.5x (~70 of 187) and Hurricane is ~100, leaving her alive to fire the Ice Beam. If Dragonite Protects this turn, the only cost is one turn, since its Protect counter is then consumed (a repeat use has reduced success) and Primarina still wins the following turn.

reflections.summary: Won game 1 (1-0) with 0 decision errors. Their 4 was Rillaboom + Clefable + Skeledirge + Dragonite (Sneasler and Greninja not brought), led Rillaboom + Clefable. My four (Mega Metagross, Primarina, Talonflame, Arcanine) were exactly right. Key winning decisions: (1) turn 1 Primarina Protected instead of attacking, blanking Fake Out and a possible Helping-Hand-boosted Wood Hammer; (2) turn 2 I switched Primarina out rather than leave it in Rillaboom's Wood Hammer range (a guaranteed 2x OHKO on its 94 Def) and absorbed Grass with Talonflame at 0.25x, while gaining a free turn; (3) I correctly valued Clefable as the Follow Me shield and removed it with Meteor Mash, then Skeledirge (the 2x Torch Song/Shadow Ball threat to Metagross) with Brave Bird chip + Zen Headbutt; (4) Arcanine's Intimidate + Flare Blitz removed Rillaboom through Sitrus; (5) I recognized Multiscale only halves the FIRST hit, so Brave Bird/ExtremeSpeed chip before a 4x Ice move; (6) I kept re-clicking Ice Beam + ExtremeSpeed through Dragonite's Protect stall - it failed on the third consecutive attempt and Primarina finished it. Talonflame and Metagross were spent as intended, and Primarina entered only after Rillaboom was dead, so she never faced a Grass attack.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same core and the same lead for game 2: Metagross + Primarina in front, Talonflame + Arcanine in back. The only real adjustment is anticipating that they will swap the two support mons for speed: Clefable + Skeledirge lost as a slow shell, so Sneasler (Focus Sash/Unburden, Fake Out, Close Combat/Dire Claw) and/or Greninja (Life Orb Protean) are the likely changes. Do not change my own team - Metagross is immune to Dire Claw and resists Close Combat and is 4x on Sneasler, Talonflame (195) outspeeds Greninja (max 191) and OHKOs it with Brave Bird. The one execution change: against Sneasler, chip it before committing to a KO (Focus Sash leaves it at 1 HP and Unburden doubles its speed), and use Arcanine's ExtremeSpeed as the finisher. Everything else - never exposing Primarina while a Grass attacker or unrevealed Fake Out mon is active, and breaking Multiscale before the Ice Beam - carries over.
