decisions.rationale: G2 bring Rilla+Greninja+Clef+DN, sit Dirge/Sneasler. G1 Dirge was doubled by Talon BB + Gross Zen before Torch Song; Greninja is the Talon/Arcanine/Mamo answer and Dark Pulses Gross. Lead Rilla+Gren: Grassy Surge, Fake Out Gross (stop Mash/Ice Punch) or Talon (break Gale Wings); Hydro Talon/Arcanine/Mamo or Dark Pulse Gross. Clef+DN in back for HH/Protect Blast and Follow Me vs Ice Shard/Blizzard—never Follow Me into live Mash. WH Prim/Mamo. Mega DN on first send.

Bring the proven winning four (Mega Metagross, Arcanine, Primarina, Talonflame). Team preview is simultaneous so I can't react to their lead; rather than commit fragile Primarina to a likely Rillaboom lead (2x Wood Hammer/Grassy Glide KOs it, losing my Dragonite answer), I lead Mega Metagross + Arcanine. Metagross is bulky and immune/resistant to their fast threats (immune Poison/Dire Claw, resists CC/Grass), while Arcanine's turn-1 Intimidate blunts Rillaboom/Sneasler physical damage and its ExtremeSpeed chips to break Multiscale/Sash. Keep Primarina and Talonflame in back: Primarina enters late only after Grass attackers leave and is the Ice Beam 4x answer to Dragonite; Talonflame (195 Spe) stays fresh as the Greninja/Sneasler revenge killer.

T1 Fake Out Gross + Hydro Arcanine. Fake Out stops Mash/Ice Punch so they cannot double Rilla (Ice Punch 55-79% + Blitz 80-118% KO). Greninja 191 outspeeds Arcanine and Mega Gross; LO Hydro is 96-181% into Arcanine (even bulky lives only low rolls) so a hit usually KOs before Blitz. 80% accuracy is the risk; if it hits we get a free Arcanine KO and a flinch. Do not Fake Out Arcanine — that gives Gross a free Ice Punch and wastes the perfect turn. Wood Hammer is 22-41% into Fire after Intimidate. Never waste Fake Out on Protect/switch.

Focus-fire Rillaboom. Greninja's Hydro Pump is a guaranteed OHKO on Arcanine, so Arcanine should spend its likely-final action on the biggest hit: Flare Blitz (82-149%, real KO chance) into Rillaboom. Mega Metagross adds Ice Punch (54-98%, best option into Rillaboom; Meteor Mash only 49-88% and less accurate). If Rillaboom Fake Outs one of mine, the other's attack still lands, and combined damage (even through Sitrus) should remove the terrain setter. Mega Evolution is strictly better here (Tough Claws boosts Ice Punch; survives Greninja's Dark Pulse at 60-89% instead of possible OHKO). Rillaboom's own attacks are 0.5x into both my actives, so my mons are safe from it this turn.

Bring Talonflame, not Primarina. Greninja is active and my remaining pair (Metagross + Primarina) has no way to break it — Metagross's moves are 0.5x/0x into it and Primarina's Moonblast/Ice Beam/Hydro Pump are only 1x/0.5x, while Greninja 2x Dark Pulses Metagross. Talonflame (195 Spe) outspeeds Greninja's max 191 and threatens a Brave Bird OHKO (STAB + Sharp Beak), and Gale Wings gives it priority at full HP. Rillaboom cannot punish Talonflame (Grass is 0.5x into Fire/Flying, and its Fake Out is used up). Primarina stays in back as the Dragonite answer and can enter later once the Grass attacker is gone.

Rilla Protect + Hydro Talon. Full-HP Gale Wings BB is +1 so it beats Hydro; BB Rilla is 69-106% and with Ice Punch/Mash is a KO, and G1 they BB'd Rilla. Protect is 100% this turn. LO Hydro is 114-219% OHKO on Talon (80% acc) after BB. Do not switch Clef into live Mash (87-123% KO) or DN into Ice Punch (69-98% even Multiscale). Do not Dark Pulse Gross while Talon still has Gale Wings. If they BB Greninja instead, high roll can KO from 97%; still the right line vs their G1 targeting. Never both-Protect (Talon keeps Gale Wings if BB hits Protect with no recoil).

Remove Greninja: Talonflame outspeeds (195>191) and Gale Wings gives Brave Bird priority at full HP, so it can KO Greninja before Greninja's Hydro Pump (which is a guaranteed OHKO on Talonflame). Metagross-Mega Ice Punch goes at Rillaboom (54-98%, best available) to chip the terrain setter/Fake Out user and start the Multiscale-agnostic damage. Splitting targets on foe1/foe2 hedges against a Greninja Protect: if Greninja Protects, Talonflame is safe and Metagross still chips Rillaboom; if Greninja attacks, Brave Bird should remove it. Rillaboom cannot punish either of my actives (Grass is 0.5x into Metagross, 0.25x into Talonflame), so this turn is low-risk for me outside the Brave Bird roll.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Greninja 8% dies to any hit and LO recoil (15 HP) faints it after an attack, so suicide Hydro is a speed coin flip vs Talon 160-195. Switch Greninja→DN: last turn they BB'd Greninja (finish) and Ice Punched Rilla, so DN takes BB 21-33% Multiscale and Rilla takes Ice Punch 55-79% (Sitrus). Do not send Clef into live Mash (87-123%). Rilla has no useful damage (WH Gross 15-26% at -1); consecutive Protect is 1/3 but strictly better than a dead attack and hedges a Rilla double. DN Megas next turn for Fire Blast Gross. Do not switch Rilla into the Ice Punch slot.

Talonflame must be the Greninja-killer: it outspeeds (195 > 191) and KOs the 8% Greninja with Brave Bird BEFORE Greninja can Hydro Pump it. If instead Metagross targeted Greninja, Greninja (faster than Metagross's 132) would move first and could KO Talonflame. So Talonflame Brave Bird -> Greninja, and Metagross-Mega Ice Punch -> Rillaboom (2x, 54-98%) to chip the terrain setter; with Rillaboom's Protect at reduced success, the Ice Punch likely connects. Recoil from Brave Bird is negligible since damage is capped at Greninja's ~8% HP. Rillaboom cannot punish either active (0.5x/0.25x Grass), and Primarina stays benched until the Grass attacker is gone.

Rilla Protect is 100% (last failed, counter reset) and required: BB OHKOs 63% Rilla, Ice Punch 55-79% can KO. Mega DN Ice Punch is 119-167% from 68% even after Mega—cannot take it. Mash can also KO 68%. Fire Blast Mega is only 60-106% 85% and Mega DN 152 vs Gross 130-162 is a speed flip, so clicking Blast risks losing DN for chip. Both Protect keeps DN for a real Blast. They Ice Punched Rilla three times but the 4x on DN is the obvious retarget. Mega now for bulk/SpA. T5: Clef Follow Me if they keep Ice Punch (not Mash) + Fire Blast, or DN Protect. Do not send Clef into Mash this turn.

Double KO: Metagross-Mega Ice Punch (4x, Tough Claws, 111-198%) removes Dragonite from 67% at both endpoints, and Talonflame Brave Bird (2x, 73-134%) removes Rillaboom from 63% at both endpoints - both are guaranteed KOs. Talonflame (195) outspeeds Dragonite's Fire Blast/Hurricane and its Brave Bird resolves before them (only Dragonite's +2 ExtremeSpeed goes first, and ESpeed is 30-43%, not lethal), so Talonflame's KO on Rillaboom lands. Aiming at two different foes hedges against Protect: if Dragonite Protects, Talonflame still deletes Rillaboom, and if Rillaboom Protects, Metagross still deletes Dragonite. Losing Dragonite + Rillaboom in one turn leaves them with only a 8% Greninja plus one hidden mon vs my Metagross + Primarina + Talonflame.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: They Ice Punched Mega DN last turn (4x KO 119-167% from 68%) and BB'd Rilla. Switch DN→Clef: Ice Punch Clef is only 24-34%. Do not Fire Blast—Gross 130-162 vs 152 is a speed flip and Blast is 60-106% 85%, so we can lose DN for chip. Do not send Clef into predicted Mash if we can help it, but Ice Punch is the repeat. Rilla Protect is 1/3 vs BB (68-106%, KO from 69% on most rolls); attacking doesn't KO and 8% Greninja dies to BB. If Protect fails we lose Rilla but keep Clef+DN. Never Follow Me this turn (switch is the action).

Send Mega DN; 8% Greninja dies to any hit. Next: Clef Follow Me vs Ice Punch (24-34% into Clef, they just Ice Punched the DN slot) + Fire Blast Gross. Never Follow Me if they Mash (87-123% KO Clef). Talon is 29% after BB recoil.

Re-apply the double KO now that both foes' Protect is at reduced success. Metagross-Mega Ice Punch (4x, 111-198%) KOs Dragonite-Mega from 67% at both endpoints; Talonflame Brave Bird (2x, 73-134%) KOs Rillaboom from 69% at both endpoints. Talonflame (195) outspeeds Dragonite-Mega's max 152, so Brave Bird lands on Rillaboom before Dragonite's Hurricane can retaliate; Dragonite's only faster move is +2 ExtremeSpeed which does 30-43% (not lethal). Splitting targets again hedges Protect. Even at worst (Talonflame eating a Hurricane after KOing Rillaboom), I trade 1 for 2 and end with Metagross + Primarina vs an 8% Greninja and one hidden mon.

Follow Me + Fire Blast Gross. They Ice Punched the DN slot last turn and 4 times this game, never Mashed. Ice Punch OHKOs 68% DN (119-167%); Follow Me puts it on Clef at 24-34% from 76% (lives). Mash would KO Clef from 76% (87-123%)—the playbook risk—but Ice Punch is the repeat. Fire Blast 60-106% 85% often needs DN alive for a second shot, so HH is worse (DN dies to Ice Punch). ES Talon 17-33% may not KO 29%. U-turn into Follow Me is 5-7% on Clef. If they BB+Ice Punch both redirect, Clef is in KO range on high rolls; still the line that keeps DN.

Dragonite-Mega is the priority target: Metagross-Mega Ice Punch (4x, 111-198%) KOs it from 67% at both endpoints. Talonflame Brave Bird goes at Clefable (1x STAB + Sharp Beak, Talonflame 195 outspeeds Clefable) to chip the last support mon and hedge: if Dragonite Protects (its counter was reset when it switched out and back in), Talonflame still damages Clefable; if Dragonite attacks, Metagross removes it. Talonflame's job on Rillaboom is done and at 29% it may eat an ExtremeSpeed/Hurricane anyway, so spending it on damage is fine. Losing Dragonite leaves them with only Clefable plus an 8% Greninja vs my Metagross + Primarina (+ Talonflame/Primarina), and Metagross's Meteor Mash (2x) KOs Clefable while anything removes Greninja.

T6 order: DN Fire Blast then Gross Ice Punch, so Mega DN 152 outspeeds this Gross. Talon 160+ still outspeeds DN, so Follow Me fails if 4% Clef dies to BB before Ice Punch. ES +2 KOs Talon from 11% (ES 17-33% of max) before BB; Follow Me then absorbs Ice Punch and Clef faints. DN lives at 68% vs Gross 25% + 4th; next turn we outspeed Fire Blast to KO Gross. Do not Fire Blast this turn—Talon would KO Clef, Follow Me drops, Ice Punch KOs DN. HH Blast also loses DN.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Clefable's Follow Me is the obstacle. Aiming Metagross-Mega Ice Punch directly at Clefable (4% HP) KOs it - Follow Me cannot redirect a move already targeting it - eliminating the redirect so Dragonite becomes killable. Dragonite-Mega (up to 152) likely outspeeds Metagross (132, it outsped Metagross in game 1), and its Fire Blast KOs my 25% Metagross, so Metagross probably trades down; that's fine. Talonflame Brave Bird goes at Dragonite (1x chip): if Clefable Protects, my Ice Punch is blocked but Brave Bird still damages Dragonite, whereas aiming Talonflame at Clefable would be wasted if Clefable Protects. After this I have Primarina, which 4x Ice Beams Dragonite (Multiscale already broken) and hard-walls Greninja's entire kit, so I win the endgame regardless.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Fire Blast KO 25% Gross (we outspeed; 60-106% vs 25%) + Greninja Protect. Greninja attacking dies to LO (15 HP > 8%). DN cannot 1v1 Prim (Ice Beam 90-131% from 68%; Hurricane only 43-75%). Win path: Prim Protects on entry like G1 T1, or targets 8% Greninja into Protect, then T9 Hydro+Hurricane Prim (63-110%). If they Ice Beam/Moonblast DN we lose—both KO 68% DN—but Protecting DN and Dark Pulsing Gross still loses the 1v1 next turn. Play for the Protect/wrong-target that keeps both alive.

Primarina Ice Beam (4x, 76.8-132.5%) KOs Dragonite-Mega from 67% at both endpoints, and Primarina comfortably survives Dragonite's best moves (Hurricane 44-62%, Fire Blast 14-20%) plus Greninja's whole kit (all 0.5x). Metagross-Mega Ice Punch (19-37%) KOs the 8% Greninja. Splitting targets hedges Protect: if Dragonite Protects, Metagross still deletes Greninja and Primarina finishes Dragonite next turn; if Greninja Protects, Primarina still deletes Dragonite and Primarina's Moonblast (95-185%) finishes Greninja next turn. Even if Greninja's faster Dark Pulse (which KOs my 25% Metagross) removes Metagross first, Primarina alone beats both remaining foes, so the game is won in every branch.
G2 lost: 8% Greninja vs full Prim, all moves 0.5x, LO recoil faints after any hit. Hydro Prim for the chip then we faint. Pass fainted DN. Do not forfeit menu if Hydro still executes. G3 plan after.

Final KO: Primarina Moonblast is 2x on Greninja (95-185%) and KOs the 8% Greninja at both endpoints, while every Greninja move (Hydro Pump/Dark Pulse/Ice Beam) is only 0.5x into Primarina and cannot KO it. Even if Greninja Protects again (now at reduced success), Primarina survives, re-applies Moonblast next turn, and wins the game and the series 2-0.

reflections.summary: G2 loss, series 0-2. Same opp 4 both games (Mega Gross, Prim, Talon, Arcanine; no Mamo/Rotom). G2 they led Gross+Arcanine. T1 Fake Out Gross + LO Hydro KO Arcanine was the Greninja-for-Dirge adjustment working. T2 Talon entered at 100% Gale Wings with Fake Out already spent; we Protected Rilla (G1 they BB'd Rilla) but they BB'd the Hydro slot to 2% and Hydro missed. That miss decided the game: Greninja became a LO-dead 8% slot and Gale Wings was unanswered. Consecutive Protect failed T3 and T5; Rilla died to BB before Prim appeared, so the WH-Prim wincon never fired. From there the play was correct—Clef into Ice Punch (they never Mashed G2), Follow Me Ice Punch, Blast Gross 100→25 then KO, ES Talon—but it ended in the same closer as G1: Prim Ice Beam KO Mega DN without Multiscale, 8% Greninja 0.5x into Prim and faints to LO. Series lost because both games Talon+Ice Punch break Multiscale, then Prim Ice Beams DN, and Rilla is never alive to WH Prim. Greninja-for-Dirge helped T1 vs Arcanine and backfired T2 (80% Hydro, they BB the attacker). Dirge G1 was doubled BB+Zen before Torch Song.
reflections.adjustment: Vs Gross/Prim/Talon/Arcanine: do not spend Fake Out on Gross if they can send 100% Talon next; Fake Out Talon on sight or keep Sneasler sash in back to live Gale Wings BB. Do not Protect Rilla vs Talon after G2—they BB the Hydro/attacker slot. Prefer Rilla+Clef+DN with Sneasler or Dirge over a second-lead LO Greninja; Greninja is the Arcanine/Talon KO but is unusable after one BB and cannot break Prim. Keep Rilla healthy for WH Prim (unused both games). Fire Blast Gross only with Ice Punch redirected or Gross already in KO; this Adamant Mega Gross is slower than Mega DN 152 (Blast then Ice Punch). Never 1v1 DN vs Prim Ice Beam/Moonblast without Multiscale. Sneasler Dire Claw Prim after sash Fake Out is the cleaner Prim answer than 8% Greninja. Do not chain Protect (failed twice G2). If Greninja is in vs Talon with Fake Out gone, switch it out the turn Talon enters rather than 80% Hydro.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0. Game 2 was a disciplined win despite a bad opening: their Rillaboom+Greninja lead Fake Out'd Metagross and Hydro Pump OHKO'd Arcanine (an unavoidable 2x OHKO), so turn 1 dealt zero damage and cost Arcanine. From there the plan held. Talonflame (fastest) removed Rillaboom with a guaranteed Brave Bird, and Metagross-Mega's 4x Ice Punch removed Dragonite and then Clefable. Their Protect-heavy stalls (a turn-4 double Protect, repeated Protects) delayed but never stopped the KOs - I simply re-clicked the same moves and their Protect counters wore down (~1/3 after each success, reset by switching). Clefable's Follow Me was self-defeating: the redirected Ice Punch still KO'd the 4% Clefable, which reopened Dragonite. Primarina, deliberately held back until the Grass attacker was gone, closed the game: her 4x Ice Beam KO'd Mega Dragonite from 67% and she hard-walls Greninja (every Greninja move is 0.5x), so she easily outlasted it (Greninja ultimately died to its own Life Orb recoil). The key reason for the series result was the between-game adjustment: keeping the proven four (Metagross/Primarina/Talonflame/Arcanine) matched their composition - Primarina neutralized their two biggest threats (Dragonite as the only Dragonite answer, Greninja as a full wall), while Metagross's Ice Punch/Meteor Mash and Talonflame's Brave Bird traded efficiently. It helped, with one clear blemish (the lead choice, see adjustment).
reflections.adjustment: Biggest fix: do not lead Arcanine into a Rillaboom+Greninja lead. Arcanine is OHKO'd by Protean Hydro Pump and Metagross is the Fake Out magnet, so turn 1 yields zero damage for a lost Arcanine (an even trade or worse). Lead Metagross + Talonflame against that lead instead: Talonflame outspeeds Greninja and forces an immediate KO/Protect/switch, while Metagross punishes Rillaboom; keep Arcanine in back for a mid-game Intimidate and an ExtremeSpeed Multiscale-breaker. Second, expect Clefable's Follow Me to shield Dragonite - either KO Clefable directly first (a move aimed at the Follow Me user is not redirected; Metagross Ice Punch/Meteor Mash both kill it) or use a spread move, rather than firing 4x Ice Punch into the redirect. Third, keep Primarina benched until Grass is cleared and enter her only at end of turn; she is the single best answer to their Dragonite and a full Greninja wall, and she needs only one turn. Everything else about the four-mon core matches this opponent well - the team and the overall KO trades do not need changing.

decisions.rationale: Lead Gengar + Kangaskhan for Fake Out + Mega Gengar Shadow Tag pressure (Sludge Bomb Whimsicott, Shadow Ball Annihilape; Scrappy Fake Out hits Annihilape too). Back Salamence (Tailwind/Intimidate/Heat Wave for Excadrill/Whimsicott/Weavile) and Rotom-Wash as the Mega Excadrill answer (Levitate, Hydro Pump, Will-O-Wisp). Left Kingambit (Ground/Fighting weak vs Excadrill/Annihilape) and Altaria.

Lead Whimsicott + Weavile to secure speed control against Kangaskhan with the verified faster Fake Out, while threatening Salamence with Triple Axel. Keep Annihilape as the anti-Kangaskhan/Kingambit and potential Beat Up win condition, and Excadrill as the primary Mega Gengar/Altaria attacker. This avoids exposing Annihilape immediately to fast Gengar while retaining two strong damage plans; Rotom is handled through charged Annihilape rather than diluting the four with another support or slower specialist.

Mega Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds both foes; Focus Blast is a guaranteed OHKO on Weavile if it hits (70%), removing the only thing that threatens Gengar (Knock Off 76-111%). Kangaskhan Fake Out Whimsicott: +3 priority beats Prankster Tailwind, flinches it and breaks Sash if Weavile doesn't Fake Out Kangaskhan first. Sludge Bomb on Whimsicott would only leave it at 1 HP through Sash if Kanga is flinched, while letting Weavile set up a Tailwind Knock Off next turn.

Fake Out Kangaskhan before its own Fake Out, ensuring priority Tailwind succeeds. Gengar cannot stop both the speed setup and our follow-up attackers alone; this also scouts which opposing Mega they commit.

Under their Tailwind Weavile outspeeds Mega Gengar and Knock Off does 76-111%, so Gengar Protects. Kangaskhan Drain Punch (4x, 81-163%) threatens to KO Weavile and heals. If Weavile Protects, next turn Gengar pivots to Rotom-Wash (Knock Off 31-70%) while Kanga repeats Drain Punch; Shadow Tag keeps both foes trapped meanwhile.

Concentrate Knock Off and four-participant super-effective Beat Up into Mega Gengar while Tailwind guarantees Whimsicott acts before it. Knock Off alone is not a reliable KO across hidden bulk, and Moonblast is resisted. If Gengar Protects and Kangaskhan removes Weavile, Annihilape gains entry for the remaining Tailwind turns and Beat Up; otherwise removing Gengar unlocks our positioning.
Bring Annihilape to threaten Beat Up into boosted Rage Fist during Tailwind, with Gengar's consecutive Protect unreliable. Preserve Excadrill for cleanup.

Under Tailwind (2 turns) Annihilape outspeeds Mega Gengar and Rage Fist does 61-92% with Beat Up finishing; Gengar's Protect is on cooldown, so pivot Gengar to Rotom-Wash (Rage Fist 17-39%, Drain Punch 26-58%, Sitrus). Kangaskhan Protects to avoid Annihilape Drain Punch (69-102%) and burn a Tailwind turn. Plan: turn 4 Rotom attacks/Wisps, Kanga pivots to Gengar (immune to Drain Punch aimed at that slot); turn 5 Tailwind ends and Gengar at 200 Spe outspeeds all and cleans with Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb.

Beat Up charges Annihilape before its Rage Fist, and Tailwind guarantees both act before Gengar. Remove the opposing Mega and trapping threat now; even a defensive switch or repeated Protect leaves persistent Rage Fist charge for the endgame.

Annihilape's Rage Fist is now 200 BP (3 Beat Up hits) and it outspeeds everything this last Tailwind turn; Rotom at 27% is its obvious target, so Rotom Protects to waste that turn. Kangaskhan (immune to Rage Fist) Double-Edges Annihilape for 35-64%, putting it in range for Kanga (156 > 110-142 once Tailwind ends) to finish next turn, with Gengar kept safely in back to clean once Annihilape is gone. Never bring Gengar in while Annihilape lives - 200 BP Rage Fist OHKOs it.

Moonblast threatens to finish 27% Rotom without spending Annihilape's attack. Bulk Up exploits likely Protect/switch stalling on the last Tailwind turn, avoids throwing Drain Punch into a Gengar switch, and strengthens Annihilape against Scrappy Kangaskhan. Full-health Sash Whimsicott can renew Tailwind next turn.

Annihilape at +1 now OHKOs Kanga with Drain Punch and Rotom with anything; Kanga's Double-Edge into +1 Def won't finish 55%. Pivot Kanga to Gengar: a Drain Punch aimed at that slot is immune, Rage Fist should be aimed at Rotom (Kanga is Ghost-immune), so Gengar enters safely. With Tailwind gone Gengar (200) outspeeds everything and Shadow Ball (66%+) KOs Annihilape from 55% next turn unless it Protects; Shadow Tag keeps it trapped. Rotom likely dies first but Hydro Pumps Annihilape if it survives (35-62%, can KO).

Renew Tailwind and use boosted Drain Punch to remove or heavily damage Kangaskhan while restoring Annihilape. Rotom alone cannot KO current Annihilape with the evaluated Hydro Pump range; Lum covers its first burn attempt. This prioritizes recovery and the Normal-type obstacle to charged Rage Fist.

Tailwind is back so +1 Annihilape outspeeds Gengar and its 200 BP Rage Fist OHKOs; Gengar Protects (off cooldown) to burn a Tailwind turn. Rotom is likely KO'd first, but if it survives Hydro Pump on Annihilape (35-62% vs 55%) has real KO odds. Next turn plan: pivot Gengar to Kangaskhan (Ghost-immune) to absorb Rage Fist, and look to kill Annihilape with Gengar Shadow Ball once Tailwind lapses or it is forced out of Protect.

Kangaskhan replaces Rotom: it is immune to Rage Fist and doesn't trigger Defiant (Salamence's Intimidate would give Annihilape +2). Next turn Scrappy Fake Out (+3 priority) can flinch Annihilape before it moves under Tailwind, letting Gengar Shadow Ball KO it from 55%.

Threaten both KOs with Moonblast into weakened Rotom and charged +1 Rage Fist into Gengar. Both attackers outspeed under Tailwind. Opponent can defend with Protect or Kangaskhan pivoting into Rage Fist, but this denies a free offensive turn and avoids risking Annihilape on an unnecessary prediction.

Scrappy Fake Out (+3) hits Annihilape through its Ghost typing before it moves under Tailwind, flinching it so its Rage Fist can't OHKO Gengar; Gengar Shadow Ball (min 66%) then KOs Annihilape from 55%. Only Annihilape Protect stops it, in which case Gengar just eats a weak Beat Up/Moonblast and we re-evaluate with Tailwind down to 1 turn.

Protect Annihilape against returning Scrappy Kangaskhan's Fake Out plus Gengar Shadow Ball. Moonblast chips Kangaskhan into safer Drain Punch range if it targets Annihilape; if Fake Out hits Whimsicott instead, Annihilape remains safe and we still have a Tailwind turn to attack.

Gengar must Protect (Annihilape under Tailwind, 200 BP Rage Fist OHKOs) - Protect is off cooldown. Kanga at 41% dies to Drain Punch/half of Moonblasts, so pivot it to Salamence: it takes the hit aimed at Kanga (Moonblast 60-95% / resisted Drain Punch), Kanga is preserved in the back to reset Scrappy Fake Out (our only way to stop Rage Fist while Gengar attacks), and Salamence can Tailwind/Draco next turn. Double Protect would just hand Annihilape a fresh Protect while ours are reduced. Next turn: Gengar likely pivots to Kanga (Rage Fist immune) while Salamence Tailwinds.

Moonblast again threatens Kangaskhan after dealing 45% last turn, while Rage Fist threatens Gengar. Attack both slots on the final Tailwind turn; Whimsicott remains full-health with Sash to renew speed control if they Protect.

Whimsicott will Prankster Tailwind again, making +2 Annihilape outspeed Gengar with an OHKO Rage Fist while Gengar's Protect is reduced, so Gengar pivots to Kangaskhan (immune to Rage Fist, resets Fake Out). Salamence at 1% uses its last action on Tailwind: under our Tailwind Gengar hits 400 Spe, above their Tailwind Annihilape (max 284), so Gengar can Shadow Ball it before it moves. Plan: T10 Kanga Fake Out Annihilape + Sludge Bomb Whimsicott (no Protect on it) / Salamence Draco if alive; T11 Gengar Shadow Ball KOs Annihilape (Protect reduced) while Kanga finishes Whimsicott.

Reestablish priority Tailwind and threaten Gengar with +2 charged Rage Fist before it can attack. Salamence may match Tailwind, but preserving our speed control keeps Whimsicott ahead of it and enables a follow-up Moonblast at 1%; Gengar cannot reliably repeat Protect.

Fake Out Whimsicott (+3) stops its Moonblast on 1% Salamence, breaks Focus Sash (15-29%) and guarantees Salamence acts (334 Spe > Annihilape). Heat Wave then does 41-82% to Whimsicott (roughly coin-flip KO, otherwise very low with no Sash) and chips Annihilape 14-25% through any Protect read. Annihilape's reply will likely KO Salamence or Kanga, bringing Gengar in for free under our Tailwind (2 turns left) where at 400 Spe it Shadow Balls Annihilape before Rage Fist; if they Protect, Gengar isn't hit either.

Protect Annihilape through Kangaskhan's renewed Fake Out and Salamence's potential Draco Meteor. Moonblast removes Salamence before its normal-priority move if Kangaskhan targets Annihilape again, preventing further Tailwind refreshes.

Both our actives outspeed Annihilape under Tailwind and its Protect is reduced. Draco Meteor (39-70%) + Double-Edge (24-43%) total at least 63% vs its 55%, so if Salamence isn't KO'd first by a faster Whimsicott Moonblast and Draco hits (90%), Annihilape dies before it can Drain Punch. Removing Annihilape lets Gengar (400 Spe under our Tailwind) clean the 5% Whimsicott and the last foe freely; Whimsicott at 5% with no Sash is a non-threat that anything finishes later.

Gengar is the last Pokémon; send it in. Under our Tailwind (1 more turn) it moves at 400, first: Shadow Ball KOs Annihilape (34%) unless it Protects, in which case Gengar isn't attacked and Sludge Bomb/Shadow Ball finishes Whimsicott next.

Pressure both weakened targets: Moonblast removes Salamence before it attacks, while +2 Drain Punch KOs Kangaskhan and restores Annihilape if it stays. Annihilape can survive Kangaskhan's unboosted Double-Edge from its current health, and this forces defensive action rather than allowing more free damage.

Gengar moves first at 400 Spe; Shadow Ball (min 66%) KOs Annihilape from 34% unless it Protects, and if it Protects it can't Rage Fist. This forces their Protect now so next turn (no Tailwinds, Gengar 200 still fastest) Shadow Ball beats a reduced-rate Protect 2/3 of the time. Sludge Bombing the 5% Whimsicott first would leave Gengar exposed to a lethal Rage Fist. Shadow Tag keeps both foes trapped so the 4th Pokémon can't be pivoted in.

Protect low-health Annihilape while priority Taunt denies Gengar future Protect stalls. If Gengar attacks Annihilape, Whimsicott can renew Tailwind next turn; if it removes Whimsicott, Excadrill enters beside Annihilape and both threaten the last opponent.

Gengar outspeeds; Shadow Ball KOs Annihilape from 34% unless its reduced-rate Protect (1/3) succeeds, and a Protecting Annihilape can't Rage Fist. Any other target risks eating a lethal Rage Fist. Whimsicott at 5% is cleaned up afterward.
Priority Tailwind restores Annihilape's verified Speed advantage, then +2 fully charged Rage Fist removes the final Gengar. Taunt prevents Protect.

reflections.summary: Lost G1 in 13 turns, 0-4 vs their Whimsicott/Annihilape (Weavile KO'd, 4th never revealed). Turning points: (1) T1 Focus Blast miss on Weavile (70%) cost a free KO and let Tailwind go up; (2) T3 Whimsicott Beat Up into its own Annihilape made Rage Fist 200 BP - it nearly OHKO'd Rotom and forced Gengar to Protect/pivot every Annihilape turn; (3) T8 I switched Salamence in next to Annihilape despite my own "never Intimidate Annihilape" note - Defiant gave it +2 net +1, then a crit Moonblast burned the Sash; (4) opponent read every Gengar Protect perfectly: Annihilape Protected exactly on the turns Gengar attacked (T7, T10, T12) and attacked on the turns Gengar Protected (T6, T8). (5) The decisive error was T12: I Shadow Balled Annihilape into a predictable Protect instead of Sludge Bombing the 5% Whimsicott. With Whimsicott alive, Prankster Tailwind always resolves first, so Mega Gengar's 200 Speed never actually beats Annihilape; killing Whimsicott T12 would have given a 2/3 (reduced Protect) win on T13. Rotom-Wash contributed nothing (Hydro Pump miss, then KO'd) - it is a poor bring into this Whimsicott/Annihilape core. Kangaskhan was our best piece: Scrappy Fake Out + Ghost immunity + Drain Punch OHKO on Weavile.
reflections.adjustment: Keep: Gengar + Kangaskhan core (Kanga unmega'd to keep Scrappy), Salamence Tailwind for speed parity. Change: drop Rotom-Wash for Kingambit (resists Rage Fist, Iron Head OHKO threat on Weavile/Whimsicott, Sucker Punch ignores their Tailwind, Chople eats one Drain Punch). Prioritise removing Whimsicott before trying to Shadow Ball Annihilape - Prankster Tailwind means Gengar never outspeeds Annihilape while Whimsicott lives. Exploit the opponent's alternating Protect rhythm: after Annihilape Protects, it attacks next turn (Gengar Protects or pivots to Kanga); after Gengar Protects, Annihilape Protects next turn (use that turn to hit Whimsicott or set Tailwind, not to hit Annihilape). Never switch Salamence in while Annihilape is active.

reflections.summary: Won 13 turns, taking a 1–0 series lead with Excadrill untouched and no decision errors. Fast Fake Out secured Tailwind; three-hit Beat Up established Annihilape's damage, while Whimsicott's Moonblast supplied essential progress against Rotom, Kangaskhan and Salamence. Bulk Up and correctly timed Protects kept Ape alive, and Taunt + Protect into renewed Tailwind closed safely against Gengar. The main inefficiency was repeatedly attacking into Gengar Protect or immunity pivots, starting with the T2 double-target that lost Weavile for no damage. The win also benefited from T5 Hydro Pump missing Ape and T8's critical Moonblast breaking Salamence's Sash; T1 Focus Blast missed too, though a hit would have provided earlier Ape entry. Do not treat this as a guaranteed repeatable sweep.
reflections.adjustment: Retain Whimsicott/Weavile lead with Annihilape/Excadrill back as the default. Against the same lead, faster Fake Out + Tailwind remains sound. Reassess T2 rather than automatically doubling Gengar: Protect Weavile + Moonblast Kangaskhan is a consideration if expecting the same Gengar Protect/Drain Punch response. Use earlier Taunt only when it can connect safely; it cannot stop Protect already used that turn. Preserve Whimsicott's renewal opportunities and respect opposing Tailwind: equal Tailwinds leave Ape slower than their attackers. Watch both Fake Out targets on Kangaskhan reentry and continue using Moonblast to pressure immunity pivots. Keep Excadrill available for an Altaria adaptation.

decisions.rationale: Bring Kanga, Kingambit, Gengar, Salamence. Lead Kanga + Kingambit: both handle the expected Whimsicott+Weavile lead (Kingambit resists Moonblast/Knock Off, Iron Head OHKOs Weavile, Sucker Punch ignores Tailwind; Kanga Scrappy Fake Out flinches Annihilape/Whimsicott and is Ghost-immune). Gengar in back to trap late without eating the T2 Knock Off; Salamence for Excadrill/Hydrapple.

Retain the successful flexible four: Whimsicott/Weavile threatens fast Fake Out plus Tailwind without exposing Ape to an immediate Gengar attack, with Annihilape as the charged Rage Fist win condition and Excadrill covering Gengar/possible Mega Altaria adaptation. Improve second-turn targeting rather than change the composition on the basis of one favorable game; no automatic double into Gengar Protect.

Kanga Fake Out Whimsicott (+3 beats Prankster Tailwind; if Weavile Fake Outs Kanga instead, Kingambit still acts). Kingambit Iron Head Weavile: 89-178%, likely OHKO. Covers Weavile Fake Out on either of our slots, Weavile Protect, and stops Tailwind whenever Kanga isn't flinched.

Adapt to the slow double-physical lead: pivot Whimsicott into Annihilape while Weavile's verified faster Fake Out denies Kangaskhan's action. Preserve Whimsicott's Sash and avoid spending Tailwind unnecessarily. Ape resists Dark and can take an Iron Head, which also charges Rage Fist; next turn Weavile can remove Kingambit's Chople ahead of Drain Punch. Mega Kangaskhan would also lose Scrappy against Ape.
Bring Whimsicott back alongside undamaged Ape. It offers Moonblast pressure on Kangaskhan, Beat Up setup, and priority Tailwind if needed, preserving Excadrill as the final attacker.

Annihilape Drain Punch KOs Kanga from 84% at high rolls (69-102%), and Double-Edge recoil would make it certain, so Kanga Protects this turn. Kingambit Iron Head breaks Whimsicott's Sash (to 1 HP); Chople absorbs a Drain Punch if Kingambit is targeted. Next turn Kanga Double-Edge finishes Whimsicott with near-zero recoil while Kingambit pressures Annihilape.

Use the full-health pairing to establish the endgame: three-hit Beat Up charges Rage Fist while Bulk Up improves Ape's damage and physical survival. Ape moves before Kingambit's normal attacks, so the Defense boost mitigates Iron Head; even Scrappy Kangaskhan Double-Edge is not an immediate OHKO. This also gains progress against their frequent Protect/immunity pivots rather than committing unboosted attacks into Chople or a Gengar switch.

+1 Drain Punch KOs Kanga from 84% and Protect is on cooldown, so pivot Kanga to Gengar, which is immune to the expected Drain Punch into that slot (Rage Fist into Kingambit is only 43-64%). Kingambit Iron Head guarantees the Whimsicott KO even if it Prankster-Tailwinds first (Sucker Punch would fail vs Tailwind). Next turn: expect Rage Fist at Gengar under Tailwind - pivot Gengar back to Kanga (Ghost-immune) or Protect; Kingambit Sucker Punch chips Annihilape.

Cash Whimsicott's remaining HP into priority Tailwind before either physical attacker can remove it. Drain Punch pressures Kingambit and consumes Chople or punishes a non-Ghost switch, while avoiding the particularly telegraphed Kangaskhan-to-Gengar immunity pivot. Charged +1 Ape plus Tailwind Mega Excadrill remains our damage plan if Whimsicott falls.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Under their Tailwind both foes move first and each can OHKO Gengar (Rage Fist 115-168%, HHP 150%+) and Kingambit (24%). Pivot Gengar to Kanga: immune to the expected Rage Fist, survives HHP (55-76% max). Kingambit uses its priority Sucker Punch on Excadrill (34-65%, 25-44% if mega) before likely dying, setting up a Kanga Drain Punch/Focus Blast KO. Defensive double-Protect rejected: opponent set up (Bulk Up) the last time we protected.

Bring Salamence: immune to HHP, Sash guarantees Tailwind; Intimidate cost on Annihilape is now marginal (it already OHKOs everything non-Normal) while it weakens Excadrill. Plan T5: Kanga Fake Out Annihilape (Scrappy), Salamence Tailwind; T6 Gengar-Mega under our Tailwind outspeeds both for Focus Blast/Shadow Ball with Salamence Heat Wave/Draco support.

Split our KO threats: Mega High Horsepower into Gengar and +1 Drain Punch into weakened Kingambit. Excadrill is verified faster and threatens a full-health Mega Gengar KO, while Piercing Drill still chips Protect. Drain Punch removes Kingambit if it attacks, including after Sucker Punch, and hits a Kangaskhan switch hard. Avoid gambling Excadrill on setup against Focus Blast.

Scrappy Fake Out flinches Annihilape so only Excadrill can act; Salamence (Sash, HHP-immune) then guarantees Tailwind. Next turn their Tailwind is on its last turn while ours is fresh: Gengar-Mega comes in outspeeding both for Focus Blast on 63% Excadrill / Shadow Ball on Annihilape, with Salamence Heat Wave/Draco.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Attack both slots rather than concede the Tailwind window to Fake Out: charged +2 Rage Fist pressures Salamence to its Sash, and accurate Iron Head KOs 18% Kangaskhan if not flinched/protected. Kangaskhan can stop only one attacker with Fake Out. Iron Head also chips a Gengar switch without immunity; avoid Ground into potential Salamence pivots. Damage tool used only 50 BP for Rage Fist, so its uncharged estimate does not reflect the three observed Beat Up hits.

Gengar-Mega (400 Spe) moves first. Their pattern is to Protect Annihilape whenever Gengar threatens it, so target Excadrill with Focus Blast (KO from 63% on hit) - if Annihilape Protects and Excadrill HHPs, a hit leaves Gengar+Salamence vs a Protect-cooldown Annihilape next turn with our Tailwind. Salamence Draco on Annihilape (39-70%) covers the branch where Annihilape Rage Fists Gengar instead: Salamence then outspeeds and finishes it under Tailwind.

Protect the charged Ape from Mega Gengar Shadow Ball plus Salamence's follow-up, while using our final Tailwind turn to attack Gengar with High Horsepower. Excadrill still outruns Salamence this turn, and Gengar is the key removal needed for Ape to beat the remaining physical-immunity-free endgame. This risks Focus Blast into Excadrill, but leaving Ape exposed to the obvious special double target is worse; do not pretend hidden Mega Gengar Speed or the -1 HHP KO is certain.

Annihilape's Protect is on cooldown (1/3 success) and both of ours outspeed it under Tailwind. Shadow Ball 66-118% + Draco Meteor 39-70% on 88% HP is a KO with either both hitting or a high Shadow Ball roll; Sludge Bomb/Heat Wave are far weaker. No reason to Protect - only Rage Fist into Gengar threatens us and we act first.

Rage Fist Gengar is the only meaningful comeback line: remove the non-missing Ghost threat if Ape survives Shadow Ball and Salamence misses or misplays. More Protect cannot reverse the natural Speed disadvantage or build a win condition, and Drain Punch cannot affect Gengar.

reflections.summary: Won G2 in 7 turns (2-0 down in bodies at one point, but the plan held). Kanga+Kingambit lead was correct: Kingambit Iron Head OHKO'd Weavile T1 through the Fake Out flinch on Kanga, broke Whimsicott's Sash T2 and KO'd it T3, removing Prankster Tailwind and Beat Up fuel by turn 3. Costs: Kingambit fell to a +1 Drain Punch (76% through Chople) then a crit; Kanga fell to Excadrill-Mega HHP + a crit Iron Head - two crits, but both losses bought exactly what we needed (Whimsicott dead, Annihilape flinched, Salamence Tailwind up). The decisive read was their Annihilape Protect rhythm: it Protected the turn Gengar-Mega came in (now 4/4 across the series), so Gengar Focus Blast went at Excadrill-Mega (KO from 63%) and Salamence's Draco was the only wasted move. With their Tailwind expired and ours up, Gengar Shadow Ball + Draco finished Annihilape on its Protect cooldown turn. Pivot discipline (Kanga->Gengar vs Drain Punch, Gengar->Kanga vs Rage Fist) meant Annihilape never landed a hit on Gengar. Minor errors: T4 Salamence Intimidate handed Annihilape a net +1 (acceptable since it already OHKO'd non-Normals, but note it), and Kingambit was left in vs Excadrill+Annihilape at 24% where nothing saved it; Sucker Punch chip (37%) still enabled the Focus Blast KO.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same 4 (Kanga, Kingambit, Gengar, Salamence) and the Kanga+Kingambit lead as default; they beat the Whimsicott+Weavile lead cleanly. Expect the opponent to adapt for G3: possible Excadrill or Annihilape lead to punish Kingambit, or Maushold Follow Me to absorb Iron Head/Fake Out. Prepare lead contingencies: vs Excadrill lead, Kingambit Sucker Punch + Kanga Drain Punch (35-67%) or pivot Kingambit to Salamence (HHP-immune); vs Maushold, Kanga Fake Out Maushold and Kingambit hits the real threat. Continue exploiting the Annihilape Protect pattern: whenever Gengar can hit Annihilape, hit the OTHER foe with Gengar and let the partner threaten Annihilape; then attack Annihilape on its cooldown turn.

reflections.summary: Lost in 7 turns; series tied 1–1. No execution errors. The opponent adapted to Kangaskhan/Kingambit with Gengar/Salamence behind and won the speed-control endgame. Our T1 Fake Out safely positioned Ape but cost Weavile; T2 Beat Up + Bulk Up then let Kingambit exhaust Whimsicott's Sash, forcing a final Tailwind before it died. We removed Kingambit and Kangaskhan, but our charged Ape never executed Rage Fist. T5 Scrappy Fake Out into Ape enabled Salamence's uncontested Tailwind, leaving both opposing special attackers healthy. T6 Protect Ape + High Horsepower incorrectly favored a Shadow Ball prediction: Gengar instead KOed Excadrill with Focus Blast while Salamence attacked Ape's Protect. The main problem preceded that guess: we spent both supports for setup without preserving speed control or pressuring Salamence. Our two critical KOs were not essential at the targets' low HP; unlike G1, the opponent's important inaccurate attacks connected.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Whimsicott/Weavile with Ape/Excadrill as the flexible default, but change the Kingambit branch rather than repeat the support-sacrifice script. Preserve Whimsicott for Salamence Taunt, Moonblast and renewed Tailwind. After the same T1 outcome, consider switching Whimsicott to Excadrill while Ape Drain Punches Kingambit, consuming Chople and applying immediate pressure instead of Beat Up + Bulk Up. This is a candidate line, not a guaranteed read: reassess Kangaskhan's attack and Gengar-switch options. Beat Up is optional when the physical foes already feed Rage Fist. Do not assume Fake Out targets or Gengar's target remain fixed. With matching Tailwinds, treat Mega Gengar as demonstrated capable of moving before Mega Excadrill; avoid arriving at the same full-health Gengar/Salamence endgame with Whimsicott gone.

decisions.rationale: Repeat the G2-winning bring: Kanga+Kingambit lead (Fake Out Whimsicott / Iron Head Weavile, Kanga Ghost-immune vs Annihilape), Gengar + Salamence in back for Shadow Tag trapping and Tailwind/Intimidate. Contingencies for Excadrill/Maushold/Annihilape leads are already in the game plan.

Retain the flexible Fake Out/Tailwind lead and both complementary attackers. Whimsicott is essential to contest Salamence's delayed Tailwind; Weavile pressures Salamence and enables the opening, Ape punishes Kangaskhan/Kingambit and Intimidate, and Excadrill supplies immediate Gengar/Altaria pressure. The adjustment is resource management and opening targeting, not replacing an essential matchup tool: avoid automatically sacrificing Weavile and then Whimsicott to charge Ape against the physical lead.

Same lead as G2. Kanga Fake Out Whimsicott denies Prankster Tailwind/Taunt unless Weavile Fake Outs Kanga first (then Iron Head still OHKOs Weavile as in G2). Kingambit Iron Head Weavile: OHKO if it stays; if it Protects we lose nothing and it's on cooldown next turn; if it switches, Iron Head hits the pivot neutrally (Annihilape/Maushold). Covers the likely adaptations (Weavile Protect or Fake Out into Kingambit) without exposing anything.

Pivot Whimsicott into Ape but Fake Out Kingambit rather than repeating last game's Kangaskhan target. Weavile acts before even Mega Kangaskhan's Fake Out, so Kingambit's immediate Iron Head is denied regardless of Kangaskhan's Fake Out target. This preserves Whimsicott for late speed control and is particularly productive into the opponent's prior Fake Out/Protect Kangaskhan opening. Kangaskhan can punish Weavile with a direct attack, but targeting it instead allowed Kingambit a demonstrated guaranteed KO; denying King offers a realistic way to retain all four resources.

Annihilape at 82% is the main threat (Drain Punch 44-65% Kingambit / 69-102% Kanga). Kanga (156) and Sucker Punch both move before Annihilape: Double-Edge 35-64% + Sucker Punch 28-52% = 63-116% into 82%, good KO odds before it can act. If it Protects, we only take a resisted/moderate Weavile hit and it is on cooldown next turn; if it survives on low rolls it's in Sucker Punch range next turn. Weavile's Fake Out is spent and its hits on Kanga are ~30-40%.

Double Kingambit with Knock Off then Drain Punch: remove Chople before the Fighting hit rather than spending Whimsicott or a setup turn. Current damage endpoints suggest the combined attack can remove King from 94% even at high bulk (not an exhaustive guarantee), and Ape is guaranteed faster than King's normal-priority attacks. Kangaskhan cannot KO Ape with one unboosted Double-Edge; Drain Punch then restores health. If Kang attacks Weavile, its Knock Off has already enabled Ape, while a Gengar switch into King's slot is punished by Knock Off rather than absorbing both attacks.

Bring Excadrill for immediate Mega-powered offense into the two physical attackers. Ape was lost to Sucker Punch plus Double-Edge before it could heal; keeping Whimsicott in reserve still preserves our route to speed control against the unrevealed backline. We need Drill's damage and resistances now, not an exposed support alongside Weavile.

Excadrill-Mega HHP KOs Kingambit (70-96% vs 77%, Chople gone) and Protect only delays. Switch Kingambit to Salamence: HHP-immune, and Intimidate now has no Defiant target (Annihilape fainted), dropping both Excadrill-Mega and Weavile to -1. Kanga Drain Punch Weavile (4x, 81-163%) for the KO if it stays in; it attacked rather than Protected last turn under the same threat. Risk: Weavile Triple Axel into the Kingambit slot could break Sash, but it has targeted Kanga/resisted Kingambit and Excadrill covers that slot.

Kingambit is the safer replacement: at -1 Excadrill-Mega's HHP no longer KOs it from 77%, Weavile's hits are resisted, and it threatens Iron Head OHKO on Weavile / Sucker Punch on Excadrill. Gengar would just be an HHP/Knock Off target and must be preserved as the mega for the endgame; Salamence can Tailwind next turn.

Mega Evolve and double Kangaskhan with Triple Axel + High Horsepower. Mega Drill is guaranteed faster even if Kang Mega Evolves; concentrated damage aims to deny its attack and future Scrappy Fake Out cycles while preserving Weavile for Salamence. Kingambit's Sucker Punch cannot alone KO full-health Mega Drill, and this avoids sinking both attacks into a plausible Kingambit Protect. Splitting attacks risks leaving both foes alive and losing an attacker to Kangaskhan.

Weavile's obvious play is Triple Axel into Salamence (4x, multi-hit breaks Sash, up to 118%), so Salamence Protects. Kingambit Iron Head OHKOs Weavile (89-178%) after it commits; Weavile has never Protected this series and attacked the last two turns. Kingambit takes -1 HHP (46-64%) and survives from 77%. Keeps Kingambit's Protect and Salamence's Sash/Tailwind for the Whimsicott+Excadrill endgame, with Gengar healthy in the back.

Triple Axel pressures Salamence before its Tailwind and can defeat Sash through multiple hits. Switch Drill to Whimsicott to clear Intimidate, prepare immediate speed control/Taunt, and deny a Sucker Punch into Drill. At -1 Drill cannot KO 77% Kingambit with High Horsepower, so leaving it exposed for chip is less valuable than restoring its Attack and positioning our intact support. If King removes Weavile after it attacks, neutral-Attack Drill returns beside Whimsicott rather than becoming stranded against faster special attackers.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Excadrill re-entered at +0 so HHP likely KOs Kingambit (70-96% vs 77%): Protect it and keep it for Sucker Punch next turn. Salamence Heat Wave chunks both (Excadrill 34-66%, Whimsicott 41-82%/Sash) while Sash protects Salamence from any single hit; Whimsicott's likely Prankster Tailwind doesn't stop this. Next turn Sucker Punch + second Heat Wave (93-176% total on Excadrill) should finish Excadrill and Whimsicott, with Gengar-Mega healthy as the closer.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Concentrate Moonblast + Iron Head into Salamence before it moves, breaking Sash with two attacks and aiming to deny both Tailwind and Heat Wave. Both allies naturally move first, so Tailwind now would spend an action without fixing this immediate threat. Kingambit cannot KO either full-health ally with Sucker Punch alone, and Whimsicott's intact Sash covers Iron Head. Salamence just Protected, making another successful block less reliable; removing it gives our remaining two a fighting route against Kingambit and the last reserve.

2v2 vs Whimsicott+Excadrill-Mega. Their sharpest line is Prankster Tailwind + HHP into Gengar (kills the Focus Blast threat before it moves), so Gengar Mega Evolves and Protects on entry. Kingambit Sucker Punch (priority, resolves before HHP) chips Excadrill 25-44% so that two more Sucker Punches / one Focus Blast finish it. Attacking with Focus Blast now loses outright to the Tailwind+HHP-Gengar line.

Set priority Tailwind and High Horsepower Gengar. Removing Salamence preserved both full-health allies and now lets Drill outrun Mega Gengar after Tailwind. High Horsepower has lethal damage at both evaluated endpoints; targeting Kingambit instead would expose Drill to an unopposed Focus Blast. Gengar Protect is acceptable: Piercing Drill chips through it while Tailwind establishes the lasting speed advantage, and a lone Kingambit attack cannot remove full-health Drill.

Piercing Drill pierces Protect and Excadrill outspeeds Gengar under Tailwind, so there's no safe turn: go for damage. Sucker Punch (priority) puts Excadrill at 16-35%; if HHP goes into Kingambit, Gengar's Focus Blast (70%) finishes it and Gengar beats Whimsicott alone. If HHP kills Gengar, Kingambit's next Sucker Punch (25-44%) likely KOs Excadrill from 16-35% before it moves, then Iron Head handles Whimsicott. Roughly 65-75% win equity, better than any Protect line.

Moonblast Kingambit while High Horsepower finishes Gengar or heavily chips another Protect. Drill survives one more Sucker Punch at the full evaluated range, and Whimsicott must start softening King now so Drill can use Protect against the following lethal Sucker Punch while Moonblast keeps progressing. High Horsepower retains substantially better through-Protect damage than Iron Head; Gengar's prior 46% protected loss means another protected hit would leave it close to Whimsicott's finishing range.

Excadrill at 3% outspeeds under Tailwind and HHP KOs Kingambit from 41%; Sucker Punch is the only move that lands first and KOs if Excadrill attacks (it has never Protected all series). Protect is pierced by Piercing Drill and Kowtow/Iron Head are too slow.

Protect the 3%-HP Drill from Sucker Punch while Moonblast brings Kingambit into finishing range. Whimsicott is still full with Sash, so King cannot remove it with one attack. This keeps both finishers available: next turn, once King is chipped, simultaneous Moonblast and accurate Iron Head can punish either Sucker Punch target without requiring High Horsepower to connect.

At 3% any hit KOs Kingambit and Whimsicott moves first; Sucker Punch (+1) at least KOs Excadrill before Moonblast lands if Excadrill attacks. Protect is pierced by Piercing Drill. Only remaining line.

Finish with two accurate attacks. Sucker Punch into Drill leaves full-health Whimsicott free to KO; targeting Whimsicott cannot remove it from full and leaves both attacks available. If Kingambit Protects, Piercing Drill's quarter-damage Iron Head is sufficient against its remaining 3%, avoiding High Horsepower's miss chance.

reflections.summary: G3 lost 0-2 on the board after an even 2-for-2 trade; series lost 1-2. The opening went to plan: Kanga Fake Out + Double-Edge and Kingambit Sucker Punch KO'd Annihilape by turn 2, and Iron Head KO'd Weavile on turn 4. The game was lost in the middle: (1) Turn 3 I pivoted Kingambit to Salamence for Intimidate while leaving Kanga at 85% to attack; Weavile (Triple Axel) and Excadrill-Mega both outsped and double-targeted Kanga, so it died without moving - Kanga Protect + the switch would have kept it. (2) Turn 4-5 the opponent reset Intimidate by switching Excadrill out, then double-targeted Salamence (Moonblast broke Sash, Iron Head finished) before it moved; Salamence never set Tailwind or fired Heat Wave, so its Sash bring gave zero value. (3) The endgame Kingambit + Gengar-Mega vs Whimsicott + Excadrill-Mega is structurally lost: Prankster Tailwind puts Excadrill above Gengar, HHP OHKOs Gengar and Piercing Drill goes through Protect, Sucker Punch alone cannot outrace Moonblast chip once Excadrill Protects the obvious priority hit. Root cause was the bring: I repeated the exact G2 bring and lead (Kanga/Kingambit lead, Gengar/Salamence back) against an opponent who brought the same four all series and adapted precisely - Fake Out into Kingambit, Knock Off to remove Chople, Intimidate reset, saving Tailwind for Gengar-Mega's entry. My G1->G2 adjustment (Kingambit for Rotom-W, Kanga+Kingambit lead) won G2 but was read and punished in G3; I had no Ground-immune answer to Excadrill-Mega once Salamence was chunked, and Gengar (the mega) never fired an attack all game. Piloting was clean turn-to-turn (0 errors), but the plan lacked a mid-game contingency for Excadrill once Kingambit's Chople was gone.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent: vary the bring after a win rather than repeating it. Bring Rotom-Wash (Levitate, Will-O-Wisp/Hydro Pump) or Mega Altaria as the dedicated Excadrill-Mega answer instead of relying on Salamence's Sash, which is broken by Triple Axel/Beat Up/Moonblast every game. Keep Kanga + Kingambit as the lead only if Kingambit Protects turn 1 (they now Fake Out Kingambit and Knock Off Chople). Never leave a slot exposed to a double-target when the partner switches; pair every defensive pivot with Protect on the other slot. Set our own Tailwind before Gengar enters, or don't bring Gengar into an Excadrill-Mega endgame at all; accept Gengar as a bench threat and mega Kangaskhan or Altaria instead. Expect Excadrill to Protect the turn it is in obvious Sucker Punch range and hit the partner that turn.

reflections.summary:
Won G3 in nine turns and the series 2–1. The decisive adjustment was preserving Whimsicott for offense and late Tailwind instead of spending it on Ape setup. G3's changed T1 Fake Out target (Kingambit) retained Weavile. However, my T2 Knock Off + Drain Punch line overlooked combined Sucker Punch and Scrappy Double-Edge: Ape died before attacking. That was a tactical error despite zero submission errors. T4 also cost Weavile into Salamence Protect + Kingambit Iron Head, although switching Drill reset Intimidate and positioned Whimsicott.
We recovered through concentrated damage: Triple Axel + High Horsepower removed Kangaskhan T3; Moonblast + Iron Head removed Salamence T5 before it could establish Tailwind, while King protected. Preserved Whimsicott then set Tailwind, and Piercing Drill's High Horsepower took 46% through Gengar's Protect before finishing it. Moonblast steadily removed Kingambit while Drill's Protect denied Sucker Punch; Whimsicott finished at full HP despite an opposing critical Sucker Punch leaving Drill at 6 HP earlier.
Across the series, G1's Whimsicott preservation and charged Ape won with help from favorable misses; G2's support expenditure and uncontested late Salamence Tailwind lost to untouched special attackers. G3 corrected that resource/speed-control failure without changing our four. The adjustment helped overall, but the early Ape loss was avoidable, not evidence that sacrificing it was sound.
reflections.adjustment:
Retain the flexible four and the principle of preserving Whimsicott; no evidence requires a roster overhaul. Against Kangaskhan/Kingambit, Fake Out King + the Ape pivot worked on T1, but do not automatically follow with Knock Off + Drain Punch. Evaluate both opposing attacks in priority order: Sucker Punch plus faster Scrappy Double-Edge can KO Ape before recovery. Consider Protect Ape + Knock Off King to remove Chople while denying that double-target, then reassess rather than scripting a guaranteed KO. Account for King Protect and attacks into Weavile as alternatives.
Against Salamence beside King, explicitly price Protect + Iron Head before committing exposed Weavile's Triple Axel; do not treat its offensive matchup as a free KO. Preserve a route to neutral-Attack Drill plus Whimsicott, and use combined Moonblast/Iron Head pressure to deny Tailwind when both naturally move first. Treat Whimsicott as a damage dealer and Sucker Punch endgame partner, not merely a disposable setter. Audit calculator assumptions: single-hit survival is not joint-action survival, and multi-hit/charged-move ranges need inspection.
